duplicate screening is pending for this WORK-ITEM CLAIM. It does not block opening an agent or fleet process; launch and queue admission are separate capabilities. A launched agent still needs claimable or validly pre-assigned work. This row carries a typed DUPLICATE VERDICT: it was adjudicated the same problem as its canonical row (EI-24817242796602056). No admission path admits a row with a duplicate verdict, the independent fail-open runner included, so this does NOT clear on its own and there is no bound to wait out. Work the canonical row instead.
floors.remedy: Choose the work route before creating a replacement. Existing-plan fleet work should use plans:start then fleet:launch-on-plan; its promoted items use the plan-item bypass. Fixed ad-hoc work should be created atomically with assign_to naming the intended owner, then launched with capability:launch-agent. Any one of these makes a NEW item born admitted: the item implements a plan item; severity:'critical'; a 'security' topic; assign_to names the intended owner. These are create-time admission bypasses, not blanket authority: assign_to is still checked against the target's live fleet scope, dependencies, locks, security, credentials and resource admission; a scope mismatch files the item unassigned and explains why. Launching does not change an ALREADY-pending item. Wait for its promoter/backstop instead of duplicating or re-filing it; only the existing server-derived dispatch/force paths may grant their narrower exceptions.

duplicate screening is pending for this WORK-ITEM CLAIM. It does not block opening an agent or fleet process; launch and queue admission are separate capabilities. A launched agent still needs claimable or validly pre-assigned work. This row carries a typed DUPLICATE VERDICT: it was adjudicated the same problem as its canonical row (EI-25492242650368024). No admission path admits a row with a duplicate verdict, the independent fail-open runner included, so this does NOT clear on its own and there is no bound to wait out. Work the canonical row instead.
floors.remedy: Choose the work route before creating a replacement. Existing-plan fleet work should use plans:start then fleet:launch-on-plan; its promoted items use the plan-item bypass. Fixed ad-hoc work should be created atomically with assign_to naming the intended owner, then launched with capability:launch-agent. Any one of these makes a NEW item born admitted: the item implements a plan item; severity:'critical'; a 'security' topic; assign_to names the intended owner. These are create-time admission bypasses, not blanket authority: assign_to is still checked against the target's live fleet scope, dependencies, locks, security, credentials and resource admission; a scope mismatch files the item unassigned and explains why. Launching does not change an ALREADY-pending item. Wait for its promoter/backstop instead of duplicating or re-filing it; only the existing server-derived dispatch/force paths may grant their narrower exceptions.

duplicate screening is pending for this WORK-ITEM CLAIM. It does not block opening an agent or fleet process; launch and queue admission are separate capabilities. A launched agent still needs claimable or validly pre-assigned work. This row carries a typed DUPLICATE VERDICT: it was adjudicated the same problem as its canonical row (EI-21306926912849713). No admission path admits a row with a duplicate verdict, the independent fail-open runner included, so this does NOT clear on its own and there is no bound to wait out. Work the canonical row instead.
floors.remedy: Choose the work route before creating a replacement. Existing-plan fleet work should use plans:start then fleet:launch-on-plan; its promoted items use the plan-item bypass. Fixed ad-hoc work should be created atomically with assign_to naming the intended owner, then launched with capability:launch-agent. Any one of these makes a NEW item born admitted: the item implements a plan item; severity:'critical'; a 'security' topic; assign_to names the intended owner. These are create-time admission bypasses, not blanket authority: assign_to is still checked against the target's live fleet scope, dependencies, locks, security, credentials and resource admission; a scope mismatch files the item unassigned and explains why. Launching does not change an ALREADY-pending item. Wait for its promoter/backstop instead of duplicating or re-filing it; only the existing server-derived dispatch/force paths may grant their narrower exceptions.

duplicate screening is pending for this WORK-ITEM CLAIM. It does not block opening an agent or fleet process; launch and queue admission are separate capabilities. A launched agent still needs claimable or validly pre-assigned work. This row carries a typed DUPLICATE VERDICT: it was adjudicated the same problem as its canonical row (EI-25433250907934100). No admission path admits a row with a duplicate verdict, the independent fail-open runner included, so this does NOT clear on its own and there is no bound to wait out. Work the canonical row instead.
floors.remedy: Choose the work route before creating a replacement. Existing-plan fleet work should use plans:start then fleet:launch-on-plan; its promoted items use the plan-item bypass. Fixed ad-hoc work should be created atomically with assign_to naming the intended owner, then launched with capability:launch-agent. Any one of these makes a NEW item born admitted: the item implements a plan item; severity:'critical'; a 'security' topic; assign_to names the intended owner. These are create-time admission bypasses, not blanket authority: assign_to is still checked against the target's live fleet scope, dependencies, locks, security, credentials and resource admission; a scope mismatch files the item unassigned and explains why. Launching does not change an ALREADY-pending item. Wait for its promoter/backstop instead of duplicating or re-filing it; only the existing server-derived dispatch/force paths may grant their narrower exceptions.

A launched agent still needs claimable or validly pre-assigned work. This row carries a typed DUPLICATE VERDICT: it was adjudicated the same problem as its canonical row (EI-25777086852625166). No admission path admits a row with a duplicate verdict, the independent fail-open runner included, so this does NOT clear on its own and there is no bound to wait out. floors.remedy: Choose the work route before creating a replacement. Existing-plan fleet work should use plans:start then fleet:launch-on-plan; its promoted items use the plan-item bypass. Fixed ad-hoc work should be created atomically with assign_to naming the intended owner, then launched with capability:launch-agent. Any one of these makes a NEW item born admitted: the item implements a plan item; severity:'critical'; a 'security' topic; assign_to names the intended owner. These are create-time admission bypasses, not blanket authority: assign_to is still checked against the target's live fleet scope, dependencies, locks, security, credentials and resource admission; a scope mismatch files the item unassigned and explains why. Launching does not change an ALREADY-pending item. Wait for its promoter/backstop instead of duplicating or re-filing it; only the existing server-derived dispatch/force paths may grant their narrower exceptions.

This row carries DUPLICATE CANDIDATES found when it was filed, at least one stronger than a soft semantic match, so only the promoter's model review can admit it (as distinct) or merge it into its twin. The promoter runs on a 30-minute tick but reviews only a few rows per tick, candidate rows first, so this wait has NO fixed bound; the independent fail-open runner deliberately never admits a row with unresolved strong candidates. floors.remedy: Choose the work route before creating a replacement. Existing-plan fleet work should use plans:start then fleet:launch-on-plan; its promoted items use the plan-item bypass. Fixed ad-hoc work should be created atomically with assign_to naming the intended owner, then launched with capability:launch-agent. Any one of these makes a NEW item born admitted: the item implements a plan item; severity:'critical'; a 'security' topic; assign_to names the intended owner. These are create-time admission bypasses, not blanket authority: assign_to is still checked against the target's live fleet scope, dependencies, locks, security, credentials and resource admission; a scope mismatch files the item unassigned and explains why. Launching does not change an ALREADY-pending item. Wait for its promoter/backstop instead of duplicating or re-filing it; only the existing server-derived dispatch/force paths may grant their narrower exceptions.

This row carries DUPLICATE CANDIDATES found when it was filed, at least one stronger than a soft semantic match, so only the promoter's model review can admit it (as distinct) or merge it into its twin. The promoter runs on a 30-minute tick but reviews only a few rows per tick, candidate rows first, so this wait has NO fixed bound; the independent fail-open runner deliberately never admits a row with unresolved strong candidates. It still CLEARS ON ITS OWN, and it is not a permanent refusal — but do not wait on it: check whether a named candidate is the same problem and work that row instead, or use a create-time admission route for genuinely distinct work.
floors.remedy: Choose the work route before creating a replacement. Existing-plan fleet work should use plans:start then fleet:launch-on-plan; its promoted items use the plan-item bypass. Fixed ad-hoc work should be created atomically with assign_to naming the intended owner, then launched with capability:launch-agent. Any one of these makes a NEW item born admitted: the item implements a plan item; severity:'critical'; a 'security' topic; assign_to names the intended owner. These are create-time admission bypasses, not blanket authority: assign_to is still checked against the target's live fleet scope, dependencies, locks, security, credentials and resource admission; a scope mismatch files the item unassigned and explains why. Launching does not change an ALREADY-pending item. Wait for its promoter/backstop instead of duplicating or re-filing it; only the existing server-derived dispatch/force paths may grant their narrower exceptions.

This row carries DUPLICATE CANDIDATES found when it was filed, at least one stronger than a soft semantic match, so only the promoter's model review can admit it (as distinct) or merge it into its twin. The promoter runs on a 30-minute tick but reviews only a few rows per tick, candidate rows first, so this wait has NO fixed bound; the independent fail-open runner deliberately never admits a row with unresolved strong candidates. It still CLEARS ON ITS OWN, and it is not a permanent refusal — but do not wait on it: check whether a named candidate is the same problem and work that row instead, or use a create-time admission route for genuinely distinct work.
floors.remedy: Choose the work route before creating a replacement. Existing-plan fleet work should use plans:start then fleet:launch-on-plan; its promoted items use the plan-item bypass. Fixed ad-hoc work should be created atomically with assign_to naming the intended owner, then launched with capability:launch-agent. Any one of these makes a NEW item born admitted: the item implements a plan item; severity:'critical'; a 'security' topic; assign_to names the intended owner. These are create-time admission bypasses, not blanket authority: assign_to is still checked against the target's live fleet scope, dependencies, locks, security, credentials and resource admission; a scope mismatch files the item unassigned and explains why. Launching does not change an ALREADY-pending item. Wait for its promoter/backstop instead of duplicating or re-filing it; only the existing server-derived dispatch/force paths may grant their narrower exceptions.

This row carries DUPLICATE CANDIDATES found when it was filed, at least one stronger than a soft semantic match, so only the promoter's model review can admit it (as distinct) or merge it into its twin. The promoter runs on a 30-minute tick but reviews only a few rows per tick, candidate rows first, so this wait has NO fixed bound; the independent fail-open runner deliberately never admits a row with unresolved strong candidates. It still CLEARS ON ITS OWN, and it is not a permanent refusal — but do not wait on it: check whether a named candidate is the same problem and work that row instead, or use a create-time admission route for genuinely distinct work.
floors.remedy: Choose the work route before creating a replacement. Existing-plan fleet work should use plans:start then fleet:launch-on-plan; its promoted items use the plan-item bypass. Fixed ad-hoc work should be created atomically with assign_to naming the intended owner, then launched with capability:launch-agent. Any one of these makes a NEW item born admitted: the item implements a plan item; severity:'critical'; a 'security' topic; assign_to names the intended owner. These are create-time admission bypasses, not blanket authority: assign_to is still checked against the target's live fleet scope, dependencies, locks, security, credentials and resource admission; a scope mismatch files the item unassigned and explains why. Launching does not change an ALREADY-pending item. Wait for its promoter/backstop instead of duplicating or re-filing it; only the existing server-derived dispatch/force paths may grant their narrower exceptions.

duplicate screening is pending for this WORK-ITEM CLAIM. It does not block opening an agent or fleet process; launch and queue admission are separate capabilities. A launched agent still needs claimable or validly pre-assigned work. This row carries DUPLICATE CANDIDATES found when it was filed, at least one stronger than a soft semantic match, so only the promoter's model review can admit it (as distinct) or merge it into its twin. The promoter runs on a 30-minute tick but reviews only a few rows per tick, candidate rows first, so this wait has NO fixed bound; the independent fail-open runner deliberately never admits a row with unresolved strong candidates. It still CLEARS ON ITS OWN, and it is not a permanent refusal — but do not wait on it: check whether a named candidate is the same problem and work that row instead, or use a create-time admission route for genuinely distinct work.
floors.remedy: Choose the work route before creating a replacement. Existing-plan fleet work should use plans:start then fleet:launch-on-plan; its promoted items use the plan-item bypass. Fixed ad-hoc work should be created atomically with assign_to naming the intended owner, then launched with capability:launch-agent. Any one of these makes a NEW item born admitted: the item implements a plan item; severity:'critical'; a 'security' topic; assign_to names the intended owner. These are create-time admission bypasses, not blanket authority: assign_to is still checked against the target's live fleet scope, dependencies, locks, security, credentials and resource admission; a scope mismatch files the item unassigned and explains why. Launching does not change an ALREADY-pending item. Wait for its promoter/backstop instead of duplicating or re-filing it; only the existing server-derived dispatch/force paths may grant their narrower exceptions.

This row carries DUPLICATE CANDIDATES found when it was filed, at least one stronger than a soft semantic match, so only the promoter's model review can admit it (as distinct) or merge it into its twin. The promoter runs on a 30-minute tick but reviews only a few rows per tick, candidate rows first, so this wait has NO fixed bound; the independent fail-open runner deliberately never admits a row with unresolved strong candidates. It still CLEARS ON ITS OWN, and it is not a permanent refusal — but do not wait on it: check whether a named candidate is the same problem and work that row instead, or use a create-time admission route for genuinely distinct work.
floors.remedy: Choose the work route before creating a replacement. Existing-plan fleet work should use plans:start then fleet:launch-on-plan; its promoted items use the plan-item bypass. Fixed ad-hoc work should be created atomically with assign_to naming the intended owner, then launched with capability:launch-agent. Any one of these makes a NEW item born admitted: the item implements a plan item; severity:'critical'; a 'security' topic; assign_to names the intended owner. These are create-time admission bypasses, not blanket authority: assign_to is still checked against the target's live fleet scope, dependencies, locks, security, credentials and resource admission; a scope mismatch files the item unassigned and explains why. Launching does not change an ALREADY-pending item. Wait for its promoter/backstop instead of duplicating or re-filing it; only the existing server-derived dispatch/force paths may grant their narrower exceptions.

floors.remedy: Choose the work route before creating a replacement. Existing-plan fleet work should use plans:start then fleet:launch-on-plan; its promoted items use the plan-item bypass. Fixed ad-hoc work should be created atomically with assign_to naming the intended owner, then launched with capability:launch-agent. Any one of these makes a NEW item born admitted: the item implements a plan item; severity:'critical'; a 'security' topic; assign_to names the intended owner. These are create-time admission bypasses, not blanket authority: assign_to is still checked against the target's live fleet scope, dependencies, locks, security, credentials and resource admission; a scope mismatch files the item unassigned and explains why. Launching does not change an ALREADY-pending item. Wait for its promoter/backstop instead of duplicating or re-filing it; only the existing server-derived dispatch/force paths may grant their narrower exceptions.

The promoter runs on a 30-minute tick but reviews only a few rows per tick, candidate rows first, so this wait has NO fixed bound; the independent fail-open runner deliberately never admits a row with unresolved strong candidates. These are create-time admission bypasses, not blanket authority: assign_to is still checked against the target's live fleet scope, dependencies, locks, security, credentials and resource admission; a scope mismatch files the item unassigned and explains why. Launching does not change an ALREADY-pending item. Wait for its promoter/backstop instead of duplicating or re-filing it; only the existing server-derived dispatch/force paths may grant their narrower exceptions.

duplicate screening is pending for this WORK-ITEM CLAIM. It does not block opening an agent or fleet process; launch and queue admission are separate capabilities. A launched agent still needs claimable or validly pre-assigned work. This row carries a typed DUPLICATE VERDICT: it was adjudicated the same problem as its canonical row (WI-10007742). No admission path admits a row with a duplicate verdict, the independent fail-open runner included, so this does NOT clear on its own and there is no bound to wait out. Work the canonical row instead.
floors.remedy: Choose the work route before creating a replacement. Existing-plan fleet work should use plans:start then fleet:launch-on-plan; its promoted items use the plan-item bypass. Fixed ad-hoc work should be created atomically with assign_to naming the intended owner, then launched with capability:launch-agent. Any one of these makes a NEW item born admitted: the item implements a plan item; severity:'critical'; a 'security' topic; assign_to names the intended owner. These are create-time admission bypasses, not blanket authority: assign_to is still checked against the target's live fleet scope, dependencies, locks, security, credentials and resource admission; a scope mismatch files the item unassigned and explains why. Launching does not change an ALREADY-pending item. Wait for its promoter/backstop instead of duplicating or re-filing it; only the existing server-derived dispatch/force paths may grant their narrower exceptions.

evidence.notes: R-related to EI-10717 (see its note) — the ATTRIBUTION half: apps/operator-vite owns a typecheck ratchet that counts FOREIGN errors from packages it imports but does not own, so an error introduced in operator-core reds a stranger's gate and lands on whoever next touches operator-vite. PARTIALLY SUPERSEDED, deliberately NOT discarded: the specific mechanism this item asked for — operator-core having a typecheck of its own — now EXISTS as `npm run lint:tsc` (scripts/lint-tsc.mjs:167, `tsc -p packages/operator-core/tsconfig.json --noEmit`), so operator-core errors are catchable at their own boundary. What I did NOT verify is whether lint:tsc is ENFORCED anywhere automatic (a green-checkpoint gate step, a CI job) as opposed to being a lever agents are told to run by hand. That distinction decides the whole item: an unenforced typecheck does not stop a foreign error from reaching operator-vite's ratchet, so the attribution defect would survive its own fix. Merit left UNTRIAGED for exactly that reason rather than guessed in either direction.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
While verifying an unrelated fix (EI-18681914950138372, psu-pty-host.mjs carry-respawn starvation), the same 11 tests in `apps/operator/lib/psu-pty-host.integration.test.ts` failed identically with `Error: Test timed out in 20000-30000ms` — every failure a generic timeout on a real pty+child-process round-trip (host start / inject / recycle / discovery self-heal), never a specific assertion mismatch.

VERIFIED NOT CAUSED BY MY CHANGE: ran the exact same test file against BOTH my fixed psu-pty-host.mjs (git-sync commit 569bacf406) AND the immediately-prior commit (85016ff9d1, via a scoped `git checkout <sha> -- <path>` A/B, confirmed via `locks:list` that no peer held the file first) — both runs produced the IDENTICAL 11 failed / 11 passed split, same test names, same timeout signature. This rules out my edit as the cause; it is a pre-existing condition.

Failing tests (all in `hostThroughPty real round-trip`, `RECYCLE — kill + respawn`, `P-020 carry-respawn drill correlation`, `carry-respawn STALENESS guard`, `RECYCLE respawns with FRESH session args`, `RECYCLE carry-inject is retried across a budget` (x2), `WI-3455 — discovery key ownership + self-heal` (x3)):
  - creates socket+meta on start, injects into the live child, cleans up on exit
  - EI-153: REFUSES a control envelope addressed to a DIFFERENT ownerId
  - replaces the child process, keeps the host alive, opens fresh process on carry-note
  - records the fresh native id / carry path / first-prompt delivery
  - a carry-respawn that ages past PAPERCUSP_PSU_PTY_CARRY_STALE_MS is DROPPED
  - feeds the child the mintRecycleArgs-rewritten argv
  - RETRIES past a fresh child that stays busy beyond one busy-cap
  - DROPS LOUDLY when the fresh child never settles
  - self-heals: recreates a deleted json + re-binds a deleted sock
  - exit cleanup leaves a SUCCESSOR's registration alone
  - stands down while a LIVE psu-marked process owns the key

By contrast, the SIBLING integration file `psu-pty-host-turn.integration.test.ts` (10 tests, also real pty+child-process round-trips exercising the SAME host module) passed 10/10 cleanly in the same run — so this isn't "real ptys are universally too slow on this box right now," it's specific to this ONE file's tests (which spawn a full host via `hostThroughPty`/RECYCLE/discovery flows — heavier setup than the turn-injection tests). Worth investigating whether this file's fixture setup (per-test host boot, `readdirSync`/socket creation, kill+respawn cycles) has a resource leak or a too-tight timeout under concurrent fleet load, rather than assuming it's simply "the box is busy" — per repo convention this needs root-causing, not deferring.

Not investigated further here (out of scope for the task in progress + would require dedicated attention to the fixture/timeout tuning). Filing per the "a suspected bug is always filed" mandate — this is a real, reproducible, fleet-blocking gate risk if this file is ever load-bearing on a merge gate.

report.message: durable admission record could not be persisted: canceling statement due to lock timeout | sqlstate=55P03 — task exits 1 and is counted as a test failure; retry re-hits the same error

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
OBSERVED in the canonical run 7 log (/tmp/p005-run7-runlog.stripped, run=241941-199610b3).

The task `@papercusp/operator-core :: lint:prompt-projections` emitted:

  AFFECTED_TASK_OUTPUT_BEGIN task="@papercusp/operator-core :: lint:prompt-projections" label=initial lane=serial workers=15 memoryMb=15360 exitStatus=1 signal=none error="durable admission record could not be persisted: canceling statement due to lock timeout | sqlstate=55P03"

and the SAME error on its `label=retry` attempt.

WHY THIS IS A BUG, not just an unlucky run:

1. FALSE RED. The guard itself is green. Re-run at HEAD: `node scripts/check-prompt-projections.mjs` exits 0 — canonical libs/papercusp/packages/harness/blueprints/base/prompts/su.md (sha256 0b998acc8bf0d3c3d128edc021ad4c5e31860df6905ecd61c003ebf8c8df72bb, 74226 bytes) matches both generated projections, mismatches=[]. The exit 1 was produced by the admission layer, not the check.

2. INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A GENUINE FAILURE. The task surfaces only as exitStatus=1. It landed in `unattributed` (reason=no-file-rows) purely because it emits no per-file rows — i.e. it was excluded from the file-level accounting by accident of shape, not because anything recognized it as infrastructure. A guard that DID emit file rows would have been reported as a plain red with no hint that the cause was a lock timeout.

3. THE RETRY DOES NOT RECOVER IT. Both attempts failed on the identical sqlstate=55P03. A retry that re-enters the same contended write path cannot clear a lock-timeout class, so the retry budget is spent without changing the outcome.

CONSEQUENCE. This inflates a canonical run's failure count with non-verdicts. The repo already has the correct concept — capability:bash_output distinguishes failure_class=infrastructure-resource-limit with test_verdict=undetermined, and the plan's own D-006/D-019 say an undetermined run is not a verdict — but affected-tests does not apply it here. On a full-suite run that must exit 0 to satisfy P-004, an infrastructure lock timeout is currently able to block the gate indefinitely, and every agent triaging it will go read a guard that is perfectly green.

CORRECT STATE. An admission/ledger persistence failure should mark the task `undetermined` with an explicit infrastructure failure_class — never fold it into the failed-task count as if the task's own command had failed — and the retry path should either back off against lock contention or report that it re-hit the same infrastructure class rather than consuming an attempt silently.

admissionIdentity.titleKey: title:actionability budget count degrades desc discarding escalation hydrated partition phase planrecurrenceescalation signatures sorts succeeds the

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
LATENT — currently costs ZERO actions. Filed because it is an inverse-scaling defect: it gets worse precisely as the mechanism it lives in starts working. Do not "fix" it before the EI-21889809467644493 ranking fix has deployed and been measured, or attribution for both is lost.

## The defect
`selectRecurringSignatures` (phase 1, recurrence-escalation.ts:127) deliberately partitions signatures ACTIONABLE-FIRST (openCount>0) before applying RECURRING_SIGNATURE_SCAN_CAP=50 — that partition is the whole content of the EI-21889809467644493 fix, which restored the documented >=3 threshold from an effective ~15.

`planRecurrenceEscalation` (line 181) then throws that ordering away:

    const recurring = signatureRecurrence(all).filter((s) => s.count >= threshold);

`signatureRecurrence` returns `count desc` (digest.ts:606). So the planner re-orders the hydrated 50 by raw count — the exact ranking whose "strongest evidence first" rationale was the original defect — and spends its `maxActions` budget in that order.

An exhausted signature (no open member) cannot produce escalate-severity or route-gym: both need `newestOpenUnclaimed`, and line 205 `if (!target) continue` bails. But the cross-scope `suggest-promotion` push at line 188 sits ABOVE that guard, so a fully-resolved signature with >=2 scopes still consumes a budget slot and a capture round-trip whose result is then discarded by capture-side dedup (dedupScope defaults to 'all', blocking on any prior state match — see the EI-9170 note at line 330).

## Why it is harmless TODAY (measured, 2026-08-30 ~15:05Z, live topic corpus 27,546 rows)
396 signatures clear >=3; 49 actionable, 347 exhausted. Phase 1 therefore hands the planner 49 actionable + 1 exhausted. With only ONE exhausted group in the hydrated set there is almost nothing for the count-desc re-sort to promote, and simulation of the real emission order gives 0/10 budget slots spent on exhausted signatures (2 suggest-promotion + 8 escalate-severity, all on signatures with an open member).

## Why it degrades as escalation SUCCEEDS
The 49/347 split is what makes the re-sort invisible. As escalation does its job and actionable signatures get resolved, the actionable count falls and exhausted signatures take more of the 50 slots. The count-desc re-sort then floats the highest-count clusters to the front of the budget — and on this corpus those are the machine-authored templated families ("Hive papercusp: fleet saturated with work still queued" x357 and kin), which are overwhelmingly resolved. At ~10 actionable signatures, 40 exhausted groups hydrate and the count-desc head of that set can consume the entire 10-action budget on suggest-promotions that capture dedup discards — restoring the original starvation through a second, unfixed copy of the same ranking mistake.

This is the same class as the shipped fix, one function downstream: a cap plus a strongest-evidence-first ordering becomes a ranking FLOOR whenever the population has a heavy machine-authored head.

## Proposed fix (small)
Preserve the actionability partition in the planner, mirroring phase 1 — either iterate `[...actionable, ...exhausted]` inside `planRecurrenceEscalation`, or gate the line-188 `suggest-promotion` push on the signature having an open member so budget can never be spent on an action whose capture is certain to dedup away. Prefer the former: it keeps the two phases' orderings consistent, and consistency between them is the property that broke here.

Guard it behaviourally, not by field name: a regression test should assert that with a hydrated set dominated by high-count EXHAUSTED signatures, every emitted action still belongs to a signature with an open member. That test fails today.

## Reproduction
    /tmp/su-planner-sim.mjs   (simulates phase1 -> phase2 -> planner over /tmp/su-corpus3.tsv)
Vary the actionable/exhausted mix to see the budget flip; at the live 49/347 mix it reports 0 wasted slots.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
## What I measured

`routines:list { name:'work-item-admission-promoter', installSlug:'papercusp' }` at 2026-09-02T22:31Z:

```
cron: 0 */30 * * * *   active: true   targetRole: system:work-item-admission-promoter
lastFiredAt: 2026-09-02T22:30:57.254Z
nextFireAt:  2026-09-02T23:00:00.000Z
health: { last_error: "The usage limit has been reached" }
```

The routine is **firing on schedule and failing inside the tick.** Its sibling `work-item-admission-fail-open` is healthy (`health: null`, fired 22:16:53Z, next 22:45).

Admission census, `harness_shared.work_items`, workspace `papercusp-workspace`, last 6h, `lane IS DISTINCT FROM 'observation'`:

| admission | n | oldest | newest |
|---|---|---|---|
| (null) | 949 | 16:31 | 22:30 |
| unreviewed | 76 | 16:32 | **21:10** |
| auto | 34 | 16:41 | 22:17 |
| pending | 17 | **21:28 (64 min)** | 22:22 |

The oldest `pending` row is **past the 60-minute fail-open guarantee** the claim refusal advertises, and no fail-open promotion has landed since 21:10.

## Verified at the source, not inferred from bucket names

`work-items-admission-promoter.ts:2179` — `SET admission = 'unreviewed', admitted_at = now(), admitted_by = ${FAIL_OPEN_ACTOR} ... AND admission = 'pending'`. So `unreviewed` is written by the FAIL-OPEN path specifically. That is what makes the census above readable: a growing `pending` bucket with a frozen `unreviewed` high-water mark is the promoter not screening, with the backstop not yet eligible.

## The actual defect — the silence, not the outage

A `system:*` targetRole means this routine is LLM-backed, so account starvation takes out its whole tick. A coord broadcast at ~22:32Z reads `infra-liveness RECOVERED (accounts-starved)`, which names the mechanism and says it has since cleared — so this instance is a self-recovering flap.

That does not make it a non-issue, for one reason: **the degraded mode is indistinguishable from the healthy one at every surface an agent or operator actually looks at.**

- Items still get admitted, so nothing appears broken.
- They are admitted `unreviewed` by `FAIL_OPEN_ACTOR` — i.e. **never duplicate-screened at all** — which is precisely the safety property admission exists to provide.
- The only trace is `health.last_error` on the routine row. Nothing raises it, and the claim-refusal text an agent sees says only "this floor CLEARS ON ITS OWN", which reads as normal operation.
- Latency silently doubles: every item rides the 60-minute backstop instead of the 30-minute screened path.

So during any account-starvation window, duplicate screening across the workspace is quietly OFF while continuing to look on. That is the same defect class this tree treats as first-order everywhere else — a bounded/failed instrument whose output is indistinguishable from a real result.

Worth noting as a plausible instance rather than a proven one: I minted **four duplicate consults** on one plan earlier today. I have not established a causal link and am not claiming one; it is the kind of outcome this failure mode would produce.

## Suggested fix, in preference order

1. **Make the degradation loud.** When the promoter's tick fails, emit/alert rather than only stamping `health.last_error`. A silently fail-open screening gate is the whole bug.
2. **Distinguish the two admissions the census cannot.** `unreviewed` currently conflates "screened and found clean" with "never screened, admitted by timeout". `admitted_by = FAIL_OPEN_ACTOR` already carries the truth — surface it wherever admission state is read, so a fail-open backlog is visible as one.
3. **Survive partial starvation.** A per-item try/catch with backoff would let a tick screen what it can instead of losing the whole batch to the first usage-limit rejection.

## Reproduction

Starve the account the `system:work-item-admission-promoter` role routes through, then file an unassigned work-item and watch: the promoter tick errors, the item sits `pending` for the full 60 minutes, and is then admitted `unreviewed` by `FAIL_OPEN_ACTOR` having never been screened.

## Note on this filing

Filed unassigned, so this item will itself sit in the `pending` queue it describes — a usable end-to-end check of the behaviour above.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Measured 2026-09-05T12:00-12:07Z while working EI-20589765301078360 (swapfile shrink). This is a SEPARATE volume from that item's target (/mnt/data) and is not mentioned in it.

## The measurement

    /dev/nvme0n1p2  1.9T  1.8T   39G  98%  /

Stable, not a spike: three consecutive `df` samples 2s apart read 39.6 / 39.6 / 39.5 GiB avail.

⚠ PROVENANCE / SELF-CORRECTION: an earlier single sample in the same session read 21G (99%), and I was about to file this as "actively filling, ~25 min to zero". Re-measuring showed that was a TRANSIENT dip that recovered. The trend claim was wrong and is retracted here so it does not propagate. What is true is the chronic level (98%), not a fill rate. Anyone re-checking should take several samples before asserting a direction.

## Why it matters

- `/var/lib/postgresql` = 99G and lives on this volume. Postgres is the operator's canonical store; ENOSPC there is a fleet-wide outage, not a local inconvenience.
- ~69 agents run against this box, and the p046-pinned overlay mounts are all backed by `/`.
- 9.0 GiB is currently held in 2280 deleted-but-still-open file handles on this volume (measured via `lsof +L1`), i.e. already-freed space that no process has released.

## Reclaim candidates (dated, look like one-off residue — NOT verified dead, needs an owner check)

    48G  /home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace-RESTORE-1845
    38G  /home/marsh-office/hetzner-rescue-20260821

Both are dated one-shot artifacts (a restore copy and a rescue snapshot from 2026-08-21). Together ~86G, which would roughly triple current headroom. I did NOT delete them: they are not mine, I cannot establish from here whether anyone still needs them, and deleting another agent's or the owner's data on a shared box is exactly the class of action that needs an explicit owner call rather than an autonomous one.

## Suggested next action

Confirm with the owner whether those two dated trees are still needed; if not, removing them is a zero-risk ~86G reclaim requiring no swap/OOM exposure at all.

## Not to be confused with

EI-20589765301078360 covers /mnt/data (97%, 2.0TiB swapfile). Different volume, different mechanism, different risk profile. That one now has an executable guarded procedure at scripts/shrink-swapfile.sh.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
## Owner report

[owner:Avi 2026-09-18] "agents use to start with just 70k or so, it might have increased a bit, but it should not have increased that much, and agents with 400k should be able to have like 20+ turns before compacting" — and, separately, that a session could only manage "a couple of turns" inside a 400k window.

**Both are correct and measured.**

## Measured launch cost (session f54de681, 2026-09-18)

From the API usage ledger in the session's own transcript (`$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/<munged-cwd>/<session>.jsonl`, summing `message.usage.{input_tokens,cache_creation_input_tokens,cache_read_input_tokens}` at entry 1):

**Turn 1 = 237,650 prompt tokens, before any work.**

Against the 400k default that is **59.4% consumed at launch**, leaving ~162k; the 90% self-compact trigger at 360k leaves only **~122k of usable headroom**. That is the "couple of turns".

## Where it goes — both halves measured, not estimated

### Tool definitions: 302,727 B for 66 tools (~95k tokens)

Measured off the live wire (`POST /api/mcp tools/list` on :9071, then summing `JSON.stringify(tool).length` for exactly this session's advertised set). Full catalog for reference: **927 tools / 1,894,825 B**.

**12 tools are 53% of the entire tool payload:**

| bytes | tool |
|---:|---|
| 41,304 | `work_items:complete` |
| 24,533 | `work_items:checkpoint` |
| 20,975 | `loop:checkpoint` |
| 12,497 | `plans:audit` |
| 10,273 | `loop:arm` |
| 9,982 | `work_items:list` |
| 8,805 | `plans:get` |
| 8,591 | `work_items:get` |
| 6,942 | `coord:orient` |
| 6,156 | `testing:runs` |
| 6,000 | `testing:run` |
| 5,710 | `recipes:run` |

**The top three alone are 86,812 B (~27k tokens) — 39% of what the OWNER REMEMBERS THE ENTIRE LAUNCH COSTING.**

### Prose: 324,593 B (~81k tokens), measured on disk

| bytes | surface | ceiling? |
|---:|---|---|
| 131,987 | su playbook render (`~/.papercusp/launch-context/session-refresh-<sid>.md`) | **none** |
| 121,670 | spliced project guide (repo `CLAUDE.md`) | **none** |
| 51,228 | carry document (`carry-<sid>.md`) | **none** (see EI-23574761245123331) |
| 18,530 | `~/.papercusp/compaction-strategy.md` | **none** |
| 1,178 | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` | none |

Verified NOT double-counted: grep confirms the playbook render does not contain the spliced CLAUDE.md, so both are delivered separately.

Tool defs + prose + native-client tool schemas + scaffolding reconciles to the measured 237,650.

## Root cause: the per-tool budget is real, enforced, and defeated by a ratchet

`SCHEMA_BYTE_BUDGET = 8_000` exists and is enforced — but `ALLOW_OVER_SCHEMA_BUDGET` pins ~23 tools at whatever they currently weigh, and the guard's own test asserts that a pin at-or-below budget is "dead weight — delete them", so the structure **requires** every pin to sit above budget. The gate can then only fail on growth past the last recorded number, and the last recorded number is whatever the previous agent measured. **The system catches the bloat, writes the number down, and blesses it. Nobody is ever forced to cut.**

The per-field cap cannot save it either: `DESCRIPTION_HARD_MAX = 1,200` chars, while `work_items:complete` assembles 41 KB out of ~100 individually-legal descriptions. The guard is per-FIELD; the cost is per-TOOL.

## Why this is not the already-refuted "135k injection"

A separate claim — that ~135-140k was being injected mid-turn by deferred-tool surfacing — was REFUTED in this same session (see loop checks `#no-135k-injection-refuted`, `#context-hook-first-reading-artifact`): it was the context-pressure hook omitting `cache_read` from its first reading. **That refutation makes THIS issue harder, not smaller** — there is no phantom payload to delete; every one of the 237,650 tokens is content we deliberately send. The work is real reduction.

## Proposed work, highest leverage first

1. **Cut the top 3 tool schemas to budget.** 41,304 + 24,533 + 20,975 = 86,812 B → 24,000 B at the 8,000 budget saves **~62,800 B (~20k tokens) off every agent's launch**. These are prose-dominated (`.describe()` text), not structure.
2. **Convert `ALLOW_OVER_SCHEMA_BUDGET` from a ratchet to a shrink-only budget with a declining ceiling**, so a pin cannot be re-blessed at its current value.
3. **Put a byte ceiling on the two ungoverned prose surfaces** (playbook render 131,987 B, spliced CLAUDE.md 121,670 B), mirroring `CLAUDE_SEED_WIRE_BYTE_BUDGET`.

Target: 237,650 → under 150k, restoring 20+ turns on a 400k window.

## Recheck

Re-read entry 1 of any fresh psu session's transcript ledger; re-run the tools/list byte sum for its advertised set; `wc -c` the five prose surfaces.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
## Observation (measured, not inferred)
- The shared QEMU VM serving the windows smoke rig on 127.0.0.1:2223 has been UP 12 days 18 hours, continuously consuming ~8 vCPUs.
- Its sshd NEVER answers: the connection reaches banner exchange and times out. The PORT IS LISTENING, so any probe that checks reachability rather than a completed handshake reads it as healthy.
- The mac rig on :2222 answers but REJECTS the provisioned `papercup-vm-mac` key.
- Host context: `/` is at 99% (35 GB free of 1.9 TB) and this box runs the whole agent fleet. 8 cores burned continuously for 12+ days is a large invisible tax on every other lane.

## Two distinct defects, deliberately not conflated
1. **The VM is wedged and nobody noticed for 12+ days.** A LISTENING port with a never-completing handshake is the worst available failure shape: invisible to a port probe, surfacing only when someone needs it — which is always mid-release.
2. **There is no detector.** Nothing alarms on a QEMU guest pegging N cores for days, and nothing alarms on a smoke rig that has served no successful run in N days. The second is the one that matters — this is a DETECTOR FAILURE, not merely a wedged process.

## Consequence for releases
The platform-smoke gate is the ONLY gate that exercises an INSTALLED artifact. Provenance and signatures prove the bytes are the bytes we built and signed; they prove nothing about whether the installer RUNS. With the rig wedged, every release since it died has had to override that gate — and an override that is unavoidable every single time stops being a decision and becomes a formality.

## Correction to a claim I was carrying (on the record as FALSE)
I nearly justified the override with a carried note saying the build VM is retired. That was FALSE. WI-5651 retired those VMs as BUILD legs; the SMOKE rig is a separate thing, both ports are live, and a genuine 0.0.19 windows smoke receipt exists on disk from 2026-09-09. The correct justification is that the rig is WEDGED — an evidenced exception. Same override either way, but only one of the two is honest in a ship record.

## Evidence
- `ss -ltnp | grep 222` → :2222 and :2223 both LISTENING.
- `timeout 8 ssh -o BatchMode=yes -p 2223 -i ~/.ssh/papercup-vm-win user@127.0.0.1 true` → timeout at banner exchange; no auth attempt reached.
- The 0.0.21-alpha ship record carries this verbatim as the smoke-gate override reason (/tmp/upload-real.log).

## Durable fix (not just a restart)
Restart/rebuild the guest (recovers 8 cores) and re-provision the mac rig key — then add the MISSING DETECTOR: alarm when a smoke rig has served no successful run in N days, so the gate cannot silently decay again. A restart alone leaves the trap armed.

_claimSubjectBaseline.summary:
## Observation (measured, not inferred)

1. **The VM is wedged and nobody noticed for 12+ days.** A LISTENING port with a never-completing handshake is the worst available failure shape: invisible to a port probe, surfacing only when someone needs it — which is always mid-release.
2. **There is no detector.** Nothing alarms on a QEMU guest pegging N cores for days, and nothing alarms on a smoke rig that has served no successful run in N days. The second is the one that matters — this is a DETECTOR FAILURE, not merely a wedged process.

terminalCompletionEvidence.verifiedHow: Read the current recovery writer, detached-run snapshot store, and adequacy reader. The bug report measured a detached run ending with exit code 143 at its 300-second limit, with no attributed integration-file row. Focused evidence tests exercise terminal, running, and measured-result paths; the detached builder test checks the recovery ceiling; the operator-core typecheck reports no new errors.

rootCauseVerification.hypothesis: recoverTestEvidence trusted only per-file test-ledger rows and did not inspect the detached process snapshot. When the process had terminated before a file-level row was attributed, finishTestEvidence appended another pending binding, leaving an attempt that could never settle. The detached process also inherited a 300-second deadline that was too short for the measured integration suite plus its adjacent unit group.
rootCauseVerification.testResult: All distinctions matched the hypothesis: terminal/no-row retracted both exact-run pending bindings with no pass binding; running/no-row stayed pending; a terminal run with a measured pass stayed settled and retracted its pending twin; the detached runtime limit was 900 seconds.
rootCauseVerification.testProcedure: Run evidence.test.ts and the focused run.integration.test.ts case 'gives detached recovery an independent runtime floor beyond the foreground timeout'; run the operator-core typecheck.
rootCauseVerification.actualObservation: The implementation reads getRunAsync during recovery. The 143/no-row test reports terminal-no-result, retires IDs 1 and 2, creates no replacement pending/pass row, and leaves the evidence bundle incomplete. The running test performs no retraction. The measured-pass case preserves testRunId 42 and retires its pending predecessor. Both detached request builders report runtimeMaxSec 900.
rootCauseVerification.distinguishingTest: Recover the same prepared evidence with an empty file ledger and a durable terminal exit-143 snapshot, then compare it with a running snapshot and with a terminal run that has an exact measured file-level pass. Inspect binding retractions, row phases, and the detached request runtimeMaxSec.
rootCauseVerification.alternativeHypothesis: The process was still running or an attributed file-level test failure existed; the clause failure came only from adequacy selecting an older pending twin.

predictedObservations.hypothesis: A terminal run with absent file attribution is surfaced as terminal-no-result and its pending rows are retracted; a running process remains pending; a measured file result is settled and supersedes its same-attempt pending rows; detached recovery is capped at 900 seconds.
predictedObservations.alternativeHypothesis: The terminal snapshot will not change pending rows, or cleanup will remove the measured file result; increasing the detached ceiling will not change the builder's runtimeMaxSec.

report.message: serverMeasurement unavailable: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading Latest)

_claimSubjectBaseline.body: [observed 2026-10-01 00:53Z, su-c0b38c83, plan blueprint-backed-work-item-execution-2026-09-23] Same args { currentness:['stale'], detail:'summary' } with limit 60/100/300 returned count 47/76/205, each with bounded.truncatedByLimit:false and currentness.stale equal to count. So count reads as a total while it is the stale subset of the newest N rows. Cause [observed code]: spec-evidence-store.ts listSpecEvidence applies SQL `LIMIT ${limit}` (~L1444, ORDER BY observed_at DESC) and only then filters by options.currentness in memory (~L1665); get-spec-evidence.ts:107 computes truncatedByLimit from the post-filter lookahead, which the filter can remove. Effect: an agent sizing ship-readiness work from count sees 47 stale rows when 205 exist. This is the CLAUDE.md 'a caller's limit bounds ROW LISTS ONLY — never an aggregate' class. Durable fix: when a currentness filter is present, classify a census-bounded population (e.g. the 1000 safety cap) before limiting, and set truncatedByLimit from the pre-slice filtered length (plus a censusTruncated marker if the census cap itself was hit). Guard: a test that binds >limit rows of which several are stale and asserts count/truncatedByLimit are honest. Workaround used: limit:1000 (205 < 1000).

admissionIdentity.titleKey: title:after audio chrome devices long loses meet profile restart running server

_claimSubjectBaseline.body: Observed during WI-10003061 at 2026-09-24 20:08 EDT: Avraham's live Google Meet prejoin showed both 'Microphone not found' and 'Speaker not found' while the Logitech BRIO camera worked. PipeWire listed BRIO as the unmuted default source and an HDMI default sink, but pactl source-outputs had no Chrome input stream. The live Chrome AudioService process (PID 2255387) began 2026-09-18, before pipewire-pulse and WirePlumber restarted 2026-09-23. I terminated only that exact AudioService PID and reloaded the prejoin tab; Chrome respawned AudioService PID 2950144, Meet then showed Default microphone/speaker with an unmuted mic button, source-outputs #1255/#1269 captured from BRIO source 63 unmuted at 100%, and sink-input #1250 appeared. A separate raw BRIO sample delivered 196608 bytes with peak 742; no audio content was saved. This restores this call, but the repair combined AudioService restart and page reload, so it does NOT distinguish stale service binding from a stale page. A future recurrence should test reload alone first, then targeted AudioService restart, and extend the existing fixmic/browser recovery path with a detector or health check. Do not USB-reset the BRIO; that can create the PipeWire lost-handle fault documented in prior microphone work. Treat current action as a temporary mitigation pending causal verification and a recurrence guard.

The task's command ran `sudo -n bpftrace ...` (root child inside the user-manager scope). The user systemd manager refuses to signal the unit because it contains a root-owned process, so the documented stop lever for a backgrounded capability:bash job has no path for sudo children. report.message: [db-call-deadline @ d740fc3802] "boundedPgReadTxn:acquire(admin)" did not resolve within 8000ms (waited 19345ms). No acquire measurements were available for this call, so both causes are still open. Two causes present identically at this point — (a) the pool's resolved endpoint is unreachable and postgres.js is silently retrying its INITIAL connect forever without rejecting (WI-7097), or (b) the CLIENT pool's acquire queue is saturated while the server is perfectly healthy. Server capacity does NOT decide (b), so dev:service_health / pg_stat_activity looking fine is not evidence against it — check this process's own pcusp:<pool>:p<pid> rows and PAPERCUSP_DB_POOL_MAX before the endpoint (WI-7097).

New targeted papercusp-dev-api.service logs show the sentinel reported STALLED at 02:58:57.896Z after 10,018ms (main thread spinning, state R, 0.99 cores, CPU PSI some60=5.4), then SIGKILLed request-worker PID 2970199 at 02:59:11.910Z after 24,031ms (mode kill, 20,000ms threshold, 0.98 cores, PSI=5.77). At 02:59:22 a PAPERCUSP_BACKGROUND_WORKERS=0 secondary host booted; the live systemd operator unit nRestarts=0 supports worker respawn without a unit restart, so the title remains accurate. Same-window bounded-timeout lines for turn-start executable frontier and agent-obligations show slow work but do not identify a caller; system journal had no OOM/hung-task/lockup matches. This establishes a nearby request-worker CPU-spin class, not exact linkage to the earlier 02:57 sample or the JS frame. The prior carry-note statement that 02:50–03:05Z had zero service-journal entries was wrong. The worker is gone, so its JS stack cannot be recovered. No code change is justified from this trace alone: on the next recurrence, act on the first STALLED line (~10s stale), send SIGUSR1 to the reported Node PID, capture /json/list and a 3–5s V8 sampling profile before the 20s kill threshold, plus per-thread /proc state/wchan/cgroup and unit+system journals. _claimSubjectBaseline.body:
The shared checkout's .git/index was truncated to zero bytes at 15:00:46Z, causing index readers to fail with 'index file smaller than expected' rather than return repository state. WI-10004909 records git-sync's declaration inventory and superproject commits blocked until read-tree rebuilt the index. WI-10004910 records a historical mutation probe rejecting a tracked file during the same index-error window; misclassifying the failed tracked-file check as 'untracked' is the inferred downstream mechanism. WI-10004911 independently confirms the zero-byte index, repeated Git failures, and doc-claims census failures that disappeared after index recovery (883/883 tests passed). The common upstream fault is the corrupt index, not missing file tracking or individual guard regressions. The truncating writer remains unidentified; coincident git-sync/bg-host activity does not establish responsibility.

Shared-root-cause evidence: Three current items connect the same zero-byte index incident and fatal read signature to multiple Git-backed workflows. The corrupt index is measured even though the responsible writer is unknown.

report.message: cross-user assignment is pull-only (D-005) for two su sessions with userId null

_claimSubjectBaseline.body: Measured 2026-10-06 01:01Z. coord:dispatch { to: su-4a152da3-..., planSlug: unified-bug-pipeline-and-honest-queue-2026-10-05, items: [P-006..P-017] } from su-93aaa593 returned ok:false for P-006 and P-010 with: "agent target 'su-4a152da3-...' resolves to ownerId 'su-4a152da3-...' owned by another user ('su-4a152da3-...') — cross-user assignment is pull-only (D-005)". Both are interactive su sessions of the same owner (Avi); coord:whoami reports userId:null. With no userId, the resolver seems to treat each ownerId as its own user, so every su->su dispatch is refused as cross-user and the owner-approved execution route (plan D-016) can only be done by a message plus a self-claim. The 'another user' text names the target ownerId, which supports that reading, but I have not read the resolver. Workaround: coord:send { wake:'required', expects:'action' } asking the peer to claim. Expected: same-human su sessions are same-user, or a null userId falls back to workspace owner.

admissionIdentity.titleKey: title:15s 2026 53z across awaits batch bursts drain drained host mark once pending select stage stalls substrate undrained workspaces

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed [logs:read papercusp-bg-host, grep 'STAGE STALL', 04:40-06:55Z 2026-10-02]: 16 [stage-stall] lines in 4 bursts of 4, at 04:40, 05:46, 06:50 and 06:53Z. Each burst hits papercusp-workspace::restart, default::spoon-knife-hive and papercusp-workspace::hello-world on 'select-undrained-batch', plus papercusp-workspace::papercusp on 'mark-drained (row id=14688916)', all 'still pending after 15000ms' in the same millisecond. Since the stage-stall watchdog fired on time, the bg-host event loop was alive, which points to the DB side (lock wait, pool starvation, or a slow plan). Cause [unconfirmed]. Not caused by the wedged-identity sweep: it fired once at 06:52:35Z and three of the four bursts are not aligned with it (WI-10004852 evidence). Next probe: at the next burst, sample pg_stat_activity (wait_event, state, query_start) for the bg-host's connections and check the bg-host pool queue depth. Related closed precedents: EI-22433048526307249 (DB_POOL_MAX starvation), WI-3825 (inbox fanout seq scan).

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Original retrieval and security continuations are omitted from coordination while their matching PSU PTY hosts remain live, so coord:send refuses unknown_recipient and a correct fork:false resume refuses duplicate live ownership.

Measured evidence (2026-11-06; complete receipts at EI-25180316715417887#1217033 and EI-28081291096944491#1217034): exact workspace-scoped ADV reads with a passing same-table control returned rows55265/55262, matching original owner/native UUIDs, ended_atNULL, started2026-11-05, outside the current10-minute recorded bootstrap window, and no coord_presence rows. Matching host metadata binds those same owner/ADV/native identities with sockets present. Targeted reconciled task-ledger rows remain running. Supported current3170 explicit-false resumes refused LIVE before spawning anyprocess. This proves the roster/host disagreement; why the hosted CLIs did not re-register presence is still unknown.

Cause of the observed addressability failure: recipient-resolve.ts/readKnownOwnerIds consults presence and listRecordedLiveSessions, whose default started_at cutoff is RECORDED_ADV_SESSION_FRESH_SEC=600. resolveResumeTarget instead checks verified findLiveHostAsync. Thus an older genuine local host can be correctly protected against duplicate resume but absent from the message-recipient roster. Do not fix this by widening a timeout/age limit, accepting arbitrary unknown IDs, forging presence, killing the old host or creating a replacement.

Reuse-first repair proposal: extend the existing targeted recipient path with getLatestActiveAdvSessionByOwner(exactOwner,workspace), already age-independent and newest-row scoped, plus existing verified findLiveHostAsync. Require exact owner, workspace and immutable ADV binding agreement; preserve ended/superseded/retired rejection, prefix ambiguity, caller/assignee rules and cached broad-roster behavior. No global PTY-directory scan or parallel identity authority. Add maintained recipient-resolve.test.ts regression coverage for aged-out genuine local sessions and wrong workspace/owner/ADV, stale host, superseded record and ordinary roster/prefix cases. terminalCompletionEvidence.testResult: Focused file passed 111/111 at local HEAD f7abe91dfd; the new same-proof test failed before the source fix with disclosed-gap not-applicable, and passed after it. The focused run exercised local source and test edits; it did not verify a deployed runtime.
terminalCompletionEvidence.verifiedHow: Current runtime evidence showed bindings 23753 and 23762 share testRunId 20700025 and identical fingerprints, while only 23753 carried disclosedGap; the pre-fix evaluator rated that criterion not-applicable. The post-fix unit test retains the gap for identical proof and allows closure in both new-proof controls. git diff --check passed.

rootCauseVerification.hypothesis: activeSpecEvidence collapses binding history by logical clause/evidence reference, while disclosed-gap grading reads only the projected row; a metadata-only rebind therefore erased a disclosure from the same immutable proof.
rootCauseVerification.testResult: Before the fix the identical-proof case rated not-applicable. After the fix it rated fail and blocked; both changed-proof controls rated not-applicable. The focused suite passed 111/111.

rootCauseVerification.actualObservation: Runtime binding rows 23753 and 23762 had the same testRunId 20700025 and identical fingerprints; only 23753 had the disclosed gap. The pre-fix evaluation selected 23762 and rated disclosed-gap not-applicable, while the overall verdict was unknown for separate criteria. The pre-fix regression matched this result and the post-fix suite passed.
rootCauseVerification.distinguishingTest: Grade two bindings for one exact clause and logical evidence reference with identical testRunId, coverage reference, and fingerprints, where only the older row has disclosedGap; compare with controls where the active row changes testRunId or source fingerprint.
rootCauseVerification.alternativeHypothesis: The current data contained genuinely new server-current proof that superseded the older disclosure, or the disclosed row was absent from the exact clause evidence population.

1. plans:get-spec-evidence {harness:'papercusp', slug:'cloud-dashboard-stripe-test-rollout-2026-10-03', specIds:['AUTO-BAR-R-1-P-001'], detail:'full'} → 4 bindings, all currentness=current. Binding 23753 (WI-10005828, 2026-10-03T12:53:27Z) has evidenceRef 'test-run-group:27fc109b-8102-46c5-b201-23068af16109:0' and testRunId 20700025. Its details.adequacy.disclosedGap = 'Registered injected Stripe account/offer unit controls; deployed account independently verified. Commercial metering remains outside approved scope.' Binding 23762 (13:07:22Z) has the SAME evidenceRef, the same testRunId and identical source/test fingerprints. It has NO disclosedGap and adds the fixtureCalibrated and oracleIndependent flags. Binding 23747 is a third copy.
2. plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy {harness:'papercusp', slug:'cloud-dashboard-stripe-test-rollout-2026-10-03', classRef:'plan-class-feature-ship', specIds:['AUTO-BAR-R-1-P-001'], specRevision:2, specFingerprint:'0f8323ea2c629d7effcda0a99cbe2f1a9d6f799a7f1516fc3535ae4885bbd59a', replaySnapshot:true, includeDraft:true, detail:'full'} (UNSCOPED, no evidenceRefs pin) → selects only bindings 23769 and 23762. It returns disclosed-gap 'not-applicable' with evidence 'No bound proof … records a disclosed gap', clause verdict 'pass', wouldBlock [].

Why this is a bug: the spec-test-adequacy rubric (rev 6) disclosed-gap drift marker explicitly lists 'a gap treated as mitigated by re-binding without closing it'. Here a re-bind with no new run erases an author disclosure from the machine verdict. The emitted evidence string also does not say that current bindings were excluded.

Mechanism UNCONFIRMED [inferred]: the evaluator appears to keep only the latest binding per (workItem, spec, revision, evidenceRef). I could not read the source because the judge principal lacks intel:read for code:structural and dev:pg_query.

Suggested fix: make disclosed-gap read adequacy.disclosedGap across every current binding of the clause, or carry a disclosure forward until a binding with NEW evidence (a different testRunId or fingerprint) explicitly closes it. Name the excluded or superseded binding ids in the evidence string.

Related (not the same issue): EI-24815130936541168 (disclosedGap read only from details.adequacy) and EI-24159008584241244 (dirty runs counted as durable). The sibling card EI-25199581201461275 on the same clause passed its audit (EI-25199769430569899) and may share this defect; I did not check it.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-06 (su-16da39cf, WI-10006486). `node scripts/check-behavioural-strands.mjs --base a0b2d4d60d --files apps/operator-vite/src/components/adv/AdvFramesTab.tsx` exited 0 and reported a strand trigger in libs/generic/memory/src/local-embedder-worker.script.mjs (a peer's change), never naming the declared file. Root cause (read in source): argv parse at scripts/check-behavioural-strands.mjs:2437 only matches `a.startsWith('--files=')`; the space-separated form is not recognized, the stray token is dropped without error, and the detector falls back to `git diff --name-only <base>` over the WHOLE shared tree (line 2480) = every peer's work. Re-run with `--files=<list>` scoped correctly (useSyncQuery 0->1, nothing reachable). Impact: a verdict about someone else's diff that reads as a check of yours. Fix: reject unknown args with exit 2 (or accept both forms) + a test that `--files X` scopes or refuses. Evidence: .papercusp/scratch/bash-a7876d20-58d.log (wrong scope) vs .papercusp/scratch/strands-p007.log (scoped).

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
OBSERVED 2026-10-06 ~12:57Z, judge session su-f042ca59. The session env had PAPERCUSP_HOME=/home/marsh-office/.papercusp-workspaces/papercusp-workspace/.papercusp and PAPERCUSP_OPERATOR_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9071. Per WI-10006600, scripts/mcp-call.mjs reads $PAPERCUSP_HOME/superuser-token (65 bytes, mtime 2026-09-30 20:56Z) before ~/.papercusp/superuser-token (33 bytes, mtime 2026-08-23).

Results (scorecards:get, same args):
- default port with PAPERCUSP_HOME set: request_rejected superuser_invalid_bearer
- --port 3070: superuser_invalid_bearer
- --port 3170: superuser_invalid_bearer
- --port 9071: OK
- `env -u PAPERCUSP_HOME` (falls back to the ~/.papercusp token), default port: OK

So the sanctioned recovery path in the judge persona and CLAUDE.md (mcp-call.mjs, the fallback when native tools die) fails out of the box in fleet-spawned sessions whose PAPERCUSP_HOME is the workspace dir. That leaves exactly the zombie case EI-1758 warns about. Root cause is unconfirmed: either :3070/:3170 do not accept the workspace token, or the default port resolution picks a direct port. FIX: mcp-call should try the alternate token (or route via :9071) on superuser_invalid_bearer, and the refusal message should name which token path and port it used.

Cause unconfirmed: a per-field string limit on code:run's summary projection (summaryNotice.truncated) is the [inferred] mechanism.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body: Observed 2026-10-06 14:30-14:45Z (su-7f8d7809, plan crm-agent-sales-onboarding-apps-2026-10-06 P-010). The live E2E submitted crm onboarding-step (receipt 38) creating WI-10006707 (harness crm, kind crm-proposal, unassigned), then cancelled it through the seam: cancelBlueprintOperation (packages/operator-core/lib/blueprint/operation-service.ts ~L680) returned accepted:true, handled:false, effected:false and only stamped payload.blueprintCancellation. 15 minutes later the item is still open. Placement skips it (coord-program-workflow excludes blueprintCancellation; operation-worker-binding requireUncancelled), so no worker will ever take it, and a direct work_items:set_state dropped through the app invoker is refused: "blueprint operation effect refused: accepted operation item requires its applied worker". Result: every cancel before a worker applies leaves a permanent open, unplaceable item and an operation stuck in cancelling. Proposed fix: when cancel finds no applied worker binding on an unsettled item, settle it to a cancelled/dropped terminal state inside the same transaction (the operator is the authority when no executor exists); add a test that cancel-before-apply reaches phase terminal / outcome cancelled. Live example left in place: WI-10006707. Evidence: papercusp/.papercusp/scratch/p010/e2e-2.log, drop-3.log.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
P003 observed new evidence beyond a plain tool failure. work_items:complete {id:EI-27982872070632258,harness:papercusp,recordOnly:true,assumptions:none,completion:<structured root cause/tests/files proof>} returned ok:true and echoed completion with19 passing installed controls. Both subsequent direct work_items:get and independent current-build3271 readback (/tmp/egm-1447-reporter-readback.json) show completion:null,hasCompletionEvidence:false,state:open. Current source packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/work_items/complete.ts has persistence in effectiveState branch and already-terminal branch (~5890), but an intentionally recordOnly open item takes neither writer. It can emit a completion without storing row evidence. Durable fix: extend the existing completion-evidence persistence path to support intentional recordOnly on an open item without changing state or emitting terminal lifecycle events; report an explicit persistence receipt. Add real framework regression completing recordOnly on an open issue and feature then reading the same row, and assert evidence persists,state/claims stay open,and no done event fires. Keep existing settled-item proof precedence and authority fences. Main task evidence will be preserved by checkpoint instead of claiming this echo is stored.

admissionDeltaSweep.reason: Three differently-worded reports converge on one live auto-commit lease/pass and incomplete source propagation. The grouping does not assume disk pressure, dead ownership, or a proven internal phase defect.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
EI-25302059364775800 and WI-10007098 identify the same live auto-commit owner, system:git-sync:1744589:a72eec88-71f5-4058-a07f-cfdd70018e94, retaining git-sync:papercusp; sanctioned manual runs return held_exclusive and bounded waits expire. EI-25302410770886637 observes a local-sync pass progressing from 05:48 past 06:48 while five newly created proof files remain untracked despite no active path locks. Across these reports, committed desktop fixes remain absent from the root gitlink and a verified Codex regression lacks a containing commit, even though root HEAD continues advancing. The concrete shared bottleneck is the long-lived exclusive writer preventing alternate sync attempts while source propagation remains incomplete. Investigate the existing owner's phase, file-census timing, and submodule-pointer scheduling together. The reason the pass is long and the precise gitlink omission cause remain unproved; preserve the live owner and lease rather than force-unlocking.

Shared-root-cause evidence: Three differently-worded reports converge on one live auto-commit lease/pass and incomplete source propagation. The grouping does not assume disk pressure, dead ownership, or a proven internal phase defect.

Earlier invocation37341211 at05:25:09Z is a DIFFERENT call: soft-failure registered_leader_not_live/buildd33eab6c32. It must not settle the later key.
3. Full targeted current assignments measured no held claims for440e1. Current state is not the timed-out call's terminal result.

Why absence cannot settle the mutation: read packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/transport/_mcp-result-replay.ts. The maintained store is best-effort, caps serialized receipts at256KiB, and sweeps entries older thanone hour. Read _mcp-host.ts: receipts are persisted from the REAL tool outcome after transactional dispatch settles, not the raced timeout envelope; deadline-path persistence is asynchronous. By the exact-key query this incident was beyond the replay horizon. The precise live failure phase, server runtime and commit outcome remain unproved; no resource/load cause asserted. This is an evidence-recovery gap, not proof that the already-maintained late-settlement ordering is broken.

Current-source verification (not a reproduction of the missing live key): maintained mcp-handler-deadline-receipt.test.ts, three focused cases on head df574832a0e2f6970c8682a22e9ac47f2b0f403e, persisted local testing:runs row21182684 (workspacepapercusp-workspace/harnesspapercusp), PASS. _claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-08 ~02:50–03:20Z from a judge-scoped session (grading-integrity audit of EI-25377456345340418, run 1791427485-judge), all via mcp__papercusp__tools_invoke on serving build d5faa7963f.

Symptoms (Claude Code MCP idle timeout = 300s with no progress):
- code:run looping scorecards:get over 9 criteria → no response/progress for 300s, aborted (task k9u5j2meg).
- scorecards:get {issueId:'EI-25377456345340418', criterionKey:'correct-layer', evidenceOffset:2274} → no response for 300s, aborted (k30bpfz06); the IDENTICAL call re-issued minutes later returned normally, so it is not payload size.
- scorecards:list {rubricRef:'spec-test-adequacy', subjectRef:'…'} → no response for 300s, aborted (ke115097e).
- plans:get-spec-evidence {slug, specIds:['RECOVERY-R-4-MISSING'], detail:'full'} → >120s; testing:runs {filePath, sinceHours:24} → >120s; scorecards:list {rubricRef, limit:100} → >120s.
- improvements:capture (this filing) first attempt shed: mcp_proxy_improvements_capture_queue_dwell, waited 20001ms in the dedicated FIFO (traceId 933196f2-26be-40b8-a6c8-e979a33c3a94).
Other calls in the same session (rubrics:get, several scorecards:get pages, plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy) returned in seconds, so the latency is intermittent rather than tied to one tool.

Cause UNKNOWN / unconfirmed. Untested hypotheses: serving-host event-loop saturation, PG pool contention, or proxy FIFO backlog. Suggested probe: harness_shared.tool_invocations for this owner over 02:45–03:20Z; compare durations by tool_name and serving_host, and check proxy queue depth at the capture traceId. A 300s silent stall with no progress notification is itself a defect: long calls should stream progress or fail fast.

admissionIdentity.titleKey: title:door error failed fails intermittently invoke result spill tools unknown with write

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
OBSERVED (judge-scoped session su-5bd1d6e7, 2026-10-08 ~04:58–05:07Z, via tools:invoke):

Two oversized results were bounded by the result door. Their `_projection.cursor` came back as `{kind:'unavailable', reason:'spill-write-failed'}`, with next: "its spill write failed (unknown error), so the omitted bytes are NOT recoverable and no spill path exists".
1. conversations:get { id:'thread-post:1164036' } (originalChars 16556)
2. scorecards:emit (grading-integrity audit EI-25386505288509888, originalChars 9652). The canonicalRatings echo and completionReceipt were lost from the response. The write itself succeeded.

In the same session, five other door spills under ~/.papercusp/scratch/papercusp-workspace/tools:invoke/<uuid>/result-door-*.md SUCCEEDED, including a retry of call 1 with a projection argument. So the failure is intermittent, not a permissions or path problem.

WHY IT MATTERS: the omitted bytes are unrecoverable. An auditor or grader that needs the truncated part (e.g. a reviewer post's census) has to guess a projection to re-fetch it. For a write tool like scorecards:emit, the receipt cannot be re-fetched by re-calling.

CAUSE: UNKNOWN. The error is literally "unknown error": the door swallows the underlying fs/IO error. Suggested first step: log or return the real error (errno, path, byte count) in the cursor `reason`, so the next occurrence is diagnosable. Hypotheses, all unproven: disk headroom (coord traffic at the same time reported git-sync fetch refusals for disk headroom on papercusp/quartermaster), a scratch-dir race, or a size or encoding edge.

REPRO: not deterministic. Call tools:invoke on a >9K-char result a few times under current load and watch _projection.cursor.kind.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Unrelated handlers lose output when the shared result-door projection requires overflow persistence but cannot write the scratch spill. EI-25408351848678899 reports an unavailable checkpoint cursor with spill-write-failed; EI-25409580348208359 and EI-25409749057195100 report explicit 30000ms ETIMEDOUT failures on document results; EI-25409763444620761 reports the same failure on directed mail. EI-25410024981236879 and EI-25410269323486697 instead receive empty output_spill_failed envelopes. The same post-handler failure affects mutations: EI-25410122061838770 retains a recorded receipt but loses canonical output, while EI-25410344016199089 confirms a committed emit whose receipt was entirely swallowed behind retryable:true. Repairing the shared persistence/fallback path addresses these manifestations together. Filesystem contention, disk pressure and writer serialization remain unverified; successfully written spills that cannot be read because of single-line truncation are a separate cause.

The common post-handler result-door path requires scratch persistence when output exceeds projection budgets, but writes fail or outlast the 30-second deadline. EI-25417009217147957 corroborates this shared projection/persistence failure. The actionable scope is the common writer and recovery fallback, preserving committed mutation receipts. Disk contention, pressure, serialization and fsync remain unverified hypotheses; generic MCP timeouts and successful-spill read truncation are separate.

admissionDeltaSweep.reason: Independent allocation failures coincide with direct measurements of exhausted blocks on the same backing device. This is a concrete shared storage cause, not test failures, inferred memory pressure or inode exhaustion.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
The shared /tmp backing filesystem has exhausted free blocks: WI-10007556 measures the 7.3TB nvme1n1 XFS device at 100% with 20KB available, while WI-10007557 independently measures 20480 available bytes with free inodes and headroom on the separate root/home filesystem. Allocation failures then fan out to focused verification reader leases (EI-25433129031369506), three isolated baseline leases (EI-25433416317393037), resolver result redirects and SDK bootstrap (EI-25433462459266428). EI-25433151376112553 shows the same exhaustion preventing mutation-probe digest writes and producing false external-change evidence. WI-10007558 identifies the /tmp bind's /mnt/data backing device and the missing headroom alarm coverage. Restore capacity through protected, sanctioned retention/reclaim and add device-wide headroom checks; the actual artifact producer remains to be established.

Shared-root-cause evidence: Independent allocation failures coincide with direct measurements of exhausted blocks on the same backing device. This is a concrete shared storage cause, not test failures, inferred memory pressure or inode exhaustion.
