report.message: request_rejected: superuser_native_session_verifier_unavailable during the before-batch run authority refresh.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
This item concerns intermittent failure of admin transaction startup during native session verification. The MCP rejection itself is the intentional security boundary: preserve fail-closed verification; do not admit an inherited or unverified native identity.

The original reporter recurrence was captured on 2026-10-09 against b7937697dc. A second encounter occurred during bulk-4903eb58-a140-4b78-b5da-8816ad1309f1 after four allowed acknowledgements and a 100-item recommendation batch. The transcript shows tools:invoke calling inbox:bulk-run-manifest and receiving request_rejected: superuser_native_session_verifier_unavailable before any further bulk report/action. The bulk pass subsequently completed through the sanctioned same-owner CLI route; that route's success alone did not establish native-wrapper health.

The exact second failure is tool_invocations:35038620 at 2026-10-10T01:04:07.336Z, coord owner su-7f5e54d1-974b-4603-9aeb-4cf2487f2a1d, serving process linux:b8c61f1d-f67c-43a8-ac9d-2286713e224f:38294679, build a2c76aa503. Its retained mcpAuthFailure is contextVerified=false, with carrier meta:threadId, candidateAdvSessionId=null and valueFingerprint=51d40c49bf5903be8bfae7dc1bbcf951855c4dc1c0ea365275222fc6c41ee1e0. verifierFailure.name=DbCallDeadlineError; phase=transaction_setup; acquisition.label=boundedOrgTxn:begin(admin); pool=org-admin; deadlineMs=7500; elapsedMs=7499; retryable=true. No PostgreSQL error code was retained. verifierFailure.durationMs=201 is a separate measurement from the deadline object's elapsedMs; the record does not establish that this verifier call itself waited 7499ms. The captured pool/ticket counts are seam diagnostics, not evidence of CPU/RAM exhaustion or a saturated pool.

Current-runtime read-only probe: invoke the same manifest read through the native tools:invoke wrapper, using this session's ordinary metadata. It succeeded at 2026-10-10T01:31:59.128Z/129Z, receipts tool_invocations:35052893 (inner) and 35052894 (wrapper). Both have the EXACT SAME serving process, build a2c76aa503, carrier and native-session fingerprint as the failure, and now show binding=bound, candidateAdvSessionId=39357. adv_sessions:39357 belongs to this Codex owner and started at 2026-10-10T00:46:42.032456Z, before the failure. This establishes current binding and identity continuity; it does not retroactively authorize the rejected call. A fresh failure did not reproduce, so reproduced=true is not claimed.

Security/source check: _mcp-host.ts:1880-1896 rejects on verifier exceptions to prevent the inherited-session authorization bug. The existing registered gating suite covers fail-closed rejection, no terminal callback dispatch, redacted diagnostics, and typed acquire/begin/setup deadline fields. Focused test run 20966201 in papercusp/local passed five selected cases; 328 cases were deliberately excluded by the name filter. Command: npm run test:file -- --require-ran packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/__tests__/mcp-handler-gating-matrix.test.ts -- '--testNamePattern=fails closed with a retryable verifier reason|retains typed .* deadline diagnostics when native verification fails closed'. The unused --require-ran token was treated as a non-test input; actual matched cases and counts are verified in testing:runs. HEAD moved 6fa9ff1f727d to b20fd572c871 during the run, runtime source capture was not configured, and the runner/ledger marked provenance unknown/worktreeDirty=true. These are exploratory guard observations, not build-bound acceptance evidence.

Remaining work: determine why boundedOrgTxn:begin(admin) failed, correlate the relevant verifier request/ticket with transaction/connection diagnostics from that serving process, and establish a durable fix with source-bound regression evidence. The existing current-process completed-query ring does not cover in-flight/acquisition/non-ReadyForQuery failures and cannot substitute for the incident's missing causal trace. The underlying database/startup cause remains unverified. No code change, restart, deadline widening, retry bypass or auth weakening was made. Keep the issue open; no fixed/shipped claim.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
## Scope

This item covers the native `tools:find` session-verifier rejection only. The `coord:orient` delays are separate symptoms and are not evidence of the same defect.

## Verifier rejection evidence

Invocation 34881069 at 2026-10-09T20:08:44.381Z used MCP on port-3271, process linux:b8c61f1d-f67c-43a8-ac9d-2286713e224f:35999738, build 42ead3e6b0. It failed after 7508ms with error_code `mcp_auth_failed` and message `superuser_native_session_verifier_unavailable`. Trace: `40f48bd2-70b7-45be-93ce-b8a449e90658`.

The recorded `mcpAuthFailure.nativeSession.verifierFailure` is a `DbCallDeadlineError` at phase `transaction_setup`, label `boundedOrgTxn:begin(admin)`, deadline 7500ms and elapsed 7506ms. Its acquisition snapshot reports pool `org-admin`, max 28, 21 waiting in pressure (22 active tickets in the sample), and 0 held; the ticket matching the invocation trace waited 7506ms. This identifies the timed-out acquisition stage, but does not establish the physical pool queue cause or a broader root cause.

The invocation row has `args_json: null`, so the exact `tools:find` query is not recoverable from persisted telemetry. The source error text says only “while querying loop:checkpoint schema”; that is not a verbatim query and I am not treating it as one.

## Separate coord:orient observations

The source session's original `coord:orient` invocation 34880904 has trace `27f29ee9-9c70-4551-82b8-0949f7a821b5`, dispatch `invoke=45183.528ms`, and total duration 47852ms. Its status was success with no output_ref; the invocation metadata has no phase diagnostics, so its inner leg is unavailable.

This session's separate `coord:orient` invocation 34923964 has trace `e55b896a-65f9-4da0-ac18-9b331f486c4e`, aggregate elapsed 45011ms, and degraded leg `fleet:assignments` exceeding 8000ms while `coord:inbox` was still active after 23305ms. That observation is filed separately as EI-25538578057719795. It is not evidence that the verifier rejection shares this cause.

## Current status

Current-session `tools:find` calls succeeded; the verifier rejection was not reproduced. The exact source query and the original orientation call's inner leg remain unavailable, and the root cause remains unknown beyond the measured transaction-setup acquisition deadline. No source fix or recurrence test is claimed.

Historical symptom and review revision

This item tracks repeated native-session verifier availability failures surfaced by tools/list and tools:find. The original watchdog aggregate and reproduction receipt tool_invocations:34629939 establish a historical user-visible failure; they do not establish its database cause or present recurrence rate.

Observed evidence
- Historical request-correlated metadata records transaction_setup/setup-timeouts and waiting acquisition tickets. A waiting ticket includes BEGIN/SET LOCAL setup; it does not alone locate checkout, PgBouncer or PostgreSQL wait.
- Saved rows35147193 and35147195–35147198 report SQLSTATE57014 statement timeouts in owner_candidate_rows_lookup; these predate the sampler-trigger patch.
- The saved post-patch exact-object scan35183481 (2026-10-10T05:37:26Z–06:19:05.435Z) reports no matching papercusp-scoped tools/list verifierFailure objects, with an untruncated result and same-scope positive control35147193. This is a bounded historical quiet window, not proof of a fix or current absence.
- The round1 evidence has no preserved time-aligned verifier/PG sample or post-patch live failure/sample-fingerprint correlation. Out-of-window pooler/PG reads do not establish cause; harness_slug='*' rows cannot control a papercusp-only query.

Security boundary
The current _mcp-host.ts catch intentionally fails with superuser_native_session_verifier_unavailable when verification throws, and mcp-handler-gating-matrix.test.ts expects mcp_auth_failed. Preserve that fail-closed behavior. Do not skip verification, cache unverifiable identity as valid, widen authority or treat unavailable verification as success. Existing bounded-deadline/SQLSTATE57014 diagnostic triggers and request fingerprints provide observability; instrumentation alone is not a causal fix.

Current disposition and approach
Cause: unconfirmed. Current recurrence after the saved scan: unmeasured. Before choosing a fix, obtain a bounded real failure with request fingerprint, serving build/process, exact DB phase, sampler interval and contemporaneous pooler/PG activity. Identify the wrong queue/query/setup behavior from that measurement. Verify a causal fix with conventional project tests and a discriminating live/reproduction result, including recurrence guards and unchanged fail-closed behavior. This revision proposes no authentication-path change.

Evidence separation
Git-sync/cache cooldown, reserve, disk-consumer and resource-lock notes are unrelated to verifier causation. _claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Suspected separate health-writer defect, not a reason to reopen settled GC. Current worker2858688's Papercusp operation system:git-sync:2858688:7c43b167-adfa-4be5-9890-a9cd3ee619ef completed with outcome_status=error. New commitc1c8ab113ff0f82968cfbec67fc2d16ddd4317af contains exact tested action/test source hashes; GC generation1 settled at that commit with exact-path-blob-history attestation and authoritycommitted. report.message: harness_scope_reader_error at claim: [db-call-deadline @ d740fc3802] "withWorkspace:acquire(app)" did not resolve within 45000ms (waited 45001ms). MEASURED IN THIS PROCESS (pid 2364479), pool "org-app": 8 acquisition(s) WAITING (oldest 45.0s), 0 HELD at this seam (oldest n/a), pool max 36; last successful acquisition on this pool 63.8s ago (840 total this process). ⇒ this pool DID work earlier but has not obtained a connection for 63.8s, so a previously-good endpoint going away is live again — note the resolved URL is memoized for the process lifetime. (These counts cover acquisitions through withWorkspace/withHarnessSchema in THIS process only: direct pool users are not counted, so HELD is a LOWER BOUND and held < max does NOT mean free slots — and a sibling process, e.g. one vitest worker of ~15, has its own pool entirely.) Two causes present identically at this point — (a) the pool's resolved endpoint is unreachable and postgres.js is silently retrying its INITIAL connect forever without rejecting (WI-7097), or (b) the CLIENT pool's acquire queue is saturated while the server is perfectly healthy. Server capacity does NOT decide (b), so dev:service_health / pg_stat_activity looking fine is not evidence against it — check this process's own pcusp:org-app:p<pid> rows and PAPERCUSP_DB_POOL_MAX before the endpoint (WI-7097).

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Watchdog signal (structural tool-error): coord:thread returned a deterministic error 2× (0% of 579 calls) in the window — the shape that recurs identically (a bug/misconfig), not transient load.

Sample error: [db-call-deadline @ cbeffe4f01] "boundedPgReadTxn:acquire(admin)" did not resolve within 5000ms (waited 5283ms). No acquire measurements were available for this call, so both causes are still open. Two causes present identically at this point — (a) the pool's resolved endpoint is unreachable and postgres.js is silently retrying its INITIAL connect forever without rejecting (WI-7097), or (b) the CLIENT pool's acquire queue is saturated while the server is perfectly healthy. Server capacity does NOT decide (b), so dev:service_health / pg_stat_activity looking fine is not evidence against it — check this process's own pcusp:<pool>:p<pid> rows and PAPERCUSP_DB_POOL_MAX before the endpoint (WI-7097).

admissionIdentity.titleKey: title:30000ms door emit etimedout exceeded invoke response result scorecards scratch spill tools write

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-11 ~00:52Z (judge su-6b349bd0, served by build 22a41ff6e9). tools:invoke { name:'scorecards:emit' } for a grading-integrity audit returned ok:true, completionReceipt { status:'recorded', effectRef:'EI-25642263855564483' }. The response projection's spill to scratch failed with: _projection.cursor { kind:'volatile-scratch-page', reason:'spill-write-failed', errorCode:'ETIMEDOUT', errorDetail:'Error: result-door scratch spill write exceeded 30000ms' }. The full payload fell back to an in-process volatile copy (papercusp://scratch-memory/f45510f8-…, expires 00:58:18Z, lost on restart). The payload was small: originalChars 8172. A spill write of about 8KB should not take more than 30s.

Impact: the write itself landed. I confirmed it with scorecards:get EI-25641616454606476: gradingAudit.state=passed, auditIssueId=EI-25642263855564483. But the emit call blocked for over 30s on the spill. And the result for a non-idempotent write was only readable from a volatile copy, so a caller with less care could repeat the emit. Earlier in the same session, code:run result-door spills succeeded. So this is intermittent and probably load-correlated. Cause unknown (unconfirmed): it could be filesystem or PG contention on the scratch store, or a serialized writer.

Related signal in the same minute: improvements:capture checkDuplicatesOnly returned dedupCoverage { lexical:'unavailable', semantic:'unavailable', degraded:true }, and the hook retrieval legs reported 'source query exceeded ~222-296ms budget'. That suggests general store latency at the time rather than a spill-specific fault. Not proven.

Repro hint: emit a scorecard of about 8KB via tools:invoke under fleet load, then check _projection.cursor.reason. Suggested fix direction: make the spill write bounded or async off the response path, and add a latency metric on result-door spill writes so stalls show up in a measurement.

admissionDeltaSweep.reason: Three differently worded current items identify the same 30-second spill-write timeout at a shared upstream persistence boundary, across distinct tool results and recovery behaviors.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
The shared response-spill persistence step is failing after tool results are produced. EI-25642413084997212 reports two exact-schema tools:find responses whose spill writes remain pending and return ETIMEDOUT after 30 seconds. EI-25643493925758323 identifies the same shared writer timeout across read/emit responses, with fallback to expiring scratch-memory cursors. EI-25643583618839257 records a 4,156-byte scorecards:get spill exceeding 30000ms; capability:read returns ENOENT until the write settles later. The common mechanism is unfinished durable spill persistence at the result-door deadline, leaving callers with unavailable or volatile recovery handles rather than reliable output. The repair boundary is the shared writer's completion, deadline and recovery lifecycle—not the individual discovery or scorecard handlers. The underlying I/O or scheduling trigger remains unconfirmed.

Shared-root-cause evidence: Three differently worded current items identify the same 30-second spill-write timeout at a shared upstream persistence boundary, across distinct tool results and recovery behaviors.

Contributing admitted work-items: EI-25642413084997212, EI-25643493925758323, EI-25643583618839257.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Found during grading-integrity audit EI-25683285827261064 of card EI-25682497216190136 (subject agent-run su-d70c727a-b61a-4db3-bbe1-ce888c65a9d5, 2026-10-10T21:01:22Z..21:41:30Z).

The text says one thing: rubric work-on-everything-stewardship-health rev47 (criteriaHash 2bf720c3…), criterion owner-report-truthfulness, has this method: 'FAIL when any report's COST line admits no measurement or any walled entry is only work-item ids. PASS when every report has a measured COST and every walled entry names an owner action.' Its model cites '2 of 2 reports had an unmeasured COST' as the witnessed FAILURE case.

The writer does another: woe.owner-report-truthfulness (rateGoalHolderBehavior in packages/operator-core/lib/goal-holder-behavior-metrics.ts, re-run at 2026-10-11T11:37:36.313Z) returns PASS for '2 report(s): COST cited the measured goal spend in 0, truthfully stated goal spend unmeasured in 2'. That is the exact pattern the rubric text calls FAIL. The writer policy (truthful send-time stamp) seems to come from closed bugs WI-10006542 and WI-10007037, but the rubric prose was never amended. This is [inferred] from titles; I have not read their diffs.

The platform also forbids grading per the text. Read-only scorecards:evaluate with the card's ratings, with this key swapped to unknown (attribution instrument, unknownReason instrument-unavailable or other, with nextEvidenceAction) or to fail (with disregard), is refused every time: 'A registered platform measurement contradicts the claimed rating', instrumentContract.verdictMismatches=['woe.owner-report-truthfulness']. So every WOE card carries a pass that the pinned rubric text calls a fail. The grader of EI-25682497216190136 disclosed the divergence in prose, but the rollup shows a bare pass.

Proposed fix (one of two): (a) amend the rubric to rev48 so the method matches the writer's truthful-unmeasured policy. If spend is platform-unmeasurable, an honest COST line should arguably rate unknown/not-satisfiable rather than pass. Then ratify it independently. Or (b) change the writer to follow the rev47 text. Whichever is chosen, add a parity test that pins the rubric method thresholds to rateGoalHolderBehavior's thresholds, so prose and writer cannot drift apart again. Unconfirmed: whether any other woe.* instrument has the same prose/writer drift.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
UNCONFIRMED ROOT CAUSE; the observations below are first-hand.

Observed 2026-10-13 ~01:08Z by the system:judge grading-integrity auditor (run 1791853511-judge) while auditing card EI-25824194280263964 (audit EI-25824691021530214).

1. The audited meta-acceptance card's prefer-structured-check evidence says: 'On current-build3170, the independent judge executes capability:git-evidence {op:readFileAtCommit,commitSha:57f7634a...,path:packages/operator-core/lib/search/chunks/registry.test.ts} ... tools:find on3170 confirms this judge-only instrument; old3070 catalog lacks it.'
2. In the judge session, tools:invoke {name:'capability:git-evidence'} returned unknown_tool. tools:find 'capability:git-evidence readFileAtCommit' found no such tool. A later error message reported the serving build as d740fc3802, and the scorecards:emit response flagged staleHost:true, deployedSha d740fc3802.
3. The typed fallback capability:git is denied to the system:judge principal (missing_capability). memory:search is also denied (missing_capability memory:read), although the judge persona and turn-start memory both point at memory recall.

IMPACT: commit-pinned test-file evidence, the core of meta-acceptance prefer-structured-check detector-adequacy claims, cannot be re-run by the designated auditor, so cards that rely on it cannot be fully audited. This will recur for every vetting card that cites git-evidence until judge sessions are routed to a build that carries the instrument.

CANDIDATE FIXES (unverified): route judge-scoped MCP sessions to a host whose build includes capability:git-evidence, or ship git-evidence to the green build. Then confirm with tools:find from a judge session.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
UNCONFIRMED CAUSE — the observation is filed; the mechanism is not proven.

What I saw: during the grading-integrity audit of scorecard EI-25828255998725711 (judge session su-628f4d8c, client papercusp-su via tools:invoke), two read-only code:run calls returned {error:'mcp_proxy_upstream_error', forwardingResult:'outcome_unknown', detail:'read ECONNRESET', attempts:1, windowMs:90000}. traceIds: 27cc7b31-c7d1-481a-9f1d-a9720b184a9f (~2026-10-13T02:10:49Z) and 0c98adaa-8afa-4744-be9d-03bf179b469c (~02:12:10Z). Each script made 23-24 scorecards:get reads plus one plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy call. An identical retry succeeded both times. Afterwards the responses carried _dataPlaneMayBeDegraded warnings. A testing:runs error at ~02:13Z said build d740fc3802 had 'started 25min ago'. The scorecards:emit response at 02:16:10Z reported gradedGeneration.hostStartedAt=2026-10-13T02:14:09Z and staleHost=true. So the serving host apparently restarted between 02:13 and 02:14:09. That restart came AFTER both resets, so a restart does not obviously explain them.

Why it matters: outcome_unknown on a code:run means the caller cannot tell whether nested writes happened, so every agent has to reason about idempotency on each reset. A read-only audit can safely retry; a writing script cannot.

Probe: query harness_shared.tool_invocations for coord_owner_id su-628f4d8c-87ea-4d57-a493-58504e273aa3, tool_name code:run, between 02:10 and 02:13Z, and read serving_host / serving_build_sha / duration. Correlate that with the :9071 proxy log for the two traceIds and the operator journal for that window. Check whether long-running code:run (~25 nested dispatches) is hitting an upstream socket or idle timeout.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body: Root cause is a telemetry/reader attribution mismatch, not a checkpoint restore failure. Green-checkpoint child env intentionally strips PAPERCUSP_WORKSPACE_ID, so gate observations default to workspace_id='default'; local Papercusp runs may write under papercusp-workspace. The watchdog previously read gate-pass-reuse without tenant or producer filtering, mixing unrelated local dirty-checkout rows into gate alarms. _claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-13 ~19:38-19:43Z on :3170 (serving_host port-3170, judge session su-9f12b151-c169-40e7-bb05-ddf85e0407a2). Root cause is NOT proven; the evidence below points at the kernel authority preflight/enforce step.

Evidence (harness_shared.tool_invocations, workspace papercusp-workspace):
- id 37777028 scorecards:emit: status ok, duration_ms 65265, output_size 283. metadata_json.kernel.preflight.serverAudit.authorityTimings.controlAnchorSql.totalMs = 19232; enforce controlAnchorSql.totalMs = 16419.
- id 37777029 tools:invoke (the wrapper around that emit): status ok, duration_ms 254812. preflight controlAnchorSql 37976ms, enforce controlAnchorSql 45379.6ms.
- Client: Claude Code aborted tools:invoke after 307s with no response or progress, so the caller never received the 283-byte result.
- No grading-integrity row was written for subject EI-25893268078685867. I checked with dev:pg_query over work_items, with a positive control returning EI-25816366956806744. The target stayed gradingAudit.state 'pending'. So the first emit was most likely refused, but its refusal code was lost because the reply never arrived. An identical retry at 19:42Z succeeded (audit EI-25894542982653930), so the refusal was probably transient. The cause of the first refusal is unknown.
- Same window: an improvements:capture checkDuplicatesOnly call timed out at 55s. capability:git-evidence readFileAtCommit calls returning file_not_found_at_commit took 15830ms and 5131ms, while successful reads of 32KB blobs took 9-2584ms. These are consistent with the same per-call authority-SQL latency (unconfirmed).

Impact: a write tool's outcome can be lost to the caller even though the server finished it. A grading auditor then cannot tell whether to retry or stop, which invites duplicate writes, or abandoned audits when the write did land. Lever to investigate: why controlAnchorSql (identityLaunchRecordSelection 'owner-workspace-fallback', advSessionId 42767) takes 16-45s per call. Also why tools:invoke runs preflight+enforce for both itself and the inner tool (double cost).

admissionIdentity.titleKey: title:55s card code criterion get inside nested one page per reads run scorecards slow timeout too

_claimSubjectBaseline.body: Observed 2026-10-13 ~21:16Z during grading-integrity audit of EI-25900285445623116 (build 78cd58273a, :3070). A code:run looping scorecards:get {issueId, criterionKey, evidenceOffset:0} over 6 criterion keys (each evidence <=1086 chars, complete in one page) failed with `request_timeout: nested tool "code:run" exceeded 55000ms via tools:invoke`. That implies more than 9s per small per-criterion read. The grading-integrity brief and card both require reading every criterion's evidence through this paged per-criterion door. Auditors therefore cannot batch it in code:run as the playbook recommends. They fall back to N parallel direct calls, and those then trip the aggregate output budget: 7 of 12 parallel calls spilled to scratch with 'aggregate-output-budget-exceeded', so each needed extra capability:read turns. Cause UNKNOWN / unconfirmed: possibly each criterionKey read recomputes the full card (currentness, evidenceBindingCurrentness, auditTarget) per call. The box also reported 'Perf budget breached (ambient)' at the time, so load correlation is possible; that is still a bug per the responsiveness design. Suggested fix: one call returning all criteria's complete evidence when it fits a size bound (e.g. criterionKeys:[...] or evidence:'all'), and/or cache the per-card currentness computation across criterion pages. Repro: code:run { script: for 6 keys await tools.scorecards.get({issueId:'EI-25900285445623116', criterionKey:k, evidenceOffset:0}) }.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body: Unconfirmed bug; root cause unknown. Observed 2026-10-14 ~07:41-07:42Z by judge su-c7612b38 during grading audit EI-25940224178375177. A code:run result was force-trimmed (originalChars 8012) and spilled to /home/marsh-office/.papercusp/scratch/papercusp-workspace/tools:invoke/f8ee1e98-82a5-46f2-b8ad-957ab88c63bf/result-door-1791963677161.md, which holds about 8 KB and 149 lines. Repro: run any code:run returning about 8 KB, then capability:read the spill with raw:true offset:1 limit:50.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Seen while auditing scorecard EI-26263239610205437 for grading integrity (audit EI-26264251939823099), on build 876c290c9b, 2026-10-17 ~21:30-21:39Z.

Symptom: code:run results whose originalChars were about 5.3K-13K came back with _projection.tier='trimmed', forced:true and returnedChars of roughly 2.4K-3.5K. Long strings were cut to about 2.5K characters, and a 10.6K rerunRecipe and an 18.8K criterion evidence string could not be returned. Examples: originalChars 6013 returned 2434; 6007 returned 2419; 10452 returned 2495; 13233 returned 2383. Every one needed a scratch-page cursor (capability:read with 3-4 KB base64 byte pages) or a re-run split into ~2K slices.

Cost: the audit took about 15 code:run calls instead of about 5. Each re-run re-fetched 7-13 scorecards:get pages server-side just to return a different slice.

Suspected cause (unconfirmed): 'forced:true' suggests the shared result-door budget is under concurrent pressure from the fleet of about 700 peers, not a fixed per-call cap. If so, this is load-correlated degradation. It needs a counter of forced trims by concurrent door load to confirm.

Related: plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy replay rows[0].ratings carries only {rating}, with no evidence text. An auditor therefore cannot byte-compare stored evidence against the replay and must re-run the plans:get-spec-evidence probe separately.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-17 22:28Z (su-8131472d, WI-6554700010016984). In ~/.papercusp-workspaces/clones/papercusp-public-site I ran `scripts/pc-heavy.sh -- npx vitest run` at 22:27Z. It failed: tests/harness.test.js flagged tests/site-nav.test.js. I edited tests/site-nav.test.js to fix it, then re-ran the identical command at 22:28:36Z. pc-heavy printed `[pc-heavy] coalesced: reusing a 39s-old identical run (same cwd+argv) instead of spawning another — see EI-18685262961418231` and returned the OLD result. Per-file durations were identical to the ms, and it still showed the failure the edit had fixed. PC_HEAVY_COALESCE=0 forces a fresh run. Impact: an agent re-running tests after an edit gets a pre-edit verdict that looks authoritative. A stale green is the dangerous case: it reports a fix as verified when it never ran. Suggested fix: never coalesce with a run that STARTED before the newest change to the tree it measures (e.g. key on cwd+argv plus a working-tree fingerprint), or coalesce only with a run still in flight, never with a finished one. Also make the 'coalesced' banner say 'result predates your edits' when files changed since that run started. Evidence: /tmp/site-full-run2.log (its head shows the coalesced banner), /tmp/site-full-run.log (the original run).

ⓘ Possible STALE RUNTIME, not an open defect: `scripts/pc-heavy.sh` (115 newer commits, tip `fa395f735cf940363aa5326140870b03c07de5b2`) have commits newer than the running build (`d740fc3802`) in `staging`. _claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-17 ~23:26Z as judge session system:judge/su-a95f6f42 reviewing WI-6554700010017007 (harness papercusp).

Repro:
1. work_items:get { id:'WI-6554700010017007', harness:'papercusp', threadLimit:10 } -> response had _projection.tier:'trimmed', forced:true, originalChars 8726, returnedChars 5945, omittedCount 20, omitted:[] (empty), omittedSamplesDropped:true. The result had NO threadWindow key, even though the caller asked for a thread window explicitly through threadLimit.
2. The same call with projection:{pick:['results[].threadWindow']} -> returned threadWindow with 7 posts (total:7), ~4.8KB, including thread-post 1189450, the post this review needed.

Expected: a field the caller explicitly asked for (threadLimit -> threadWindow) should either survive the forced trim or be named in _projection.omitted[] / given an inline '[omitted: …]' marker, as the other dropped fields are. Actual: it vanished. A caller reading result 1 can conclude 'this item has no thread posts', which is a false absence. That matters most for acceptance-bar amendment reviewers, whose whole task is to read a specific thread post.

Cause unknown (unconfirmed): possibly the bounded-payload shaper drops top-level per-row enrichments before it records them in omitted[] when omittedSamplesDropped is set. Workaround: projection pick on results[].threadWindow.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Found during the grading-integrity audit of spec-quality card EI-26276547297104261 (plan papercup-compact-tool-profile-2026-10-12, subject spec-set:plan-class-feature-ship:ef9273ea8f2aa0d562daf42e8a98a44a9d82521b911cbde30e0e2e08ad5db0ce:5094df89d45ee060, created 2026-10-18T00:54:28Z by su-0abdb075).

OBSERVED (hard evidence, read-only probes 2026-10-18 ~01:10-01:20Z, from a judge-scoped session):
1. plans:evaluate-spec-quality { slug:'papercup-compact-tool-profile-2026-10-12', harness:'papercusp', classRef:'plan-class-feature-ship', expectedSpecSetHash:'ef9273ea…' } returns specSetHash ef9273ea…, verdict pass, and per-criterion evidence that is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the card for all 8 keys. details has only {uncoveredPlanItemIds, invalidExemptionSpecIds, draftSpecIds}.
2. The same call with replaySnapshot is REFUSED by the serving schema: "args.replaySnapshot is not accepted by the current tool schema", accepts [classRef, expectedSpecSetHash, harness, slug].
3. The same plan's earlier card EI-26269305220067153 (2026-10-17T22:59Z, prior hash be4375d3…, author su-09924a8c) has much richer evidence from the same verb family:
   - atomic-observable-behavior: "31 of 50 active behavioral clause(s) evaluated; 19 active sourceBar-pinned BAR projection(s) excluded … details.atomicityClauseDiagnostics … Detector controls: two compound counterexamples rejected and two single-outcome controls accepted".
   - implementation-independence: "Detector coverage: implementation filenames/symbols, internal route literals, … Inspected 50 … details.implementationIndependenceDetectorControls".
   - a "Historical replay (same rated snapshot)" probe carrying replaySnapshot {planContentHash, clausesAsOf}.
   The new card lacks all of these: its atomic evidence reads "41 behavioral clause(s) are structurally atomic" (get-specs shows 41 active clauses, 4 of them sourceBar-pinned, so sourceBar projections are evidently NOT excluded/reported as spec-quality rev 6 atomic-observable-behavior.method requires), and its implementation-independence evidence is only "No active clause is coupled to an obvious implementation filename or construct" (no detector coverage/controls).
4. EI-26056033667551378 records a running build whose evaluate-spec-quality accepted "harness, slug, expectedSpecSetHash, classRef, replaySn…", so at least two builds with different evaluator surfaces are serving this verb.

CONSEQUENCE: spec-quality cards emitted via the thin build (a) omit the evaluated/excluded population the rubric method requires, (b) give prohibition passes with no instrument-sensitivity statement (grading-integrity base-rate-check rev 9 → fail), and (c) carry no historical-replay probe, so they stop being re-runnable after the next clause revision. EI-26276547297104261's grading-integrity audit fails base-rate-check for this reason.

HYPOTHESIS (UNPROVEN, [inferred]): the 00:54Z card and my calls were served by an older build (e.g. :3070 green main, reportedly ~374h since last green) while the 22:59Z card came from a newer build (:3170 staging / current tree). Could not confirm: judge principal lacks intel:read for dev:pg_query on harness_shared.tool_invocations. Probe to confirm: SELECT invoked_at, coord_owner_id, serving_host, serving_build_sha FROM harness_shared.tool_invocations WHERE workspace_id='papercusp-workspace' AND tool_name='plans:evaluate-spec-quality' AND coord_owner_id IN ('su-09924a8c-5be3-475c-8c3f-7b1d2074c9ce','su-0abdb075-3e8f-4a3d-856a-199f47c1c3ce') AND invoked_at BETWEEN '2026-10-17T22:50Z' AND '2026-10-18T01:00Z'.

FIX DIRECTION: (1) find which serving build lacks the replaySnapshot/diagnostics evaluator and get it current; (2) make scorecards:emit for rubricRef 'spec-quality' refuse, or flag, evaluator evidence that has no population-coverage/detector-controls section; (3) re-grade spec set ef9273ea… on a current build and re-audit.

admissionIdentity.titleKey: title:acceptance amendment applied approval approved bar barhash binds can check differ from lineage method only outside preview rev reviewer the

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
UNCONFIRMED CAUSE; the observation itself is hard evidence.

Subject: acceptance-detached-hook-home-resolution-2026-10-18, applied as rev 2 (plan D-001 'Amendment-Id: acceptance-detached-hook-home-resolution-rev2-apply-1191659').

Observed:
- Outside-lineage approver thread-post:1191637 (su-8a88db09, 11:32:58Z) approved R-2 prior 9fc574b5 -> next 92b42fdc. It explicitly verified: "Check drops artifact-url-delivery-guard.test.ts, correct because the ledger clause left this bar; installed-hooks-parity.test.ts remains."
- Reviewer thread-post:1191642 (su-81e9a973, 11:49:24Z) re-confirmed that R-2 is "byte-identical to preview 1191634 in model, falsifier, method, check".
- Judge thread-post:1191659 (12:09:27Z) approved 1191654 (R-2 -> 92b42fdc, R-3 -> 2fb5dba5).
- LIVE rev 2 (rubrics:get detail:'full', updatedAt 12:14:50.459Z) has r-2 barHash 92b42fdc (matches), BUT r-2 check.files = [installed-hooks-parity.test.ts, artifact-url-delivery-guard.test.ts] and method = '... artifact-url-delivery-guard.test.ts for environment-scoped ledger selection ...'. That is exactly the coupling the reviewers approved as REMOVED, and r-2's check is now a superset of r-3's check, so the bars co-rate.

Hypothesis (unproven): method/check are not barHash material (1191637: 'R-1 is method-only so no hash moves'; 1191642: 'the durable-write scope survives only in the bound case, which is not hash material'). So the amendment approval cannot detect a divergence between the approved preview's non-hashed fields and what is applied.

Alternative hypothesis: the 1191654 preview body itself carried the two-file check, and the earlier reviewers' 'byte-identical' statements referred to 1191634 only.

Distinguishing probe: diff the patch JSON in the amendment-review consult body for 1191654 against live rev 2 r-2 check/method.

Correct state: an approval should bind a hash over every gradeable field (model, bar, method, driftMarkers, check), or the apply step should refuse when non-hashed fields differ from the approved preview.

Found during the grading-integrity audit of EI-26501172812591817 (audit EI-26501685154215801).

On 2026-10-20 ~13:06Z, a judge was launched by system:acceptance-bar-amendment-review to review the R-1 amendment of acceptance-bug-triage (WI-6554700010018096, thread-post:1191706). admissionIdentity.titleKey: title:005 and brief dark fired idle judge kickoff mcp resumed session watchdog with

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
UNCONFIRMED CAUSE. Evidence (2026-10-20, session su-aeb7ecaf-3c97-4703-be4f-3eb05181ff63, run id 1792501548-judge, role judge):
- The conversation's ONLY user turn is a watchdog-origin carry: 'MCP transport auto-recovery (mcp-dark-watchdog P-005): headless session ... had no Papercusp MCP call for ~0m. Its psu host resumed this same conversation with a watchdog-tagged carry. Re-read the active work-item and loop checkpoints, then continue.' The turn-provenance stamp says VERIFIED AGENT-ORIGIN (watchdog).
- No judge kickoff brief is present in the conversation: no subject plan/rubric/scorecard/work-item. FEATURE_ID and TRIGGER env vars are empty.
- work_items:list { assignee:'self', notTerminal:true } returns [] (nothing held).
- sessions:read { session:'self' } is refused for role judge (role_not_allowed), so a judge cannot recover a lost brief from its own transcript.
- MCP calls through mcp__papercusp__tools_invoke succeed, so the transport was not dark when the watchdog fired. The message reports '~0m' since the last MCP call, which is below any plausible dark threshold. That looks like a false alarm.
Two suspected defects: (1) the watchdog fires on a session with zero idle time and/or a judge that never made an MCP call; (2) the resume carry drops the original kickoff brief, or the session started with no brief at all. Either way, the judge cannot act, and per persona it stops without grading. Suggested fix: the watchdog should skip sessions under its idle threshold, and the carry should re-inject the original kickoff (or refuse to resume a role-scoped session whose kickoff is missing).

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-21 08:51-09:03Z, session su-2ea0f358-8c3f-41ce-bfed-bb6379290c4c (role judge), grading-integrity audit of scorecard EI-26577353033210593 (audit card EI-26579054352729640).

What happened: the papercusp MCP transport dropped mid-audit. The mcp-dark-watchdog (P-005) resumed the session from a deterministic carry document built 2026-10-21T08:51:08Z. That carry document has no copy of the kickoff brief (the first user turn naming the subject, the lease key/reservedAt, the emit tool and the expected output). It holds only the session's own last verbatim turns. The lease key and reservedAt survived only because the pre-drop turn happened to quote them in prose.

The judge role persona says: "If the brief is missing ... do NOT infer a mission and do NOT grade." The documented recovery is sessions:search / sessions:read { session:'self' }, but for this principal it is refused:
- tools:invoke sessions:search -> role_not_allowed: Role "judge" cannot call tool "sessions:search" (allowed: scoper, architect, worker, validator, reviewer, debugger, operator, mug, documenter, curator, papercup, kettle, release-fixer)
- memory:get -> missing_capability memory:read
- search:fulltext -> missing_capability search:read
- capability:bash -> missing_capability capability:bash

So a resumed judge must either stop, or reconstruct the brief from the target card plus the scorecards:emit schema. I did the latter: gradingAuditReservation key/reservedAt read off the card's gradingAudit.dispatchReservation. It worked here only because the emit schema documents the lease field.

Expected (either fix closes it): (a) the carry document for a mission-launched role (judge / any kickoff-brief role) re-injects the kickoff brief verbatim; or (b) the judge role may read its OWN transcript (sessions:read/search with session:'self' only, no cross-session reads), which keeps least privilege.

Cause not proven: I could not read the carry-document builder (no bash/grep), so whether the builder deliberately omits the first turn or simply ages it out of the tail is unknown.

MEASURED 2026-10-21 (su-2b61b6ab, audit WI-6554700010019485):
- bg-host journal: "[scheduled-registry] ephemeral:rt_papercusp_acceptance_grading_sweep long tick finished after 2557003ms (42 fire(s) skipped while it ran, interval 60000ms)" at 18:49:08Z.
- the bg-host restarted ~18:56Z; the new tick has been "still running" since (log lines at 120 s, 253 s, 982 s, 1,944 s). schedule:inventory (bg-host:3271) shows fires=0, running=true, armedAt 18:56:35Z.
- routines row rt_papercusp_acceptance_grading_sweep: active, last_fired_at 18:49:08Z.

EFFECT: a 60 s sweep that re-dispatches graders and mints escalations effectively runs once per ~40 min, and a bg-host restart mid-tick discards the whole pass. The registry logs "still running" but nothing alarms or bounds the tick, so a hung tick stops the cadence silently until the next restart.

ROOT CAUSE: NOT established; which await inside the action (harness/routines/acceptance-grading-sweep-action.ts and acceptance-grading-sweep-run.ts) takes the time was not measured. Related: EI-26281797513320642 (hypothesis about lastFiredAt not advancing).

FIX DIRECTION: keep the scan on the ephemeral timer but cap its wall time, and run each per-plan dispatch as a DBOS workflow keyed by plan + gradeable-since, so the tick finishes in seconds and dispatches survive restarts. Add an alarm when a managed tick holds its guard past N intervals.

report.message: [db-call-deadline @ d740fc3802] "coord:emit.sendMessage" did not resolve within 45000ms (waited 45000ms). No acquire measurements were available for this call, so both causes are still open. Two causes present identically at this point — (a) the pool's resolved endpoint is unreachable and postgres.js is silently retrying its INITIAL connect forever without rejecting (WI-7097), or (b) the CLIENT pool's acquire queue is saturated while the server is perfectly healthy. Server capacity does NOT decide (b), so dev:service_health / pg_stat_activity looking fine is not evidence against it — check this process's own pcusp:<pool>:p<pid> rows and PAPERCUSP_DB_POOL_MAX before the endpoint (WI-7097).

_claimSubjectBaseline.body: Avi reports seeing literal citation syntax in Codex chats: U+E200 cite U+E202 turn613222view0 U+E201. Official OpenAI citation-formatting documentation identifies these delimiters and says applications must parse source IDs to render links or remove raw markers. Current web tool instructions in this Codex session explicitly require ordinary Markdown links and prohibit exposing internal turn reference IDs. Confirmed symptom from owner example; exact originating message, client renderer and source metadata availability have not been inspected. Suspected causes to distinguish: model uses unsupported citation markup despite tool format instructions vs client/integration fails to render a supported citation/loses annotation context. Suggested durable direction: enforce host-compatible Markdown source links at output boundary when citations can be resolved, preserve unresolved citation evidence, and add regression coverage for literal citation tokens. Do not infer that a source was actually retrieved merely from a marker. No product source change made for this explanation.

report.message: Scratch byte page requested by absolute file_path returned only a build notice, while the same page by URI returned base64 bytes.

directEvidence.actual: The file_path read yielded only an informational build-provenance text block with no byte-page fields; the URI read returned a valid base64 page.
directEvidence.expected: A byte_offset+byte_limit read from the returned scratch file_path yields byte_length, total_bytes, data, eof, and next_cursor fields, as the same read by papercusp://scratch URI does.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body: Suspected API-contract defect. For a scratch spill, capability:read with the returned absolute file_path plus byte_offset/byte_limit returned only the build-provenance notice and no data/eof/cursor fields. Repeating the same byte page with the documented papercusp://scratch URI returned byte_length, base64 data, and eof=false. Line query/view_lines by file_path worked. The schema advertises file_path|uri for the read surface; investigate why byte paging behaves differently for the file_path alias.

terminalCompletionEvidence.summary: Prevented recipient-side explicit asks from being counted as loose replies that erase older unanswered asks. Applied the same eligibility rule to the mirrored sender-side query.
terminalCompletionEvidence.testsRun: npm run test:file -- packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/coordination/unanswered-directed.integration.test.ts
terminalCompletionEvidence.testResult: PASS after fix: 36 tests passed. The added real-Postgres regression failed before the fix with undefined instead of 3 incoming asks.
terminalCompletionEvidence.verifiedHow: The maintained integration fixture exercised both fetchUnansweredDirected (used by coord:inbox unanswered_only) and fetchOpenAsks. Before the SQL change, independent outgoing ack/answer/action asks cleared all three incoming asks; after the change both views retained all three, and the full file passed.

rootCauseVerification.hypothesis: The loose-reply CTE counted any later unthreaded message from the recipient to the asker, including a new message with expects ack, answer, or action. That falsely satisfied older asks and made unanswered_only return zero.
rootCauseVerification.testResult: Before the fix the new assertion failed: fetchUnansweredDirected returned no map entry instead of count 3. After the mirrored SQL filters, both query views returned count 3; all 36 integration tests passed.
rootCauseVerification.testProcedure: Run `npm run test:file -- packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/coordination/unanswered-directed.integration.test.ts`; compare the pre-fix regression failure with the post-fix full-file pass.
rootCauseVerification.actualObservation: The pre-fix fixture returned undefined instead of the expected count 3. The post-fix run retained all three incoming ask ids in both query surfaces and passed 36/36 tests.
rootCauseVerification.distinguishingTest: In the real-Postgres integration fixture, send three asks from leader to member. After each, have the member send a separate unthreaded ack, answer, or action request back. Assert both unanswered-query views retain all three incoming asks.
rootCauseVerification.alternativeHypothesis: The original ask had already been answered or its sender was positively ended, so filtering it was correct.

predictedObservations.hypothesis: Before the fix, explicit outgoing asks are counted as loose replies and the incoming ask count drops to zero; after the fix, incoming asks remain open.
predictedObservations.alternativeHypothesis: Because the fixture has no actual answer and no ended-sender verdict, incoming asks remain open both before and after the change.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed an active `work-item-admission-promoter` routine health error: `routine2.now.getTime is not a function` in the papercusp install and papercusp-pr-drill install. The papercusp row was active, lastFiredAt 2026-10-25T22:11:08.157Z, nextFireAt 2026-10-25T22:30:00.000Z (past at read), with health.last_error set to that TypeError.

Likely source: `work-item-admission-promoter-action.ts` types `OrdinaryRoutine.now` as `Date`, selects `now() AS now` through getOrgPg(), then calls `routine.now.getTime()` in `claimOrdinarySlot` (line 71). `reconcile-loop-routines.ts` documents that getOrgPg() uses prepare:false and returns timestamptz as raw strings. The live error matches this Date/string mismatch; the routine row's actual runtime `now` value was not directly observed, so treat the source attribution as likely pending a focused reproduction.

Potential impact: EI-25812519922184353 has admissionReview pending since 2026-10-12, retryOwner system:work-item-admission-promoter, lastRetryAt 2026-10-16, and an admissionHold that cites review-gated twin EI-24743561522616011. The hold's causal link to the current routine failure is not proven. EI-24743561522616011 remains open and unassigned.

Suggested durable fix: normalize the timestamptz value before Date operations (or use a shared PG timestamp coercion helper) and add a maintained regression where the promoter query returns a string-typed timestamptz.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-26, papercusp, owner su-7eaf5 (WI-10006055). Verify run 1fxzuva (attempt 0c64e7b7) judged repairHead 616efbae. Mid-run an admission moved repairHead to 327e4d1d, the round was recorded as superseded, and the unit exited 0 at 10:25:14Z. The qualification watchdog then emitted 'green-checkpoint qualification LOST ... runner proved dead without a terminal verdict; an ordinary guarded retry was requested' (10:27Z); the runner was NOT dead, see the systemd terminal service_result=success. The guarded retry (run dd75c734) was prepared for 616efbae and crashed in preflight: 'Error: prepared selection queue authority changed after commit at beginPreparedCheckpointPreflight (apps/operator/lib/release/green-checkpoint.ts:19307) at async beginCheckpoint (:26608)'. It emitted green-checkpoint:inconclusive reason=error. A manual release:checkpoint-run at 10:34Z correctly selected 327e4d1d.
Two defects: (1) a retry whose prepared queue authority went stale should re-resolve the queue's current repairHead (or retire cleanly with a typed 'superseded-before-start' outcome), not throw a crash-class inconclusive; (2) the qualification watchdog classifies a superseded-verdict clean exit as a dead runner.
Fix: in beginPreparedCheckpointPreflight, on an authority mismatch re-prepare against the fresh queue row when phase/candidate are unchanged and only repairHead advanced. Teach the qualification-loss detector that a terminal exit 0 with a FROZEN_REPAIR_VERDICT_SUPERSEDED round is a terminal outcome. Tests: retry after a mid-run admission selects the new head; superseded clean exit is not reported as LOST.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-27 02:10Z (su-ad3061a6, owner directive #2375 agent recovery).

Evidence:
- `harness_shared.task_ledger` GROUP BY workspace_id,state (updated_at > now()-3d): papercusp-workspace rows are reconciled continuously (running/exited/ended_unobserved updated to 02:10Z). workspace_id='default' has 14 rows in state='running' whose newest last_seen_at is 2026-10-26 04:12Z and oldest 2026-10-24 02:18Z — never touched since insertion.
- Example: task 0mvmvat7w12xrl4v10z (class agent-session, title 'headless member: successor · su-16e3554c-…', fleet nonp2p-bug-drain-luna-max-0930, scope pc-0mvmvat7w12xrl4v10z--successor-su-16e3554c-….scope). `processes:kill { taskId }` returns already_gone (systemd no longer knows the scope), yet the row still reads running / ended_at NULL / last_seen_at 2026-10-24 20:44:51Z.

Mechanism (from source, unverified beyond reading): `task-reconcile` system action → `reconcileTick({ workspaceId: deps.workspaceId })` → `listLiveTasks(workspaceId)` → `listTasks({ workspaceId, states:['pending','running'] })` (packages/operator-core/lib/task-manager/store.ts:1194, reconcile-tick.ts:192). The routine runs per install with ctx.workspaceId='papercusp-workspace', so rows written under workspace_id='default' are outside every reconcile population. cgroups are host-global, so the host's reconciler should own every row on this host regardless of workspace tag.

Impact: a never-terminal 'running' row is false liveness evidence. `capability:launch-agent { successor }` for su-16e3554c refused 'predecessor liveness is live/draining; positive terminal evidence is required' while the process was gone; that agent stayed wedged on stale-artifact (29 authorization_denied, 0 ok, last 01:54Z).

Proposed fix: (1) reconcile ALL workspaces' pending/running rows whose scope_unit/cgroup is on this host (or explicitly include 'default'); (2) find the writer that records workspace_id='default' for headless fleet-member launches (managedSpawn/enroll called without an active workspace — 10-24 headless member successor launches) and pass the real workspace; (3) killTask: when a live-owned row's scope resolves already_gone, record the terminal transition (ended_unobserved, reason scope-collected) instead of returning without updating the ledger. Recurrence guard: a reconcile-tick test that seeds a running row under a different workspace_id with a collected scope and asserts it is transitioned.

Related (distinct symptom, same subsystem): EI-26986308927850569 / EI-26993855168505100 / EI-26991528350067840 (rt_papercusp_task_reconcile 'hung' alarms).

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-27 on consult conv-mvq2vlgs-0000-eebfb91af52c405a8ae7d3b9c53ed149 (decision-review for EI-25927909729992864).

Timeline (all UTC, from conversations:get payloadTier:'full' + my own launch stamp):
- 03:02:39.334 reviewer 1 (su-2a8dbdd0) posts answer 1207631 → per D-005 the cascade ADVANCES and launches reviewer 2/2.
- ~03:02:59 reviewer 2 (this session, su-ec58d1ae) boots on a ported codex transcript (session-port 7946addc-68e4-4209-af56-48d392f3551c, fidelity: full — a full context carry).
- 03:03:11.213 reviewer 1 posts close 1207633 → consult.state = closed_answered.
- 03:05 reviewer 2 finishes reading the thread + grounding evidence and calls consult:reply { kind:'answer', stance:{position:'support'} } → refused: {"error":"consult_not_open","state":"closed_answered"}.

Net: an entire reviewer session launch (full-fidelity transcript port + ~15 tool calls of evidence reading) produced nothing deliverable, and the launch brief told reviewer 2 it was 'launched to answer ONE question' with no indication the thread could already be terminal.

Three plausible fixes (any one suffices; first is cheapest):
1. consult:close (and any terminal transition) should CANCEL an in-flight reviewer dispatch for that conversation if that reviewer has not yet posted — the launch is attributable (dispatch.recent walks), so the close handler can mark it cancelled and the wake-executor can skip/abort the boot.
2. The reviewer launch brief / first wake should re-check consult.state before spending the transcript port; if state is terminal, deliver a one-line 'already closed — stand down' instead of the full answer brief (saves the boot cost even when fix 1 misses the race).
3. When a reviewer's reply is immediately followed by its own close (same author, < N seconds), do not advance the cascade on the reply — treat reply+close as one atomic 'answer and settle' and never launch the next reviewer. (D-005 'reply advances' is correct when the replier does NOT close.)

Also worth noting: consult:reply on a closed thread returns a bare consult_not_open with no pointer to the accepted answer; a hint naming accepted_post_id would let a stranded reviewer confirm concurrence cheaply instead of re-reading.

Evidence: conversations:get conv-mvq2vlgs-0000-eebfb91af52c405a8ae7d3b9c53ed149 (consult.state, closed_at, posts 1207631/1207633 timestamps); the refused consult:reply invocation by su-ec58d1ae-58c7-4c7a-88ce-8a479bb0f29c at ~03:05Z in harness_shared.tool_invocations. Related but distinct: EI-27099846407216760 (duplicate consult minted by idempotent park replay) — that one spends a THIRD reviewer on the orphan; this one spends reviewer 2 on the live thread.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body: Observed 2026-10-27 on gate item WI-10006055: su-a763c3ee wrote no-rerun / no-cancel / no-repair-queue-mutation walls into its own carry notes (seen from ~18:11Z 10-26; observations EI-27072876646052633 / EI-27072820099514427 cite a live gate producer). Root cause class (measured on EI-27114233692780034): Postgres jsonb stores object keys ordered by length then bytes, so JSON.stringify(readBack) !== JSON.stringify(inMemory) for logically equal objects. admissionIdentity.titleKey: title:actively alarm fire flaps git infra intervals liveness local missed progressing recover sweep sync while

_claimSubjectBaseline.body: Observed 2026-10-27 15:12-15:15Z (su-2fde89b1), papercusp install. The coord stream showed '[infra-liveness] git-sync on papercusp has missed 4 consecutive scheduler intervals: nothing written there is being committed', then 'infra-liveness RECOVERED (git-sync-missed-intervals:papercusp)', then the same alarm and RECOVERED again within ~3 minutes. During that window, routines:list { name:'git-sync', installSlug:'papercusp' } showed health.git_sync_activity active=true, phase 'local-sync', started_at 15:03:48Z, updated_at 15:11:08Z, with a live git command (rev-parse in libs/test-config) and owner pid 1285287. So a sweep was progressing, just slowly (host load ~90). The alarm text asserts 'nothing written there is being committed', which was not shown at that moment. Suspected cause (unconfirmed): the detector counts scheduler intervals whose fires were skipped because a long sweep holds the per-slug lock, without consulting git_sync_activity liveness or updated_at progress, and a fire that briefly completes clears it. Plausible fix: when git_sync_activity.active is true and updated_at is fresh, report 'sweep slow (N min in <phase>)' instead of 'missed intervals / nothing committed', and add hysteresis so recover-then-refire within a few minutes does not page twice. Also note: the last_error at the time was an unrelated github-bridge divergence string, which made the alarm harder to read.

admissionIdentity.titleKey: title:baseline discarded guard identities longer measurements present records reports same scan seed that the tree

_claimSubjectBaseline.body: Unconfirmed cause; measured 2026-10-27 ~16:58Z by su-96b7fe62 (WI-10006055). In papercusp-desktop: `python3 bin/lib/scan-discarded-measurements.py --seed-baseline bin/lib <rh-extract>/bin/lib` wrote 37 identities including b9-attestation.sh::*, fed-reap.sh::*, membership-churn.sh::* (bin/lib/scenarios/). Immediately after, `--guard` (default root = bin/lib, and also with an explicit `bin/lib` root) reported those 9 as 'baseline entry no longer present — prune it' with 28 candidates. Yet scanning the file directly (`scan-discarded-measurements.py bin/lib/scenarios/b9-attestation.sh`) prints two hits ([measurement] reasons_before, [lookup] ws). So the guard's population and the seed/report population differ for the same files: either guard mode filters some hit kinds/paths that seed mode keeps, or identity is computed differently. Effect: every re-seed produces a baseline the guard immediately calls stale, which trains reviewers to ignore its stale list. Fix: make --seed-baseline and --guard compute `found` and `_identity` through one code path, and add a self-test that seed-then-guard on the same tree reports 0 stale.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed by su-f4c37369 (fleet frozen-burndown member, psu Claude, warm loop every 900s) on 2026-10-27 ~17:56-18:20Z.

Evidence:
1. coord:inbox: '[await-event] coord:inbox-wake:su-f4c37369-… fired — delivered to your coord inbox (delivery remained parked and exhausted 8 attempts: psu-host pending-delivery-id: delivery accepted before turn-start proof; retry remains durable)'.
2. loop:status at 18:19Z: active:true, nextFireAt 18:29:48Z, rewake.rewakeGuaranteed:false reason 'last-fire-no-loop-turn'; loop:checkpoint continuation lastDeliveryOutcome 'loop-delivered-wake-no-loop-turn'.
3. The predecessor session had already re-armed the same loop (loop:arm upsert) at ~18:02Z after seeing nextFireAt:null + last delivery stuck at 'queued', then self-compacted (carry-respawn). The verdict still reports last-fire-no-loop-turn after the respawn, and the continuation gate tells the agent that ending the turn would SILENTLY HALT the session.

Suspected (unconfirmed) mechanism [inferred]: a loop fire / inbox wake that lands while the session is mid-turn or mid carry-respawn is accepted by psu-host but never produces a turn-start proof, and the respawned successor does not inherit or re-trigger it. So every fire that overlaps a busy turn or a respawn strands the loop's guarantee.

What should have caught it: the loop engine's delivery-to-turn watchdog (it reports the state but does not re-deliver after the respawn), and psu-host's pending-delivery retry (8 attempts exhausted without a turn).

No specific fix identified yet. Probe: loop:status { } for owner su-f4c37369-6459-436f-a9f5-3f83e4a5007b; events:status for the coord:inbox-wake await; psu-host pending-delivery log for that delivery id.

admissionIdentity.titleKey: title:15s browser fixture flakes fork integration out ready real session startup test timed timeout tsx worker

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Evidence (2026-10-27, head d47a64ee2f, shared tree): `npm run test:file -- packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/capability/browser-session.integration.test.ts` failed 1 test ('managed browser process enrollment and loss (real PG/Chromium) cleans real Chromium, its directory and ledger after owner worker SIGKILL') with `Error: real browser worker startup timed out` at browser-session.integration.test.ts:121. The immediate rerun passed both tests (INTEG_RC=0). Logs: .papercusp/scratch/burndown/fix2/integ.log (fail) and integ2.log (pass).

The failing wait is `start()`: it forks `__fixtures__/browser-owner-worker.mts` with `--import tsx` and waits a hard-coded 15_000 ms for the child's `fixture:ready` IPC message. That window has to cover a cold tsx transform of the worker's whole import graph plus a real PG connection. Nothing in this run separated those two costs, so which one went past 15s is UNMEASURED.

Proposed fix (unverified): timestamp the child's phases (tsx-loaded / db-connected / ready) on the fixture:ready path, and include them in the timeout error so the next failure says where the time went. Then either size the timeout from the measurement, or have the worker post an early `fixture:booting` heartbeat and start the 15s window from that message instead of from fork. Related: browser-owner.test.ts forks the same fixture and passed 5/5 in the same session. Found while verifying WI-6554700010030420 (browser-session.ts screenshot frame-wait fix). The timeout fires before any screenshot call, so it is not on that change's code path.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-27 (su-fc263bb4, papercusp install). The git-sync activity row showed one fire (started_at 18:59:09Z, phase local-sync) running until about 19:19Z. During that fire it ran `git status` in papercusp-desktop for 80s+ and then pushed that submodule. Its commit 5e6605dc3b (19:19:26Z) contained only test-config and the papercusp-desktop gitlink. The fire's last_content_errors still list push-channel.ts, task-brief.ts and task-brief.test.ts as quarantined importers of push-toolset.ts, 'held by su-fc263bb4 — turn-scoped hold: edited during its editor's current turn'. That editor's turns ended at about 19:06Z and again at about 19:20Z. No commit landed between 18:44Z and 19:19Z: freshness reported 9 missed intervals and the scheduler was 'stalled_behind_in_flight_fire'. Meanwhile the infra-liveness condition git-sync-missed-intervals:papercusp kept broadcasting RECOVERED while freshness still said degraded.

Suspected (unconfirmed): the turn-scoped hold set is evaluated once near the start of a fire and not re-checked at commit time, so a slow fire commits against a stale hold list. Separately, one fire spending 20 minutes in local-sync (a submodule `git status` taking 80s+) blocks every agent's commits for that whole period. The repeated RECOVERED broadcasts while freshness says degraded look like a false recovery signal.

Evidence: routines:list { name:'git-sync', installSlug:'papercusp' } health.git_sync_activity / git_sync_freshness / last_content_errors, read at 19:12Z, 19:15Z and 19:20Z; `git log` shows d47a64ee2f at 18:44:11Z, then 5e6605dc3b at 19:19:26Z.

Proposed fix: re-check turn-scoped holds right before staging each repo's commit, not once per fire. Bound how long the local-sync phase may run per submodule. Make the infra-liveness RECOVERED broadcast agree with git_sync_freshness.status.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-27, unconfirmed cause.

Run: testing:run on packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/docs/_guidance-adapter.live.test.ts hit the 25s foreground cap and started detached recovery run 3097eae4-4345-46c9-a6da-0560bb1acbcd (taskId 0mvr2wdu9yredme18y0, startedAt 19:28:39Z).

Evidence that the run had its verdict:
- vitest's --outputFile JSON report /tmp/pcv/papercusp-testing-run-detached-0d349771-7cd6-4e45-b043-634d7f954558.json exists: numPassedTests 3, numFailedTests 0.
- testing:runs shows a pass row for that file at 19:30:32.695Z-19:30:33.246Z (551ms, commit 8be3c30f).

And yet: testing:run-status { runId:'3097eae4-…' } still returned status:'running', exitCode:null, finishedAt:null, output:'' at about 19:34Z, at least 3.5 minutes after the report was written. Two sibling detached runs started the same minute, for feed-contract.test.ts and browser-owner.test.ts, finalized normally in about 40-45s with status pass.

Why it matters: a caller polling run-status sees 'no verdict yet' and keeps polling, or blocks a close, even though the verdict exists on disk and in the ledger.

Cause unknown. Two candidates: (a) the vitest child hangs at exit after reporting, perhaps an open handle in a .live test; :3070 restarted around 19:28Z mid-run; (b) the detached bookkeeping missed the child's exit. A distinguishing check: is the child PID for taskId 0mvr2wdu9yredme18y0 still alive (processes:list)?

Suggested fix direction: when the outputFile report exists, run-status should surface a distinct state such as 'reported, process not exited' that carries the report's counts, and track a teardown hang as a separate signal, so a written verdict is never shown as 'running' with empty output.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body: Evidence (cold loop wake #4, su-14d44480, 2026-10-27 ~19:47Z): my loop carry-note wrote my held item as the short form 'WI-422' (meaning WI-6554700010030422, state=wip, assignee me). The cold-wake/carry builder annotated each line with '⚠ LIVE: WI-422 status=passed' and emitted a '⚠⚠ STALE-NOTE CONTRADICTION ... TERMINAL ... Do NOT follow any instruction to complete/verify/close/work on it'. It resolved 'WI-422' to an UNRELATED item: '[chunk/passed] IG test-hardening #7: launch.ts hot-reload ...'. The same happened in the prior carry, where 'WI-393' resolved to an unrelated '[task/done] Refactor inference gateway ...'. An agent trusting the banner would abandon live, held work. Proposed fix: in the carry-note citation resolver, (a) never resolve a short WI-NNN when the author's held items include a long id whose suffix matches (…0030422 ends in 422), or prefer the held/claimed item; (b) when a short id is ambiguous across the workspace, render 'AMBIGUOUS short id' instead of asserting TERMINAL; (c) add a regression test with a held long id plus an unrelated short-id row. Also an authoring-side mitigation: loop:checkpoint lint could warn when a note abbreviates a held long id to its suffix.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-27 22:57Z closing WI-6554700010030445 (su-f6ff509d). completion.deferred was the string "none". The close returned requirementShortfallWarning: "this close DECLARES deferred work but supplies no verification.requirementDisposition".

Mechanism (read from the writer, not inferred): packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/work_items/complete.ts:4952 computes `declaresDeferredWork: Boolean(it.completion.deferred?.some((d) => d.trim()))`, so any non-empty string counts as a deferral, including the conventional no-deferral sentinels "none", "n/a", "-". requirementShortfall is also one of the conditions at :5031 next to fabricatedPaths/untouchedPaths, so it looks able to hold completionAuthority at 'proposed' [inferred from the condition list; not traced further].

Why it matters: the warning is a false alarm (a close with no deferral is told it under-delivered), and if :5031 does gate authority, a close that wrote "none" may never settle to 'committed' even after its files commit.

Proposed fix: normalise deferred entries before the check, dropping a case-insensitive sentinel set (none, n/a, na, -, nothing, nothing deferred) in the same place completion.deferred is coerced to string[]. Reuse that normaliser for every reader of completion.deferred (completionTextParts, the residue scan near :2776/:2968) so they agree. Test: a close with deferred:"none" raises no requirementShortfallWarning; deferred:"X is left" still does.

Workaround: omit `deferred` entirely when nothing was deferred.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body: Observed 2026-10-28 ~02:12Z (su-76dc3403, owner directive #2536). Resumed 14 ended su agents with capability:launch-agent { agent:'claude', resume:{ agentId }, fork:false, brief, idempotencyKey } (7 in parallel via code:run). For 3 of them (su-96b7fe62, su-fe99c651, su-2fde89b1) the result had no resumeVerification/resumeVerified, and each original identity came up on a NEW native session id (9fab66ac / 2b6a3bc1 / bda1c09f). Two extra sessions then appeared with launch_parent_owner = me, started 22:12:50 ET, argv `psu --no-picker --resume=<that new sid> --fork --agent=claude ...`: su-35233845 (fork of su-fe99c651 sid 2b6a3bc1; it detected the duplicate and stood down) and su-5f692bae (fork of su-2fde89b1 sid bda1c09f). Contract per the arg doc: `fork:false requires non-live in-place recovery` and refuses a live source, so no --fork launch should ever come from a fork:false call. Unconfirmed mechanism [inferred]: the source turned live mid-call (a system revive/wake-executor or the first in-place launch registering), and some path such as a retry, a second attempt or an auto-fork-on-live branch ignored fork:false. Evidence: harness_shared.adv_sessions rows for su-35233845 / su-5f692bae (launch_argv), plus the code:run batch output. Fix: thread fork:false through every retry/live-source branch so it refuses (typed error) instead of forking; also return resumeVerification on every resume result.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-27 ~23:50Z on su-1957b874 (frozen-burndown member, Claude psu session af168676…, fresh carry-respawn successor). In the same turn, reads and writes had worked: coord:orient, work_items:get, state:read, release:repair-queue status, and a work_items:claim that reached the fleet-scope check. Then every call was refused before dispatch with `request_rejected: superuser_native_session_unverified`. That included work_items:comment, the same call via tools:invoke, and coord:whoami. The session ended mid-call shortly after, and the owner reopened it in a visible terminal at ~02:13Z. After the reopen, the identical work_items:comment payload succeeded (post 1208547).
Cause: unknown, unconfirmed. Suspect the native-session verification for ?superuser=1 lapsed (heartbeat or session-binding expiry around the carry-respawn) while the process stayed up.
Impact: an AUTO fleet member silently loses all tools, cannot even checkpoint, and needs a human reopen. That is the 'TOOLLESS but connected' / 'IDENTITY' recovery class, but the error code named neither one, nor a recovery verb.
Proposed fix: (1) map superuser_native_session_unverified to a self-recovery path (re-verify the session binding transparently, or return the exact recovery command in the refusal); (2) make sure these refusals are recorded in tool_invocations so the invocation-friction watchdog sees them; (3) find out why verification lapsed mid-turn.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-28 ~04:46Z, su-28bda5ad (plan change-provenance-and-admission-throughput-2026-10-27).

Evidence:
- Predecessor session emitted spec-quality card EI-27177195506640205 at 23:29Z with item-contract-coverage=pass ("All 14 plan item(s) are covered"). gradedGeneration.deployedSha=d740fc3802 (main, :3070).
- After a carry-respawn, every MCP call from the successor (coord:orient, plans:start, plans:evaluate-spec-quality, scorecards:get) has harness_shared.tool_invocations.serving_host='port-3170' with serving_build_sha=a771bcbf59. The query was by coord_owner_id, last 15 min.
- Same clause set (clausesAsOf 23:29:44): the :3170 evaluator fails item-contract-coverage and plan-class-specialization. Commit cc30e0be62 (2026-10-01) excludes sourceBar-pinned AUTO-BAR projections from item coverage. `git merge-base --is-ancestor cc30e0be62 main` is false: main has been without it for about 27 days.

Impact: an activation gate (plans:start) gives different verdicts for identical inputs depending on which operator served the call. The audit cycle was spent on a card that the other host will not accept. CLAUDE.md also says never to bind a long-lived session's MCP to :3170 (it restarts about 200 times a day), yet the respawned session is bound there.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-28 06:46Z (su-f6ff509d), :3170 build 96cbf1656f, plan one-work-graph-structured-holds-2026-10-26.

plans:start via scripts/mcp-call.mjs --port 3170 at the default (trimmed) tier returned results[0] = { ok:false, error:'plan_inputs_not_ready', code:'acceptance_bar_contract_not_ready' } and nothing else (.papercusp/scratch/owg/r4/start.out). The same call with payloadTier:'full' returned missing:['bar_snapshot_rubric_revision_mismatch'], source, and a multi-line hint naming the exact repair (.papercusp/scratch/owg/r4/start-full.out).

PlanStartRefusal (packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/plan-start-gate.ts:60-73) documents hint as "One-line, actionable — surface this to the caller as-is", and start.ts:284 spreads the whole refusal into the result. So the fields are emitted and then removed by the trimmed-tier payload shaper. Cost: the predecessor session carried an [inferred] wrong cause (R-4 clause vs the rubric bar snapshot) across a carry-respawn; the real cause was a plain revision-pin mismatch.

Proposed fix: the trimmed-tier shaper should preserve the refusal-contract fields (code, missing, issues, hint, message) on any result with ok:false, or plans:start should mark them as never-trim. Guard: a test that runs plans:start's refusal through the trimmed-tier projection and asserts that hint and missing survive. Cause unconfirmed beyond the A/B above: I have not read the shaper itself.

admissionIdentity.titleKey: title:12min 1601 abandoned accessexclusive boot client fleet held items migration outage statement timeout wide work

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-28 08:26-08:38Z. Backend pid 2365442 (application_name papercusp-boot-migrate, client = hono-host PORT=3270 pid 2278678) ran migration 1601-plan-line-work-item-nodes.sql (WI-6554700010030910) as ONE transaction: ALTER TABLE work_items ADD COLUMN (AccessExclusiveLock, verified in pg_locks) followed by a whole-workspace data conversion (convert_plan_lines_to_nodes over ~440k work_items / 15.8k plan_items). The script runs SET LOCAL statement_timeout = 0, so it was never cut off. While it ran, 64-68 backends queued on Lock, including plain SELECTs on work_items. Effects: every work_items:get timed out (55P03), work_items:checkpoint writes failed, and governed test admission refused (TEST_FILE_ADMISSION_ERROR admission-starved). The backend was CPU-bound (no read_bytes growth over 5s). By ~08:37Z the client socket was FIN-WAIT-2 and the server side CLOSE-WAIT, so the boot runner had already abandoned the connection while the orphaned backend kept the lock. It committed on its own at ~08:38Z (schema_migrations row present).

Root causes (the class, not this one file):
(1) Data conversion over the hottest table ran in the same transaction as AccessExclusive DDL, so the lock was held for the whole conversion.
(2) The migration runner and script allow an unbounded statement_timeout on boot.
(3) When the boot runner abandons a connection, its in-flight migration transaction is not cancelled.

Proposed durable fix:
(a) The migration runner sets lock_timeout plus a bounded statement_timeout for boot-path migrations, and cancels its backend (pg_cancel_backend) when it gives up.
(b) A lint fails a migration that combines ALTER TABLE on work_items (or any hot table) with UPDATE/INSERT data conversion in one file. Conversions go in a separate file or in batched app code.
(c) Set client_connection_check_interval on migration connections so a closed client aborts the statement.

ⓘ Possible STALE RUNTIME, not an open defect: `libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/1601-plan-line-work-item-nodes.sql` (1 newer commit, tip `f49c4cb399a879cb8f7e443e03c585ecd8da1930`) have commits newer than the running build (`d740fc3802`) in `staging`. If this was observed live, verify the deployed generation before triaging; the behavior may already be fixed in the tree.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed by su-96b7fe62 (gate owner WI-10006055), 2026-10-28 10:35-11:00Z.

Symptom: these MCP writes repeatedly returned client-side "The operation timed out" (direct calls and via tools:invoke): work_items:checkpoint, loop:checkpoint, loop:status (55s request_timeout), session:request-compaction. In the same window these succeeded quickly: state:read, release:repair-queue op:get, dev:pg_query (45-70ms), coord:declare-intent.
Also at 11:03Z, tools:invoke release:repair-queue op:admit on :3170 (build d924c00ba3) returned request_rejected: superuser_native_session_verifier_unavailable. The same call sent through scripts/mcp-call.mjs --port 3170 one minute later succeeded.

Consequence: the green-checkpoint ownership lease on WI-10006055 lapsed at 10:46:03Z (state:read gate.greenCheckpoint.ownership = lease-expired, holder still live). The holder could not renew it, so the gate showed as re-claimable while its owner was actively working it. Compaction also could not run, so the session went past 108% of its context limit.

PG evidence at 10:59Z (pg_stat_activity, active backends): 37 running, 26 ClientRead, 5 IO/DataFileRead, 2 LWLock/WALWrite, 1 IO/WalSync, 3 Lock/advisory (transient, no blockers at the next sample). Two autovacuum VACUUMs on pg_toast tables were waiting on WALWrite. UPDATE harness_shared.work_items SET payload=... statements took 4s+ in DataFileRead. One org-admin SELECT on sa.run_id/transcript had been running for 601s (pid 3381943). WI-10006055's updated_ts advanced at 10:50:42Z, so some writes land late, after the client has already timed out.

Cause not established. Suspects: (1) IO-bound work_items payload UPDATEs (large jsonb payload rewrite + toast) amplified by WAL contention from autovacuum on toast tables; (2) the shared harness_admin pool / PgBouncer acquisition already filed as EI-26434665056322536 / EI-25518647225512022 (verifier-unavailable class).
Missing guard: a gate-hold lease that the holder cannot renew because of platform write latency should not expire into "re-claimable" while the holder is live and progressing (lastProgressAt / declared intent / coord activity).
