_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed by su-96b7fe62 (gate owner WI-10006055) on 2026-10-28. A release:repair-queue {op:'admit', confirm:true, 149 paths, wholeBlob@969ae43a} sent via mcp-call --port 3170 at 11:10:22Z returned MCP request_timeout ("exceeded 300000ms, commit status is UNKNOWN") at 11:15:24Z. tool_invocations id 45515599 shows the server finished in 305063ms with a complete answer: refused admission-incomplete 0b51b3bb3434 with 32 missing refs. timings.steps build-proof = 275187ms. The answer existed only in the output_ref scratch spill. The caller had to reconstruct it by hand: dev:pg_query on tool_invocations, then parse a 400KB scratch file. A naive agent would blind-retry (risking a double apply) or wait.

Proposed fix: make admit confirm an async operation like admission previews. Return {operationId} immediately and emit release:repair-queue:admit-settled:<id> carrying verdict/missing/movedRepairHead, so callers events:await instead of holding a 5-min request. Alternatively, give release:repair-queue a per-tool timeout above the build-proof ceiling. Cause [inferred, not probed]: the test reaches the real repo walk rather than an injected `code` dependency or a small fixture root, so a wall-clock budget that is fine unloaded fails under fleet load. _claimSubjectBaseline.body:
MEASURED 2026-10-28, run papercup-green-checkpoint-manual-1fxzuva, candidate 63442ecf, base d740fc38 (last green, ~12k commits back). Log /tmp/papercup-green-checkpoint-manual-1fxzuva-2026-10-28T12-32-55-693Z.log:
- 'early changed-file typecheck preflight: FAILED in 2707.6s across 13843 file(s) (23353 total changed file(s))'
- P-016 path: 'running the affected-test sweep anyway so round 1 measures the full failing set'
- then 'infra fault: the affected-tests run REFUSED to render a verdict (reason=deadline-insufficient) — 192 of 192 task(s) UNDETERMINED and 0 measured failures'
- GATE_ROUND_PHASES total 1h03m: early-typecheck-preflight 45m09s (71%), setup-tree 10m, candidate-suite 4m25s.

Effect: P-016's whole purpose (round 1 measures the full failing set) is defeated whenever the base is far behind. The frozen queue opens knowing only the lint legs. Every test red is discovered one round later, which costs at least one extra full gate cycle (about 1h) per candidate.

Proposed fix: the early typecheck should not draw from the suite's deadline budget. Either (a) give the affected-tests sweep its own deadline that starts after the preflight, or (b) when the preflight fails on round 1, skip the remaining preflight legs and start the sweep while time remains. Its reds are already known, and the post-suite legs re-run anyway. (c) Separately: 2707s for one changed-file typecheck means the TSC_SERVICE path fell back (the log shows 'TSC_SERVICE request failed ... identity mismatch changedIdentityFields=["compilerInstall"]' three times), so every leg cold-compiled. That service identity mismatch is likely the root of the 45 minutes.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-28 16:14-16:20Z (su-a835dc70, WI-6554700010042405). 15 of the 32 Codex agents relaunched under owner directives #2561/#2579 have a live psu-pty host (kill -0 ok) at hostCodeVersion fc21449d, but NO harness_shared.coord_presence row. Their resume kickoff turn (host injectTurnAtPrompt) failed on gateway 429 sheds (native-turn-failed, code response_too_many_failed_attempts / other; execution.phase='failed'). Now:
- coord:send and coord:wake both return unknown_recipient (measured on su-58f6ce8c, su-8f6cb08e). psu-pty-host.mjs:12610 documents this as by design: a resumed session's presence rows were reaped, so only the host kickoff can reach it.
- capability:launch-agent resume auto-FORKS a live source (WI-3882), which makes a duplicate identity rather than delivering a turn.
- restoreVisible refuses alive hosts, and fleet:respawn-member relaunches under a fresh identity.
So no sanctioned external lever can seed a turn into a live, idle, resumed host once its single kickoff is spent. 10 of the 15 have been idle since 15:30-16:01Z.
Proposed fix (either half works; both is best):
(1) The host should treat a kickoff/turn failure whose cause is retryable (429 exhaustion, response_too_many_failed_attempts) as quota-class: hold, then re-inject the same kickoff once the gateway serves again (relates to WI-1386682, quota-blocked first-class state), instead of retiring the delivery as native-turn-start-failed.
(2) The live host should upsert its own coord_presence row at boot (heartbeat 'parked'), so a roster-gated wake can reach a resumed session that has not yet completed a turn.
Workaround in use: processes:kill the idle host by taskId, then capability:launch-agent resume by its exact codex sessionId.

ⓘ Possible STALE RUNTIME, not an open defect: `apps/operator/scripts/psu-pty-host.mjs` (412 newer commits, tip `60a994f29dcb56481e53b230c3a586889f616b11`), `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/capability/launch-agent.ts` (162 newer commits, tip `20749293e16f4a11ee2bcb41df2e2d39ca3a4070`) have commits newer than the running build (`d740fc3802`) in `staging`. If this was observed live, verify the deployed generation before triaging; the behavior may already be fixed in the tree.

admissionIdentity.titleKey: title:absence bounded carry check claims explicitly flags lint returned rows scope

_claimSubjectBaseline.body: Reproduction observed 2026-10-28: work_items:checkpoint returned scopeLint for a ✓ check whose claim says the exact dev:telemetry match count was zero WITHIN the one bounded activity:recent result of 500 returned rows. The recheck is also explicitly limited to the same returned 500 rows. The current detector in packages/operator-core/lib/carry-note-probe-scope.ts detectScopeOverreach treats the lower-case quantifier 'zero' plus `limit 500` as overreach, even though the claim's population is precisely the bounded result. This creates a false alarm on correctly scoped claims. A small fix is to recognize explicit claim language that binds absence to the returned result/window (while preserving the existing regression where absence is asserted across the wider population).

admissionIdentity.titleKey: title:agent host kill not pid processes psu recorded reports signalled sigterm survives task taskid the true while wrapper

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-28 16:27-16:31Z by su-a835dc70 (WI-6554700010042405).

[measured] processes:kill { taskId:'0mvs9r0uzmk59r10e6b', includeSubtree:true } (agent-session task for su-e470543c, launched by capability:launch-agent resume at ~15:30Z) returned ok:true, "pid 4193028 signalled SIGTERM". 4193028 was gone afterwards, but the real psu host 4193037 (psu-launcher.mjs, parent 4193029 = bash ~/.papercusp/bin/psu …--resume=01a17c57…) and its codex child 5894/5970 kept running. The host's ~/.papercusp/psu-pty/<owner>.json/.sock stayed in place. All of them were in cgroup vte-spawn-048ef4c0-….scope. Four sibling kills in the same batch (d6cc9ca2, a1fd3b21, 1b1c4d3e, 637d70bf) did take their hosts down.

[measured] Recovery levers all failed: processes:kill { pid:4193037 } → unsupported_kind ("not a managed agent kind"). processes:kill { scopeUnit:'vte-spawn-…scope' } → no_target ("not a validated Papercusp task scope unit"). The task is confined:false, so its cgroup is the terminal tab's vte-spawn scope. systemctl --user stop is unreachable from either agent shell (native Bash masks /run/user/1000; capability:bash's systemctl reported "inactive" while the pids lived). _claimSubjectBaseline.body:
CORRECTED 19:45Z (su-96b7fe62). My first filing said this divergence blocks the git-sync push leg. That was wrong. Origin staging advanced normally until 18:56:46Z (2a72f0de87) while this divergence has stood since 09:26Z. The current push lag is a git-sync fire in flight since 19:16:33Z in phase local-sync (health.git_sync_freshness.execution: still progressing, safe_to_restart=false). That's the same class as EI-27245008645300283. Local staging f7bc9e1e1a is 17 commits ahead of origin.

What the divergence actually is (measured): harness_shared.harness_escalations (papercusp, phase github-bridge) signals = [{kind:'ingress-non-ff', branch:'main', local:b1f1d0cd2ba4, remote:d740fc3802}], needs_owner=true, recorded 09:26:35Z. b1f1d0cd2b is exactly one commit on top of d740fc3802 ('sync(.papercusp): blueprint.yaml', 2026-10-14) and carries the tag refs/tags/backup/drill-main-b1f1d0cd-20261021. So a 10-21 drill moved origin main to b1f1d0cd2b and later restored it to d740fc3802. The bridge's synthetic github-origin namespace ingressed b1f1d0cd2b, then by design (github-ingress.ts: the namespace only advances fast-forward) refused the restore as 'origin rewrote history'. Origin main IS d740fc3802 (git ls-remote), and local main is d740fc3802.

Harm: (1) a permanent needs-owner condition for a non-event; (2) it occupies git-sync's health.last_error, so anyone diagnosing push failures reads it as the cause (I did). Fix options: (a) accept the drill restore for main once via the allowNonFF lever (origin is authoritative; the drill commit is preserved by its backup tag); (b) durable: have drills that move origin main record a drill marker the bridge recognises, so a restore isn't classified as a rewrite; (c) don't surface the bridge divergence as git-sync's last_error when push/commit legs are healthy. [inferred] Promotion should be unaffected: it pushes local main (FF from d740fc3802) directly, not through the bridge namespace. Not verified.

admissionIdentity.titleKey: title:because blocks code guard inline literal path prose python3 resolved shell string tree write

_claimSubjectBaseline.body: [observed 2026-10-28 22:26Z, su-05452b08, WI-6554700010030904] A native Bash call ran `python3 - <<'EOF' ... json.dump({...,'summary':'... claim cap 1/1 ...'}, open('/tmp/wi904-send.json','w'))`. The PreToolUse shell-write guard (EI-18691482279179647) REFUSED it with: "inline code that references `1/1`, which resolves INSIDE the shared staging tree". The only write target was /tmp/wi904-send.json, outside the tree. `1/1` appeared only inside a human-readable message string, not as a path argument to any write call. Expected: the guard treats only write-call path arguments (or path-shaped tokens) as candidate targets, and does not classify a bare `N/N` ratio inside a string literal as a repo-relative path. Workaround used: wrote the payload with the Write tool to /tmp/su05452-wi904/send.json. Suggested fix: in the guard's path extraction, require a path token to contain a letter, a dot-extension, or a known top-level tree dir (packages/, libs/, apps/, scripts/ ...) before resolving it against the repo root; or restrict extraction to arguments of open()/writeFileSync()/write_text() calls, which the sibling advisory guard EI-18828866497684686 already parses. Same command shape earlier in this turn (writing /tmp/wi904-cp.json) passed with only the advisory notice, so the refusal was caused by the literal alone.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Code-confirmed integration gap discovered during owner-requested architectural assessment. dependency-staleness.ts observeCell() takes status:value reads and hashes only read.value, optionally read.material.value; CurrentCellObservation has no assessment code/status, evidence digest, source-authoritativeness, or unknownHoist. evaluateDependencyStaleness() returns fresh when headline/material digests match. By contrast state:subscribe defaults to assessment changes. Concrete case: git.pipelinePosition headline is positions.deployed; both live and restart-required can have true, while assessment changes based on serving.startedSinceCodeChange. Even more directly, a read may keep status:value and unchanged headline while assessment becomes unavailable; freshness still hashes that value and can report fresh. No production incident claimed; mechanism established by source. Proposed fix: extend existing FactDependency/CurrentCellObservation with a versioned assessment/status anchor (and necessary measuredness/source qualifiers), capture from the same read, and mark semantic changes stale or unassessable readings undeterminable. Preserve explicit materiality semantics. Add canonical regression tests for same measurement/different assessment and assessment unavailable. Existing tests cover raw/material drift but have no assessment cases (rg assessment|semantic over dependency-staleness.ts and its test).

admissionIdentity.titleKey: title:advances before change confirmed context delivery facts watermark

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Source-confirmed mismatch in the delta delivery boundary. composeOrient standing-facts fold calls factsCellDelta(withDeps, wm.cursors.facts), then writes delta.nextCursor to coord_watermarks during construction of a full fold, before result.facts is returned/serialized/emitted. If response fails after the write, the next full fold compares against that advanced HLC and no longer marks those facts changed. The full fact content remains available; the lost item is its changed notification, not the stored fact. Meanwhile turn-start orientation/control/package delivery already uses read-cursors stage + confirmedDelivery token proof to avoid this class. No production incident claimed. Proposed fix: stage facts-surface HLC with the delivered output and commit only on the existing host-confirmed delivery boundary; keep full baseline/rebootstrap and narrowed-fold no-advance behavior. Test: write newer fact -> construct output -> drop output before emission -> next unconfirmed read must show its changed marker; matching token may then commit it. Existing factsCellDelta tests cover HLC comparison, not this caller delivery boundary. Dedup search was degraded; no absence claim about prior records.

If this was observed live, verify the deployed generation before triaging; the behavior may already be fixed in the tree.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Source-derived suspected scoring defect noticed while explaining recipes for WI-6554700010045423 (2026-11-05). agent-tools/recipes/run.ts records every executed script in code_recipe_runs, but sets countTowardRecipe = successfulReuse && !dryRun. code-recipes-store.ts recordRecipeRun updates parent run_count/success_count only when countTowardRecipe. code-recipes-candidates.ts computes successRate from those parent counters, while capture-recipe.ts attaches only successful authored executions. _claimSubjectBaseline.body: During read-only audit WI-6554700010046166, PreToolUse blocked three independent native exec reads because the execution-authority lookup got no headers within1500ms from http://127.0.0.1:9071 (stage wall-during-fetch, elapsed1504ms). Do not route around current refusals or widen write authority.

The original zero-measured result was a transient open-circuit response from the shared sidecar path, not evidence that the stored bindings were absent or persistently unreadable. The explicit degraded/unknown evaluator result preserves that distinction.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed in owned P025 v6 exact7ab92da0344dec949a6aa9cd930958e8709c63b6 run20261106T080855Z-2461837: prepare passed, nested installed OMP production MCP case rejected at measureLifecycle execFile. The original worker failure only retained generic Command failed and Node child_process stack; measureLifecycle awaits promisify(execFile) without a catch to preserve error.stdout/error.stderr, then finally recursively removes home/session/result. This obscures the command's cause after an expensive retained runtime run. Root cause of the underlying OMP command exit is not yet known. Specific fix: use existing retained-artifact/evidence-dir mechanisms to write a sanitized command receipt (surface/version/status/signal, stdout/stderr and result if present) on both success and rejection before home cleanup; attach receipt ref to thrown error. Add regression coverage in maintained installed-client/helper suite that a rejecting command preserves its output while session cleanup still occurs. Current test:file final result is FAIL, not accepted. Original evidence /mnt/data/offload/verification-harness/isolated-integration/20261106T080855Z-2461837/phases/execute/{worker.log,census/worker-result.json,census/worker.log}; original nested runtime/PG removal receipt present; parent finalization still running. No duplicate expensive run launched.

Measured exact D005 acceptance lane: canonical plans:blind-review mint for current plan30/activation12 timed out at caller, but maintained findBlindReviewSessionBinding returned binding30/reviewer su-07c530c7-7a6b-4cb2-aa44-25f57d52740f/adv56501/native949a6bb7-a3f3-43e4-bf40-72ac772e79ef/statusready/reviewIdnull. Binding accountRoute auto, modelSpec opus[1m]:max. Transcript session_turn:claude:949a6bb7-a3f3-43e4-bf40-72ac772e79ef:1 is exactly 'Credit balance is too low' at11:56:35Z; current binding remainedready with no review at12:46. Confined kickoff reached the process; no product work is recorded in that bounded transcript window. Existing-session wake d56a4e41 at12:47:42 queued/woken but pickup initially unconfirmed; new transcript turn3 at12:47:50 says 'API Error: Request rejected (429) · inference-gateway: all accounts throttled; retry after 60s'. No root cause of provider/account availability is established; these are the API's reported errors, not a resource-pressure explanation. Source of misleading readiness is the launch/binding lifecycle treating a started process as ready without representing this first-turn provider failure. Extend the existing readiness/recovery path to retain the SAME binding, classify pre-review provider failures as a blocked/retryable condition, honor provider retry timing/account capacity, recover that same confined context through the supported route, and require actual product-turn pickup before reporting progress. Add a maintained regression that initial billing failure/429 cannot leave a ready-but-unworked acceptance lane invisible or trigger a duplicate reviewer. Do not bypass confinement, change immutable binding history, synthesize an inconclusive reviewer post, or spawn an ad-hoc replacement. Root diagnosis/source repair remains required; this is an owned follow-up, not a resolution claim.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
EI-10733 durable backup-health probe: '/mnt/backup/db-dumps/pg/papercusp-transcript' has not advanced in 67 hours (size 4096B). The DB dump is supposed to run ~hourly.

THIS IS THE SIGNAL THAT WAS MISSING. On 2026-07-12 the backup had been failing 100% for ~30 DAYS (newest good dump 2026-06-12) and nothing detected it, because a plausible-looking 1.4GB .gz sat on disk the whole time. 'The backup file exists' is not 'the backup works' — only its FRESHNESS discriminates.

LIKELY CAUSES (check in this order):
 1. db-backup.sh's timer stopped firing: systemctl --user status papercusp-db-backup.timer papercusp-db-backup.service ; journalctl --user -u papercusp-db-backup.service -n 50. Read /mnt/backup/db-dumps/STATUS.json (ok / failed[] / lastSuccessEpoch) and /mnt/backup/db-dumps/db-backup.log.
 2. A specific DB's dump is failing validation: db-backup.sh only renames a dump into place after pg_restore -l passes, so a per-DB 'FAIL' in db-backup.log means the archive was unreadable or the dump errored — read the actual pg_dump error there. DO NOT blindly raise PC_BACKUP_TIMEOUT_SEC without reading it.
 3. An orphaned pg_dump is holding locks (the EI-10730 knock-on): check for a pg_dump backend older than its timeout (SELECT pid, application_name, backend_start FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE application_name LIKE 'pg_dump%'). db-backup.sh tags its own dumps PGAPPNAME=pcbackup and reaps foreign ones; a lingering 'pg_dump%' backend is a legacy/manual dump.
 4. Disk full on the backup volume: df -h /mnt/backup/db-dumps

An orphaned/stuck dump is not just a dead backup — it holds AccessShareLock on ~593 tables, which starves every migration's ACCESS EXCLUSIVE and can wedge the whole release pipeline (EI-10730).

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
[self-imposed; su-b0194963, measured first-hand 2026-09-22T11:05Z. Found while closing WI-10002222/P-011 -- NOT claimed, filing so it is not lost.]

## Symptom
A scorecard emitted by scorecards:emit gets `gradingAudit.state='pending'` plus a `dispatchReservation`. For 23 scorecards that reservation has never cleared, the oldest for 10 days. Each one HARD-BLOCKS a work_items:complete: the spec-test-adequacy gate refuses with `pendingGradingAuditTargetIds`, short-circuiting BEFORE it evaluates the caller's specAdequacy fingerprints (the refusal reports `checked: []`, which reads misleadingly like a malformed payload).

## The reservation is self-blocking
scorecards:repair -- the documented repair path, whose own description says "pass targetIds for a stale scorecard named by a refusal" -- is a NO-OP for exactly these rows. It returns `state:'skipped', reason:'another dispatcher already reserved this scorecard'` under idempotencyKey `grading-audit:<issueId>`. The blocking reservation IS the emit-time dispatcher's own. So the sole documented repair verb cannot repair the one class of row it was written for, and returns a success-shaped receipt (`ok:true`) while doing nothing.

## Evidence: the age distribution is bimodal, which is what makes this a leak and not a backlog
Measured over harness_shared.engineer_issues (workspace_id='papercusp-workspace'), pending + reservation present, ordered by reservation age in minutes:
  5 (mine, EI-23959061823082216, settled normally later)
  2238, 3302, 3666 x3, 3717, 3721 x8, 4152 x2, 4167 x2, 4227, 4228, 4230 x2, 4258
  9555, 13508, 13540, 13897, 14104 x2
There is NOTHING between 5 minutes and 2238 minutes. A queue that is merely slow produces a continuous age curve; a 37-hour hole with 23 rows stranded beyond it is a leak. Oldest: EI-23070559141095796 (AUTO-BAR-R-6-P-002@4), reserved 2026-09-12T16:00:10Z.

## The mechanism is otherwise alive -- so this is a leak, not an outage
Settled audits in the last 24h: passed n=45 (median 454s, min 162s), failed n=5 (median 502s). Newest passed was stamped 2026-09-22T10:11:55Z. So most audits settle in ~7 minutes; a minority strand permanently.

## Suspected root cause (INFERRED -- not observed, re-probe before acting)
The reservation is written durably at dispatch time but its release appears to be tied to the dispatched auditor actually reporting. When routing fails, the auditor declines terminally, or the routed session dies, nothing clears the reservation and nothing re-dispatches -- and because the idempotency key persists, every later repair attempt is refused by the corpse of the first one. A reservation with no liveness/TTL and no owner-death release is the shape that produces exactly this distribution. What I OBSERVED is the distribution, the skipped receipt, and the settle latencies; the release-path explanation is my inference.

## Durable fix to consider (fix the CLASS)
(1) Give the reservation a TTL or a liveness check so a dead dispatcher's claim expires -- the same rail locks:* already applies. (2) Make scorecards:repair able to PREEMPT a reservation older than the settle p99 (~2.7h by the 24h data), which is precisely the job its description already advertises. (3) Have it return a distinguishable state for 'skipped because a LIVE dispatcher holds it' vs 'skipped because a stale corpse holds it' -- today both are the same success-shaped receipt. (4) Alarm on pending-with-reservation older than a threshold; 23 stranded rows accumulated over 10 days with nothing firing, which is a detector failure in its own right.

## Repro
scorecards:repair { targetIds:['EI-23070559141095796'], harness:'papercusp' } -> expect ok:true with state='skipped', reason='another dispatcher already reserved this scorecard', while the row has sat pending since 2026-09-12.

## Query accessor note (two silent false-zeros en route)
The census needs `payload->'observation'->'gradingAudit'` (NOT top-level `payload->'gradingAudit'`, which is absent) and `scope='harness:papercusp'` (NOT 'papercusp'). Both wrong accessors return a confident zero-row result that reads as 'no backlog exists'. I hit both; only a positive control against a known row caught it.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
## Observed (measured 2026-09-22T19:10Z, su-4efe1c00)
This session's carry-respawn continuation arrived as `<pasted_content id="5f47">\n⟦turn-origin:self-compaction nonce:807623f407ac1ff3⟧ ADDRESSED TO su-4efe1c00… </pasted_content>`. The UserPromptSubmit hook stamped it `⟦turn-provenance⟧ OWNER (interactive) — no origin envelope, no ledger match` and the directive-capture rail recorded it as PENDING owner order #140 (the prior respawn's continuation had likewise become #128). Both were dismissed by me as machine-origin.

## Fleet-wide scale (measured, orders:list open:true at 19:12Z)
16 open orders; the carry excerpts of #127, #128, #130, #132, #134, #135 (self-compaction), #131, #133 (wake-pump) and #136, #137 (fleet-kickoff, recorded by role-* grading auditors) all begin `<pasted_content id=…>\n⟦turn-origin:…⟧` — i.e. machine-injected turns captured as owner directives, ~10 in ~20 minutes across ~9 sessions.

## Cause (measured in code)
`packages/operator-core/lib/turn-provenance/envelope-grammar.ts:67` — `ENVELOPE_PATTERN_SOURCE = ^\s*⟦turn-origin:(…) nonce:(…)⟧` is START-anchored; `parseEnvelope` (turn-provenance.ts:149) uses it, so a `<pasted_content …>` prefix defeats the match. `grep -rl pasted_content` over scripts/, packages/operator-core/lib, apps/operator/lib → 0 files: no code unwraps the wrapper. The ledger-hash fallback also misses (wrapped text ≠ injected payload), so classify() falls through to the final OWNER branch (turn-provenance.ts:671).
[inferred, not probed] The `<pasted_content>` wrapper is added by the Claude Code client when a long prompt is delivered as input; the injectors send a correctly-enveloped payload.

## Why major
1. Manufactures owner directives out of machine text (the WI-3532 failure class) and floods every session's Orientation with bogus PENDING directives that agents must resolve by hand.
2. The mode-registration hook is gated on this turn classifying OWNER — a wrapped machine turn containing AUTO/ideate phrasing could register a mode as ownerDirected:true.
3. Session search provenance (`turn_origin`) marks these turns owner-typed.

## Suggested durable fix
Unwrap a leading `<pasted_content id=…>` … `</pasted_content>` (and whatever other client wrappers exist) BEFORE envelope parse + ledger hash, in ONE shared normalizer used by all 4 grammar sites (see EI-20202332205249019 — the grammar is re-typed in 4 sites/3 languages, incl. the shell form at envelope-grammar.ts:93). Recurrence guard: a unit test in turn-provenance feeding a wrapped enveloped continuation and asserting VERIFIED AGENT-ORIGIN, plus a test that a wrapped owner paste without an envelope still classifies OWNER. Consider a one-shot sweep dismissing currently-open orders whose text starts with a wrapped envelope.

Related (different leak paths, both closed): WI-38268, WI-37908.

`packages/operator-core/lib/turn-provenance/envelope-grammar.ts:67` — `ENVELOPE_PATTERN_SOURCE = ^\s*⟦turn-origin:(…) nonce:(…)⟧` is START-anchored; `parseEnvelope` (turn-provenance.ts:149) uses it, so a `<pasted_content …>` prefix defeats the match. `grep -rl pasted_content` over scripts/, packages/operator-core/lib, apps/operator/lib → 0 files: no code unwraps the wrapper. The ledger-hash fallback also misses (wrapped text ≠ injected payload), so classify() falls through to the final OWNER branch (turn-provenance.ts:671).
[inferred, not probed] The `<pasted_content>` wrapper is added by the Claude Code client when a long prompt is delivered as input; the injectors send a correctly-enveloped payload.

## Why major
1. Manufactures owner directives out of machine text (the WI-3532 failure class) and floods every session's Orientation with bogus PENDING directives that agents must resolve by hand.
2. The mode-registration hook is gated on this turn classifying OWNER — a wrapped machine turn containing AUTO/ideate phrasing could register a mode as ownerDirected:true.
3. Session search provenance (`turn_origin`) marks these turns owner-typed.

## Suggested durable fix
Unwrap a leading `<pasted_content id=…>` … `</pasted_content>` (and whatever other client wrappers exist) BEFORE envelope parse + ledger hash, in ONE shared normalizer used by all 4 grammar sites (see EI-20202332205249019 — the grammar is re-typed in 4 sites/3 languages, incl. the shell form at envelope-grammar.ts:93). Recurrence guard: a unit test in turn-provenance feeding a wrapped enveloped continuation and asserting VERIFIED AGENT-ORIGIN, plus a test that a wrapped owner paste without an envelope still classifies OWNER. Consider a one-shot sweep dismissing currently-open orders whose text starts with a wrapped envelope.

Related (different leak paths, both closed): WI-38268, WI-37908.

Mechanism [measured by reading code]: papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/seed is gitignored (papercusp-desktop/.gitignore:61). apps/operator/bin/release/setup-release-checkout.sh extract_submodule_source does rm -rf $RELEASE_ROOT/<submodule> and re-extracts from git archive on every fire, so an isolated cut root NEVER has a seed snapshot. release-local.sh cut_release_seed (auto mode) then falls to the fresh-from-live-store branch. That branch requires release_seed_cut_is_quiesced (a runtime marker or masked bg-host), which a managed routine never has. _claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Measured 2026-09-27 09:02-09:10Z by su-5b9cde39 (host-memory-reduction-2026-09-27 investigation, #688). [measured unless tagged]

SYMPTOM: box-wide IO PSI some avg60 48-54%, full 44-50% (/proc/pressure/io at 09:04Z and 09:07Z), while memory is healthy (MemAvailable 116 GB, memory PSI ~0).

DEVICE: iostat -dx 10 s on nvme0n1 at 09:07Z: r/s 4,066, r_await 0.86 ms (reads are fine); w/s 364, 22 MB/s, w_await 785 ms, aqu-sz 289, util 84%. An earlier 5 s sample at 09:02Z: w_await 745 ms, aqu 441. D-019 (plan host-memory-reduction-2026-09-27) measured fdatasync ~500 ms per write on this disk vs ~0.6 ms on nvme1n1.
- nvme0n1 = TEAM TM8FPW002T (hwmon model string), 2 TB, ext4 root, 90% full (1.7T used / 194G avail), mounted without discard; fstrim.timer weekly, last run 2026-09-21. Temperature 54.9 C (not throttling).
- nvme1n1 = WD_BLACK SN850X HS 8000GB, xfs /mnt/data, 76% (1.8T free).
- [inferred] A DRAM-less 2 TB drive at 90% full with its SLC cache exhausted writes at native speed plus GC. That fits reads at 0.9 ms next to writes at 785 ms.

WHAT WRITES TO IT (sampled 09:02-09:05Z):
- Postgres: data_directory /var/lib/postgresql/18/main, 136 GB, pg_wal NOT separated. So every commit's WAL fdatasync queues behind the 785 ms write backlog. [inferred] This is a floor under the latency of every tool call.
- apps/operator/bin/release/dependency-generation.sh: `cp -a --reflink=auto node_modules` (15 GB). ext4 has no reflink, so it is a full 15 GB copy (pid in bg-host, 270 MiB/10 s, running 12+ min), plus a second copy of a generation inside the green-checkpoint scope. 8 generations sit in .papercusp/dependency-generations.
- Dirty page cache: 7.7 GB Dirty in /proc/meminfo, 6.2 GB of it charged to papercusp-bg-host.service.
- Reads: kopia-home-snapshot (daily, started 08:11Z) at 228 MiB/s. Reads are not the bottleneck (r_await <1 ms).

SECOND DEFECT — IO de-prioritisation is inert box-wide:
- nvme0n1 and nvme1n1 use scheduler `none`, which ignores ioprio. So IOSchedulingClass=idle / ionice -c3 have no effect (kopia pid 3738236 is class idle, and it still reads at full rate).
- user@1000.service has DelegateControllers=cpu memory pids (its cgroup.subtree_control is 'cpu memory pids'). The io controller is not delegated, so IOWeight / IOReadBandwidthMax / IOWriteBandwidthMax in any user unit is silently ignored too.
- 19 installed user units depend on these settings (kopia-home-snapshot, kopia-snapshots, papercusp-db-backup, papercup-backup-health, docker-reclaim, tmp-scratch-reclaim, vitest-orphan-reaper, webkit-reaper, pc-estate-mirror, ...). Sources: apps/operator/scripts/systemd/*.service.

PROPOSED DURABLE FIXES (in value order):
1. Move Postgres data (or at least pg_wal) to nvme1n1: stop PG, rsync, then a bind mount or data_directory change, start. Needs a PG restart window, so the owner decides (it stops every agent's DB access for the copy; 136 GB at ~1-2 GB/s is a few minutes if the source is read while PG is down).
2. Move the other write-heavy trees off root the way .gitnexus was moved (D-020, fstab bind mount): .papercusp/dependency-generations, and consider the scratch/log dirs. On xfs with reflink=1, `cp --reflink` between generations on the same fs becomes near-free. [inferred: check xfs reflink=1 with xfs_info first]
3. Make IO de-prioritisation real: (a) nvme0n1 scheduler mq-deadline (it honours ioprio classes since 5.14; builtin here), persisted by a udev rule; and/or (b) delegate io to user@.service (drop-in Delegate=cpu cpuset io memory pids, then daemon-reload + user-manager re-exec) so IO*BandwidthMax works (blk-throttle works with any scheduler). Measure w_await / IO PSI before and after; revert is one write.
4. Root at 90% on a DRAM-less drive: free space helps its GC. Consider a daily fstrim (or discard) on /.

Do NOT: stop kopia or the release pipeline by hand; both are legitimate jobs. The fix is placement and priority, not killing them.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Measured 2026-09-30 08:22-08:26Z on avi-test (host-3daf37098c8096b5d9e0ac72, r61 0.0.21-p318r61) by su-be77f2f5 while preparing P-318 customer acceptance.

## Observed
- `desktop.roster` over the broker: one desktop 381b0aab-0bde-42c6-92db-4d7c3ad261b9, state=ready, display 110, lastActiveAt 06:06:45Z.
- Opening it through the local control-plane broker (probe `.papercusp/scratch/wi10004167-watch-probe.mts`) closes 4000 `desktop_dial_failed` in BOTH modes: watch at 08:22:12Z and 08:24:19Z, takeover at 08:24:23Z.
- Process table on avi-test at 08:24:46Z (customer uid, `ps -eo`): the only desktop processes are `session.cjs --stdio` (pid 7723), `flock ... display-locks/110` (7748) and `session.cjs --display 110` (7749), all started 06:07:21Z. There is NO Xkasmvnc, no xfce4-session, and nothing listens on 127.0.0.1:7010 (the KasmVNC websocket port for display 110). At ~05:55Z the previous desktop had Xkasmvnc pid 6352 `-websocketPort 7010` plus xfce4-session/panel (transcript 69f38223).

## Why it stays broken (code)
- `serveWorkspaceDesktop` (packages/operator-core/lib/desktop/workspace-desktop-session.ts) provisions once, then loops on stdin until the host closes the socket. It never watches the X server, so a dead X server leaves the worker and its socket alive.
- The host's lease liveness is socket-only: `isAlive: () => !released && !socket.destroyed` (same file). So `leasedDesktopBySessionId` still returns the lease, `lookup` succeeds and `dial` hits a closed port.
- `ensureHiveDesktop` returns the existing lease while `isAlive` is true, so `desktop.start` hands back the same dead desktop.
- The hosted desktop backend reconciles the registry only once per process (`reconcileOnce`, hosted-desktop-backend.ts), so the roster keeps the row 'ready'.
- The hosted protocol has no desktop.stop, and the customer account has no sudo, so nothing short of a VM reboot or a host service restart recovers it.
- The X server is spawned with `stdio: 'ignore'` (desktop-provisioner-core.ts), so why it exited is not recorded anywhere.

## Cause of the X server exit
NOT established. The worker's journal is not readable from the customer account. [inferred, unconfirmed] The same state may explain Avi's first 'Opening desktop…' stall at 05:53Z (#1025/#1026).

## Fix direction
1. Provisioner: `isAlive` reflects the X server child; keep a bounded stderr tail and log the exit code/signal.
2. Worker: when the X server exits, log it and end the session (release + close the socket) so the host lease reads dead.
3. Host backend: the roster drops rows whose lease is dead, on every call, and `desktop.start` re-provisions.

Blocks P-318 customer acceptance on avi-test (Take control fails right now).

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
MEASURED 2026-09-30 on avi-test (pc-host-3daf37098c8096b5d9e0ac72-877db740-vm, r62b 0.0.21-p318r62b), serial console (.papercusp/scratch/avi-test-serial-r62b.txt), su-be77f2f5, P-318:
- 11:16:27Z GCE start. 11:18:04Z startup-script [workspace-host-bootstrap] phase:verify-release, 11:18:51Z phase:install-runtime, 11:19:21Z phase:migrate-database + phase:configure-service.
- papercusp-desktop.socket and papercusp-workspace.service were already active at 11:18:56Z, so desktop.start succeeded: papercusp-desktop@0-694-999 started 11:18:58Z (desktop 0f9dadb3, watch probe reached desktop.ready 11:19:11Z).
- 11:19:23Z the bootstrap restarted papercusp-workspace.service. papercusp-desktop@.service has BindsTo=papercusp-workspace.service, so systemd stopped the desktop first. The customer's desktop was gone 25 s after it opened. The bootstrap completed at 11:19:54Z.
- The same restart also ends any terminal or agent session the customer opened in that window [inferred from the unit stop; not separately measured].

Impact: after any reboot, whatever a customer opens in roughly the first 3 minutes is killed without explanation. 'Units active' is not a readiness signal, which also misled the P-318 r62b avi-test acceptance script.

Fix options: (a) skip the reinstall and restart on a boot where the installed release already matches the manifest (verify-release passes, same storage:current), and only restart when something actually changed; or (b) keep papercusp-workspace from accepting desktop or session starts until the bootstrap writes its completion marker. (a) also removes about 110 s of redundant work on every boot.

Not a P-318 shipment blocker [self-imposed judgement, su-be77f2f5]: the desktop works once the bootstrap completes, and the reboot plus desktop.start acceptance passes.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
[observed 2026-09-30, su-0531fc91, while re-auditing native-cutover P-002 for WI-10002212; CORRECTED 16:50Z — see comment 1151390]

⚠ CORRECTION: this was originally filed as "secret-shaped values returned UNREDACTED". That was a MISREADING. The actual output contains NONE of the fake credentials — only a PID and the literal variable names. No secret reached the output; the redactors were not exercised in the failing run. This is NOT evidence against capability:bash redaction (WI-10003538).

OBSERVATION: test `credential-SHAPE output redaction + owner-only spill (WI-10003538) > background: redacts shapes from retained output and the spill log; spill is 0600` in packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/capability/bash-jobs.test.ts FAILED once:
  command:  printf "gh=%s aws=%s ant=%s\n" "$WI3538_GH" "$WI3538_AWS" "$WI3538_ANT"   (bash-jobs.test.ts:490)
  actual:   gh=1612402WI3538_GH aws=1612402WI3538_AWS ant=1612402WI3538_ANT
  expected: gh=[redacted] aws=[redacted] ant=[redacted]
`1612402` is identical for all three = one shell's `$$` (PID) followed by the literal names: bash received `"$$WI3538_GH"`, not `"$WI3538_GH"`. The failed assertion was toContain(shapeRedacted) (:565).

- FAIL: test_runs 20272858 (finished 2026-09-30T16:31:53Z, worktreeDirty=true), HEAD 1880386d3d, testing:run detached recovery run d7e4338c-75d0-4a8e-80e1-29b43ce843bb, batch of 5 files in ONE vitest invocation: pty.test.ts, bash-jobs-service-signal.test.ts, bash-jobs.test.ts, bash-output-task-reattach.test.ts, bash-kill-task-reattach.test.ts (all five tested blobs [clean]; the other four passed).
- PASS: same file alone, test_runs 20272880 (2026-09-30T16:34:55Z), same HEAD 1880386d3d, detached run 1dc9fae4-bc05-4549-bbf3-173dec3cceea.
- PASS in CI on the deployed :3070 build 29bf735091 (test_runs 20254768, 20246288) and on 599dbeeb11 (20267464).
- bash-jobs.ts (blob ab970ba1), bash-jobs.test.ts (36c5a8a3), sensitive-text.ts (unchanged since 2026-09-27 6c15b5cbc1) and systemd-scope-env-runner.mjs (d045c7e3) are identical between the failing and passing runs.
- Host at the time: loadavg ~63-83 on 128 cores.

WHY IT MATTERS: intermittent silent COMMAND CORRUPTION — a background capability:bash command's parameter expansions can run as PID-prefixed literals instead of values. Any background script using `$VAR` would produce wrong results with no error.

[inferred, UNPROBED — do not treat as cause] The only `$`→`$$` transform on the spawn path is escapeSystemdServiceArgument (packages/operator-core/lib/systemd-scope.ts:239-244), applied in buildTaskArgv (:525) only for kind==='service'; systemd's ExecStart parser normally undoes it. Candidates: (a) a service-escaped argv executed without systemd's ExecStart unescape; (b) escaping applied twice; (c) a sibling file in the same vitest worker leaking module/env/mock state (cf. WI-972553; bash-output-task-reattach.test.ts prepends a fake-bin to process.env.PATH at :245/:323, stubbing only systemctl). No retry/re-spawn path was found in bash-jobs.ts spawnShell/startBackground, and the env runner (systemd-scope-env-runner.mjs:356-363) passes argv through unchanged.

REPRO ATTEMPT: testing:run { files: [the five above] } (it will detach past 45s; poll testing:run-status). Loop it several times; compare against the file alone. A direct probe: a background capability:bash job running `echo "[$HOME]"` should print the home dir, never `[<pid>HOME]`.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body: Observed 2026-10-01 by su-72d22e0c: a broad read-only `pgrep -af` matched peer launch commands and surfaced full kickoff text plus a possible `PAPERCUSP_KICKOFF_PROOF_TOKEN` assignment. Do not copy the observed value. Source measurement: `spawnHeadless` creates `launchEnv` containing `PAPERCUSP_KICKOFF_PROOF_PATH` and `PAPERCUSP_KICKOFF_PROOF_TOKEN`, then passes that same object to `buildConsoleOneliner`; `buildConsoleOneliner` serializes every env entry as `export KEY='value'` inside the `bash -lc` argument. The same `launchEnv` is already passed through `spawn(...,{env})`, so putting the proof material in argv is redundant. The proof is random per launch, its parent wait is capped at 30 seconds, and `cleanupKickoffProofRequest` unlinks the unique 0600 receipt path after the wait; therefore the specific observed token has no durable revocation surface and is unusable once that path is gone. The systemic defect is the argv exposure during the active launch window (and accidental ingestion into logs/LLM context), which can permit same-UID proof forgery before cleanup. Durable fix: keep the proof path/token out of the oneliner argv while preserving them in the child environment, audit the headless launch-only env boundary for any other values violating `ConsoleEnvelope.env`'s documented non-secret invariant, and add canonical `console-spawn` tests that assert proof path/token are absent from `[bin,...args]`, present only in the child env, and the native kickoff receipt still succeeds. This is the same secret-in-argv defect class previously fixed on other surfaces in WI-41140 and EI-21270327070599812, but this headless console-spawn path remains exposed.

- 110 '[spawner-socket-error] read ECONNRESET'
- 24 'RPC request timeout: spawn:cancel'
- 20 'RPC request timeout: process:exec'

Spread over all 24 hours (6-26 per hour), so this is steady state, not one incident.

(2) whether the spawn:cancel timeouts come from cancelling a spawn the sidecar is itself blocked on.

COST PER RESTART [measured from the journal]: about 18 s esbuild bundle in ExecStartPre, about 9 s spawner-sidecar warm boot, plus substrate/DBOS boot and recovery. bg-host RSS reached 11.99 GB only 569 s after start (pid 3212589, 10:43Z).

CONSEQUENCE [measured]: the hourly wedged-identity sweep (WI-10005391) runs at HH:52:35Z. Over the same 24 h, 23 ticks: 19 ran in a process younger than 1 h (cold verdict cache), 3 warm, 1 with no process. Any in-process cache with a horizon longer than about 15 min is mostly cold for the same reason.

[inferred, not measured] Most external stops are peers loading their own code changes. bg-host has no hot-reload, and every restart rebundles the whole working tree.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
[measured 2026-10-06 su-6008b, EI-25222670171204378 follow-up]
Cold-start window (llama-ornith stopped 10:01:23Z, gateway answered 10:06:36Z): 193 cache-bypassing /embed samples every 2s, median 0.053s, but 13.3s @10:01:36, 14.3s @10:04:10, 30.0s client timeout @10:04:56, 22.0s @10:07:08, 21.8s @10:08:26 (raw: docs/evidence/reboot-residue-live-probes-2026-10-06/r002-coldstart-embed-samples.tsv).
Baseline right after, ornith loaded and idle (10:11-10:15Z): 92 samples, max 1.5s, none over 5s; healthz queue never saturated.
So the stalls go with the cold start, but they begin before the GPU upload (10:01:36) and continue ~2 min after the answer, so GPU memory contention alone does not fit. Mechanism NOT established. [inferred] candidate: reading the 15.4 GB GGUF from /mnt/data evicts page cache, so the sidecar takes major faults on its model files. Distinguishing probe: sample /embed plus the sidecar's major-fault count (/proc/<pid>/stat field 12) and vmstat si/bi through a cold start; then repeat with the GGUF pre-warmed in page cache (vmtouch) — stalls that vanish point to page cache.
Impact is bounded now: the watchdog no longer restarts on a single slow probe (2-consecutive threshold, EI-25222670171204378), so a stall delays embeds but no longer takes the sidecar down.

EI-20115751074601731 durable disk-headroom probe: the filesystem containing PostgreSQL data path '/var/lib/postgresql/18/main' is 100% used (warn threshold 90%). A full shared root volume takes PostgreSQL down fleet-wide by preventing WAL, lock, and data-directory writes.

trend: losing 0.63 GiB/h over the last 1.0h — ETA TO FULL ~7h at this rate

/dev/nvme0n1p2  1966788624 1941918128   4861160     100% /

LARGEST RELATIONS RIGHT NOW (read at alert time, not written down — see below):
  39.53 GiB  harness_shared.session_archive_files
  18.21 GiB  harness_shared.session_turns

  11.84 GiB  harness_shared.session_turn_chunks
  9.89 GiB  harness_shared.coord_thread_posts
  6.95 GiB  harness_shared.session_turn_parts

A relation flagged LIKELY TOAST BLOAT is the cheapest win available and needs no owner
decision: its bytes are almost entirely dead TOAST pages that plain VACUUM can never
return to the OS. Confirm by comparing pg_total_relation_size(reltoastrelid) against the
live payload (sum a denormalized length column, or sample pg_column_size), then reclaim
with a rewrite. ALWAYS bound the lock, because a rewrite takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE and a
blocked one queues AHEAD of every later lock request on that table:
  sudo -n -u postgres env PGOPTIONS='-c lock_timeout=10000' psql -p 5432 -d papercusp \
    -c 'VACUUM (FULL, VERBOSE, ANALYZE) <schema>.<relation>'
Measured 2026-09-02 (WI-2140986): that reclaimed 60.89 GiB from gateway_payload_blobs in
55s with no contention and no data loss.

INVESTIGATION RECIPE (traps verified while working WI-38595, 2026-08-14, and WI-2141004, 2026-09-02):
1. PostgreSQL is usually NOT the consumer, despite this alarm's title — but "not PostgreSQL" is a HYPOTHESIS TO TEST, never a conclusion to inherit. The probe watches the VOLUME holding PGDATA, and that volume is shared with $HOME. Size PGDATA with 'sudo -n du -xsh /var/lib/postgresql/18/main' — an unprivileged du prints a SILENT '4.0K' (permission denied) rather than an error, which reads as 'Postgres is tiny' for the wrong reason. Start from the LARGEST RELATIONS block above and from a fresh directory scan; do not start from any remembered figure, including one quoted in an older issue. This step used to carry a measured example here, and it went stale and misdirected three work-items for three weeks.
2. CONFIRM WHICH VOLUME a directory is on before reclaiming anything: 'findmnt -T <path>' or 'stat -c %d <path>'. On this box /tmp is a BIND MOUNT from a second physical disk, so deleting 136 GiB of stale /tmp scratch frees exactly nothing on the volume this alarm is about.
3. Enumerate consumers in ONE bounded backgrounded pass: 'nice -n 19 ionice -c3 du -x -d3 / | sort -hr > /tmp/scan-1.txt' (~7 min here). Re-run it later into scan-2.txt and DIFF the two — a diff of two snapshots is the only reliable attribution of NET growth per directory.
4. Do NOT attribute growth by mtime ('find -newermt'). It counts a file's WHOLE size when the file is merely touched, so a single live VM image reads as hundreds of GiB 'written' in 26h. Note also that qcow2 images grow monotonically and never return space the guest frees — and the .img suffix lies, so check the magic ('QFI\373' = qcow2).

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
EI-10733 durable backup-health probe: '/mnt/backup/db-dumps/pg/papercusp-transcript' has not advanced in 18 hours (size 4096B). The DB dump is supposed to run ~hourly.

THIS IS THE SIGNAL THAT WAS MISSING. On 2026-07-12 the backup had been failing 100% for ~30 DAYS (newest good dump 2026-06-12) and nothing detected it, because a plausible-looking 1.4GB .gz sat on disk the whole time. 'The backup file exists' is not 'the backup works' — only its FRESHNESS discriminates.

LIKELY CAUSES (check in this order):
 1. db-backup.sh's timer stopped firing: systemctl --user status papercusp-db-backup.timer papercusp-db-backup.service ; journalctl --user -u papercusp-db-backup.service -n 50. Read /mnt/backup/db-dumps/STATUS.json (ok / failed[] / lastSuccessEpoch) and /mnt/backup/db-dumps/db-backup.log.
 2. A specific DB's dump is failing validation: db-backup.sh only renames a dump into place after pg_restore -l passes, so a per-DB 'FAIL' in db-backup.log means the archive was unreadable or the dump errored — read the actual pg_dump error there. DO NOT blindly raise PC_BACKUP_TIMEOUT_SEC without reading it.
 3. An orphaned pg_dump is holding locks (the EI-10730 knock-on): check for a pg_dump backend older than its timeout (SELECT pid, application_name, backend_start FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE application_name LIKE 'pg_dump%'). db-backup.sh tags its own dumps PGAPPNAME=pcbackup and reaps foreign ones; a lingering 'pg_dump%' backend is a legacy/manual dump.
 4. Disk full on the backup volume: df -h /mnt/backup/db-dumps

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Discovered while investigating WI-5978. Historical host-side records reported qemu-system-x86_64 consuming 46.4 CPU-days over 9.3 days (~5 cores). Short identity-matched host samples measured 480.9%, 602.8%, and 593.9% CPU, with QEMU task guest_time confirming vCPU execution.

The reported guest process-level 0.0% readings came from a measurement error: this macOS VM's `man top` states that the first sample's process `%CPU` is invalid because it needs a prior-sample delta. A same-session comparison confirmed it: `top -l 1` produced no process rows at or above 0.1%, while `top -l 3 -s 1` reported active processes. Use at least two samples and disregard the first per-process sample.

A paired read-only sample over 6.038s measured QEMU guest_time at 727.5% of one core. The guest is macOS with 8 logical CPUs; three `top` intervals reported 67.18/30.84/1.96, 52.40/32.78/14.81, and 64.81/29.25/5.92 percent user/system/idle. The high processes included WindowServer (205.4%), a Papercusp Node sidecar (117.5%), Papercusp harness Postgres backends (59.1%, 33.1%, 32.4%), diagnosticd (40.3%), and the diagnostic top process (21.6%). The Node process parent was Papercusp; it listened on local ports 3068, 3070, and 3076.

This confirms real guest workload in the sampled interval and explains the zero process readout. It does not establish whether this activity was expected or explain the historical multi-day host average; high CPU during genuine guest idle remains unresolved.

QMP's relative `unix:./qmp.sock` path resolves against the VM process cwd and is reachable. `query-status` reports running, `query-cpus-fast` maps 8 vCPU threads, and HMP `info cpus` lists thread IDs without a halted-state indicator; `query-cpus` is unsupported.

Operational constraint: keep the VM running; do not restart or change launch flags without an explicit coordinated window. Continue read-only investigation of the active Papercusp workload and seek an idle baseline when one occurs naturally.

admissionIdentity.titleKey: title:and are codex ends enrolment homes hook hooks journal json live never predates repaired sessions stale stop turn

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Measured 2026-10-11 ~03:50Z (for WI-6554700010008397 / plan git-sync-turn-scoped-commit-hold-2026-10-11 P-001).

Symptom: 23 coord owners made 1,000+ file edits in 24h (edit_attribution_ledger) yet have ZERO harness_shared.session_turn_journal rows in 7d under any owner id (checked by session_id via session_turn_parts, so not an id mismatch). All 23 are INTERACTIVE codex sessions (adv_sessions.launch_spec headless:false, principalId system:superuser); every journaling codex owner sampled is a headless fleet member.

Root cause (observed): their per-session CODEX_HOME hooks.json (~/.papercusp/su-codex-homes/session-38919, -38890; written 2026-10-09) has Stop = [inject dispatcher only] — no stop-turn-journal.sh, and also no userpromptsubmit-provenance.sh and no pretooluse-unreserved-migration-guard.mjs. A headless member home written 2026-10-10 22:48 (session-39023) has all three. Census: 141 of 279 su-codex-homes lack stop-turn-journal.sh.

Why no self-heal: repairSuCodexHomeIdentity (packages/operator-core/lib/role-codex-home.ts ~L1087) rewrites the canonical hooks (incl. ['Stop', CODEX_TURN_JOURNAL_HOOK]) but only runs on RESUME; a long-lived interactive codex session never resumes, so its home keeps the hook set from launch time. Why the 10-09 homes lacked the hook although the writer code landed on staging 10-06/10-08 is [inferred] launch from an older :3070 release build or the installed ~/.papercusp/hooks/cc copy being absent — unverified.

Durable fix to design: (1) establish whether codex re-reads $CODEX_HOME/hooks.json per event (if yes, a sweep that repairs every LIVE su-codex home whenever the managed hook set changes fixes the class; if no, surface 'hooks stale since launch' on presence so the owner can restart); (2) a recurrence guard: a census check that flags live codex homes whose hooks.json differs from the canonical writer output.

Impact on the turn-scoped hold: those sessions get no turn-end signal, so their edits are held up to the 60-min D-001 cap instead of releasing at turn end.

Related observation (not filed separately): OMP wrote zero session_turn_journal rows in 7d, but no OMP session made edits in the 24h window, so it does not affect the hold today.

admissionIdentity.titleKey: title:51g and dev docker ext4 filesystem free full holds host lib nvme0n1p2 root var

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Measured 2026-10-11 ~06:00Z by su-6baa8 (df -h /var/lib/docker): /dev/nvme0n1p2 1.9T size, 1.8T used, 51G avail, 98%. The same ext4 filesystem holds the shared repo tree, every agent's scratch, and docker's data root (overlay2, 95 running / 109 total containers, 78 volumes).
Why it matters: (1) the fleet fills this disk; at 98% a few large writes can exhaust it. (2) EI-25660493481108673: every docker create waits for a full syncfs of this same filesystem (kernel stack ovl_sync_fs -> sync_inodes_sb -> wb_wait_for_completion), so create latency reached 120-180s+.
Hypothesis, NOT tested: the open spill-write-failed / spill timeout bugs (EI-25390414387699833, EI-25327232452706390, EI-25396682599838692) may share this disk pressure. Needs a measurement before anyone acts on it.
Next: measure the largest consumers (docker images/volumes/build cache, scratch dirs, test containers' upper dirs, logs) without unbounded find -L; propose a reclaim plan. Deleting other agents' data needs the owner's sign-off.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Split from WI-6554700010008868 (su-8cec8a78, 2026-10-12).

Measured: with the committed-source loader in NODE_OPTIONS (which `npm run test:file` sets), `npx tsx scripts/measure-startup-cache.ts --input <file> --json` exits 1 in a clean as-committed root (afc18a086c) with `COMMITTED_SOURCE refused scripts/measure-startup-cache.ts: a checkout module was loaded through CommonJS, which bypasses the committed-source check` (scripts/lib/committed-source-loader.mjs:250). Without the loader it exits 0. The root has no package type, so tsx compiles a root `scripts/*.ts` as CJS. The repo convention for scripts that tests spawn is `.mts` (scripts/state-census-roots.mts, state-census-units.mts), which load through ESM and pass the check.

Effect: packages/operator-core/lib/launch-cost/startup-cache-real-journal.test.ts fails under `npm run test:file` (testing:run and the gate's test:affected do not put the loader in NODE_OPTIONS, so they pass).

Fix: rename to scripts/measure-startup-cache.mts and update package.json `measure:startup-cache`, the test's spawn args, and the reviewed bypass entry in scripts/check-resource-governor-enforcement.mjs (~line 1872). Recurrence guard: a test that fails when any *.test.ts spawns tsx on a root `scripts/<name>.ts` (CJS) path.

DEFERRED until plan token-efficiency-prompts-cache-and-behavior-2026-10-11 ships [self-imposed]: the rename changes the blobs of P-001's audited evidence files (test + script cited in code-truth audit #4 and bound to SPEC-P-001 / AUTO-BAR-R-1-P-001), which would force re-binding and re-audit right before acceptance grading.
_claimSubjectBaseline.title: Rename scripts/measure-startup-cache.ts to .mts: under npm run test:file the committed-source loader refuses tsx's CommonJS load of it
_claimSubjectBaseline.summary:
Split from WI-6554700010008868 (su-8cec8a78, 2026-10-12).

Measured: with the committed-source loader in NODE_OPTIONS (which `npm run test:file` sets), `npx tsx scripts/measure-startup-cache.ts --input <file> --json` exits 1 in a clean as-committed root (afc18a086c) with `COMMITTED_SOURCE refused scripts/measure-startup-cache.ts: a checkout module was loaded through CommonJS, which bypasses the committed-source check` (scripts/lib/committed-source-loader.mjs:250). Without the loader it exits 0. The root has no package type, so tsx compiles a root `scripts/*.ts` as CJS. The repo convention for scripts that tests spawn is `.mts` (scripts/state-census-roots.mts, state-census-units.mts), which load through ESM and pass the check.

Effect: packages/operator-core/lib/launch-cost/startup-cache-real-journal.test.ts fails under `npm run test:file` (testing:run and the gate's test:affected do not put the loader in NODE_OPTIONS, so they pass).

Fix: rename to scripts/measure-startup-cache.mts and update package.json `measure:startup-cache`, the test's spawn args, and the reviewed bypass entry in scripts/check-resource-governor-enforcement.mjs (~line 1872). Recurrence guard: a test that fails when any *.test.ts spawns tsx on a root `scripts/<name>.ts` (CJS) path.

DEFERRED until plan token-efficiency-prompts-cache-and-behavior-2026-10-11 ships [self-imposed]: the rename changes the blobs of P-001's audited evidence files (test + script cited in code-truth audit #4 and bound to SPEC-P-001 / AUTO-BAR-R-1-P-001), which would force re-binding and re-audit right before acceptance grading.

admissionIdentity.titleKey: title:cadence cannot census cgroup dbos device disk every finish host inside one restart step the under walks

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-13 (su-fe8c2627, from WI-6554700010009429, plan disk-headroom-standing-reclaim-2026-10-12 P-001 / R-1).

The 04:35Z diskConsumerCensus run had written no rows by 05:45Z. bg-host was SIGTERMed externally at 05:29:41Z (journal: 'deploy, systemctl, or a sync timer'), and du (in papercusp-bg-host.service's cgroup) died ~44 min into the `/` walk. DBOS recovery restarted the walk from zero (new du pid 605958 at ~05:30:43Z). bg-host restarts observed today: 00:15Z, 02:14Z, 04:45Z, 05:29Z. A 2026-10-02 measurement found a mean bg-host uptime of ~33 min, mostly peer dev:restarts. One census needs ~45-50 min for `/` plus ~25 min for /mnt/data.

Structural cause (read, packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/periodic-workflows.ts diskConsumerCensusTick): ONE DBOS.runStep wraps runDiskConsumerCensusOnce for all devices, so any restart re-walks every device, including ones whose row is already written.

Fix options:
(a) one DBOS step per device: a recovered run skips measured devices. Necessary, but not sufficient when the restart lands inside one 45-min walk.
(b) run the walk in its own transient systemd unit that outlives bg-host, with the step polling for its result file/row.
(c) persist per-subtree partial progress so a resumed walk continues.

Acceptance: across a bg-host restart mid-walk, the run still writes a complete row for every device, proven by an integration test that kills the walk mid-step and by one live run that spans a real bg-host restart.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Ship blocker for plan papercusp-performance-audit-2026-10-12 R-6 (rubric acceptance-papercusp-performance-audit-2026-10-12; amendment B, under review as of 16:05Z, requires every metric strictly better than its 2026-10-12 baseline). Measured by su-98253 on 2026-10-13.

Measurements (method: papercusp-app-performance pg-statement-load, sum(total_exec_time) delta of pg_stat_statements toplevel rows / window ms):
- 15:49-15:54Z, three ~90 s samples: 10.51, 11.77, 8.50; median 10.51 vs baseline 9.49 (original target 5). dealloc stayed 8, so no eviction skew. Raw: papercusp/.papercusp/scratch/r6-pg-cores-2026-10-13T1550Z.txt; also thread-post:1179075 on WI-6554700010009999.
- 15:58Z 90 s per-statement window: ~14.0 cores of real traffic (15.03 total minus 1.00 from the probe's own pg_sleep). The load is diffuse: the top 25 statements sum to ~9 cores. Leaders: pg_advisory_xact_lock(int, hashtext) 0.86 cores, 1067 calls, 72 ms/call (lock wait); coord_event_log lookup by (workspace_id, surface, writer_key, body->>key) 0.86 cores, 312 calls, 247 ms/call; two work_items issue selects at 741-1047 ms/call; coord_links tagged CTE 1252 ms/call; event_wake_deliveries / event_awaits lookups by event_key at 82-140 ms/call; tool_invocations max(invoked_at) per owner 212 ms/call. Raw: papercusp/.papercusp/scratch/r6-pg-top-statements-2026-10-13T1557Z.txt.
- 16:07Z 26 s window: exec 8.37 cores, of which block-read time 0.43 cores (5.1%), shared hit ratio 99.96%, track_io_timing on.

Ruled out (measured): IO contention as the main driver. Root disk nvme0n1 was reading ~612-733 MB/s at 72% util (Postgres 144 MB/s; papercup-oddsmith-sidecar 128 MB/s; GNOME Terminal scopes 93 MB/s; papercusp.slice 84 MB/s), but only 5.1% of Postgres execution time was block reads. CPU PSI 3-6%, so not CPU-starved either.

Working hypothesis [inferred, unprobed]: per-call cost of a handful of hot statements (likely missing/unused indexes or JSON-predicate scans on coord_event_log / event_awaits / event_wake_deliveries, plus advisory-lock contention), multiplied by fleet call volume. The metric also moves with fleet activity (8.37 to 11.77 within 20 min), so before/after comparisons must control for headcount and call volume.

Next: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) the top 6 statements on representative parameters; check index use; fix the worst offenders in their owning code/migrations; re-measure with >= 3 samples. Do not change the bar.

admissionIdentity.titleKey: title:before cause command current host its itself journald logs memory pressure stalls sudo unconfirmed under

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Residue of WI-6554700010011924 (su-98253, measured 2026-10-14 from the system journal, SYSLOG_IDENTIFIER=sudo, 04:00-06:05Z, 5,937 entries / 859 pids; script and data in .papercusp/scratch/su-98253-sudo-lag/).

OBSERVED: sudo pid 473367 was alive at 04:53:55Z (systemd: 'Unit process 473367 (sudo) remains running after unit stopped') but its COMMAND line has _SOURCE_REALTIME 04:54:32.875Z and journald receive 04:54:32.878Z. So journald was current, and the sudo spent >=37 s inside itself BEFORE logging. Separately, in-sudo COMMAND->'session opened' gaps of 10.95 s (05:48:15Z) and 10.86 s (05:54:39Z) occurred, and journald ingest lag reached 20.2 s (05:44Z; p99 3.8 s). Host load ~220-280, memory PSI full avg10 up to ~73 in the window.

IMPACT: every privileged step on this host (pg_dump via sudo -u postgres, Kopia via sudo, backup cleanups) inherits this latency. WI-6554700010011924 made the Kopia cleanup tolerant of it (bounded 45 s calls, fewer sudo forks, TimeoutStopSec=180s); it did not remove the stall.

HYPOTHESES [inferred, none tested]: (1) exec + shared-library page faults after page-cache eviction under memory pressure; (2) NSS/PAM lookups (passwd/group, hostname) blocked on IO; (3) sudo's timestamp/IO-log file writes under IO pressure.

DISTINGUISHING TEST: during the next pressure episode run `perf trace`/`strace -f -tt -e trace=%file,%process,%network sudo -n true` (root) and compare the time spent before the first syslog sendto against major-fault counts (`/proc/<pid>/stat` field 12) for the sudo process.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Host-side residue split out of WI-6554700010012153 (follow-up of EI-25930229050142968, owner #1845). That item shipped the LOOP-side alarm: reconcile-loop-routines now opens an advisory `loop-no-turn-wedge:<install>:<routine>` escalation once a 'delivered-wake-no-loop-turn' streak reaches 3 (PAPERCUSP_LOOP_NO_TURN_ESCALATE_AFTER), well below the 8-error circuit, and auto-resolves it on the next ok fire. Still open, both on the host in `apps/operator/scripts/psu-pty-host.mjs` (`retryPendingSubmissions`), and both [inferred, not yet observed live]:

1. **Wedge diagnosis + recovery on the host.** When the host sees >=2 consecutive `pending-submit-recovery-exhausted` events with no native turn between them, request a child recycle through the existing hard-recycle path, and capture a screen snapshot (the TUI buffer) at exhaustion so the cause of a composer that never accepts Enter can be diagnosed. The loop-side escalation only makes this visible; it does not recover the session or capture why.
2. **Composer residue after retirement.** Retirement does not clear the staged text. The next wake's paste is appended to it, and `findNativeTranscriptMarker` matches by PREFIX, so the next delivery's proof fails even when the combined row submits. Options: clear a machine-owned composer at retirement (TUI-specific; never when owner ownership is lost), or let the proof match a marker anywhere in the row.

Evidence: the 72h host-log census on EI-25930229050142968 (393/381/377/199/64 recovery Enters).

Source apps/operator/scripts/ptool.mjs dynamically imports @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js, client/streamableHttp.js and types.js (lines ~2505, 3427-3428), so the sidecar staging/pruning step ships ptool.mjs without its runtime dependency.

[inferred, unverified] the sidecar node_modules pruning keeps only the operator's static import graph; a dynamic import() is not traced.

Impact: the documented admin CLI (and the product backup verb path through it) is unavailable on packaged installs; the 120s connect-retry loop also masks a module-resolution error as a connection failure (83x other).

Acceptance: the packaged sidecar includes @modelcontextprotocol/sdk (or ptool is bundled); a packaged-install check runs `ptool --help` / one read verb and fails the package build when it errors; ptool reports a module-resolution failure immediately instead of retrying it as a connect failure.

admissionIdentity.titleKey: title:60h backup database have may old papercusp recoverable stale threshold transcript

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
EI-10733 durable backup-health probe: '/mnt/backup/db-dumps/pg/papercusp-transcript' has not advanced in 60 hours (size 4096B). The DB dump is supposed to run ~hourly.

THIS IS THE SIGNAL THAT WAS MISSING. On 2026-07-12 the backup had been failing 100% for ~30 DAYS (newest good dump 2026-06-12) and nothing detected it, because a plausible-looking 1.4GB .gz sat on disk the whole time. 'The backup file exists' is not 'the backup works' — only its FRESHNESS discriminates.

LIKELY CAUSES (check in this order):
 1. db-backup.sh's timer stopped firing: systemctl --user status papercusp-db-backup.timer papercusp-db-backup.service ; journalctl --user -u papercusp-db-backup.service -n 50. Read /mnt/backup/db-dumps/STATUS.json (ok / failed[] / lastSuccessEpoch) and /mnt/backup/db-dumps/db-backup.log.
 2. A specific DB's dump is failing validation: db-backup.sh only renames a dump into place after pg_restore -l passes, so a per-DB 'FAIL' in db-backup.log means the archive was unreadable or the dump errored — read the actual pg_dump error there. DO NOT blindly raise PC_BACKUP_TIMEOUT_SEC without reading it.
 3. An orphaned pg_dump is holding locks (the EI-10730 knock-on): check for a pg_dump backend older than its timeout (SELECT pid, application_name, backend_start FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE application_name LIKE 'pg_dump%'). db-backup.sh tags its own dumps PGAPPNAME=pcbackup and reaps foreign ones; a lingering 'pg_dump%' backend is a legacy/manual dump.
 4. Disk full on the backup volume: df -h /mnt/backup/db-dumps

An orphaned/stuck dump is not just a dead backup — it holds AccessShareLock on ~593 tables, which starves every migration's ACCESS EXCLUSIVE and can wedge the whole release pipeline (EI-10730).

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Owner directive #1899 (2026-10-15, Avi): 'we are low on disk space. no matter what we do we keep running out ... fix it durably ... what is the best target we can expect to achieve'.

Measured 2026-10-15 ~12:40-13:00Z (su-271cfdc6):
- / (1.9T NVMe): 10G free; census growth ~2 GB/h avg over 66h, ~6 GB/h in the last 6h. Root drivers 10-12→10-15: ~/.papercusp/scratch +71G, ~/.papercusp/evidence +44G (one 38G cargo-target), Postgres +30G (216G db), in-tree .papercusp +29G, su-codex-homes +9G, embedded-pg +9G.
- /mnt/data (8T NVMe): 43G free. 1.1T swapfile (308G in use), 2.7T kopia repo, 2.8T offload (root-disk 808G, VM images ~1T, private-release-evidence 247G +213G in 3 days), back+Debug 364G, tmp 256G.
- Hourly disk-retention reclaim (disk-reclaim.ts) never completes, removes ~100 small entries/run, and protects every large growing tree (foreign-owner / symlink / protected-root / not-a-deletable-class).
- sda: GPT partition 2 (5.8 TB) exists but kernel never loaded it (no /dev/sda2), never formatted. sdb: 5.8 TB unallocated + sdb1 1.4 TB with no filesystem signature. ≈13 TB HDD idle.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Gate signature entry `@papercusp/operator-core :: test:coverage-attribution-venue` (repair queue 4224bf7c, repairHead 8705c635). Fails identically at repairHead (ci test_runs 10:08Z and 07:16Z, clean worktree), at the PR-drill checkpoint bfada1aa (ci, 12:10Z), and in the shared tree (local, 12:03Z).

Observed: all 3 cases fail. (1) and (2) `capability_denied: Session confinement policy is unavailable` from session-confinement-port.ts checkSessionConfinement. The installed store resolver (capability-envelope/session-confinement-store.ts:307) reads through the org-admin pool, and libs/test-config/src/setup-no-live-pg.ts (WI-10006585, integration layer, PAPERCUSP_FORBID_LIVE_PG=1) refuses that pool because it resolves to live localhost:5432/papercusp. (3) The learning.observations REST case sees an extra console.warn (`[adv-sessions] … failed`), which comes from the same refused pool.

Root cause [inferred from source; not yet probed by a mutation]: a design conflict between two rails. persistence-venue.integration.test.ts (P-027, unchanged since 2026-09-14) persists coverage_evidence to the CANONICAL admin PG on purpose. Its header says "canonical admin PG -> createPgEvidenceStore -> coverage_evidence", and its final assertion reads testing_surface_depth. The integration live-PG rail (landed by 2026-10-07) refuses exactly that target, and setup-no-live-pg.ts offers no scoped opt-out.

Options: (A) a named, script-scoped opt-out. The test:coverage-attribution-venue package script sets e.g. PAPERCUSP_LIVE_PG_VENUE=coverage-attribution, and setup-no-live-pg.ts then skips arming the forbid only for that value; pin the opt-out with a guard test so it cannot spread. This keeps the venue's purpose (real persistent evidence), but the test also dispatches improvements:capture against live state. (B) Route the venue to createOrgTestDb (env-route HARNESS_ADMIN_DATABASE_URL/HARNESS_DATABASE_URL to adminDsn/appDsn before any pool opens). Safe, but the evidence no longer reaches the canonical census, so the venue stops moving the ladder.
Next: decide A vs B. A preserves P-027's intent and needs a review of the improvements:capture write; B is the safe default.

terminalCompletionEvidence.summary:
Removed the two stale ElevenLabs-CDN scratch pages from the committed sidecar staging SPA artifact, AND corrected this item's central claim: they were never shipped. The filed title said the SPA 'still ships' them; verification of the actual ship path shows no packaged artifact ever carried them. Corrected in full in the thread comment (post 79055).

Ship-path finding: the pages sat at the TOP-LEVEL papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/env-sidecars/staging/spa/. No `resources` glob in any of the six tauri config variants covers that path — every glob is rooted at src-tauri/SIDECAR/, a different directory. What ships is generated: bin/stage-env-sidecars.sh does `rm -rf $SIDECAR/env-sidecars` then `cp -al $SIDECAR/spa $ENV_SC/spa`, hardlink-copying the PRIMARY sidecar SPA, which does not contain these pages. bin/build-windows-cross.sh independently rm -rf's and re-stages the top-level dir before building.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
## The defect

`plans:set-plan-status shipped` / `plans:get { shipReadiness }` executed against the DEPLOYED build report `acceptance_rubric_missing` for plan `tool-contract-repair-2026-09-05`, whose acceptance rubric is present, active, and correctly pinned. Because agent MCP calls are proxied to :3070 (the release checkout), the ship write itself would refuse on this false verdict — so the plan is unshippable through the ordinary surface until the deploy catches up.

## Decisive evidence (A/B; only variable is the build)

Same database, same plan, same rubric row, same request, 2026-09-06T06:47Z:

| port | build sha | shipReadiness.code |
|---|---|---|
| :3170 (working tree) | bf6f5851df | `acceptance_bar_contract_not_ready` |
| :3070 (deployed release) | 6e898b6cf8 | `acceptance_rubric_missing` |

:9071 (the MCP proxy every agent calls) reports sha 6e898b6cf8 — i.e. it forwards to :3070, so agents get the WRONG verdict by default.

## The rubric genuinely satisfies every predicate of the gate's own lookup

`getAcceptanceRubricsForPlan` (packages/operator-core/lib/rubrics.ts) selects on seven conditions. Checked individually against `harness_shared.harness_plans` row `acceptance-tool-contract-repair-2026-09-05`, ALL are true: template='rubric', template_slug IS NULL, archived=false, status='active', template_data->>'kind'='acceptance', template_data->>'subjectPlan'='tool-contract-repair-2026-09-05', workspace_id='papercusp-workspace'.

## Where it diverges

The SQL predicates are byte-identical between deployed and staging (`git show 6e898b6cf8:packages/operator-core/lib/rubrics.ts`), so the row IS selected in both builds. The divergence is in the post-mapping:

- deployed: `rows.map(planRowToRubric).filter(r => r !== null && r.kind === 'acceptance' && r.subjectPlan === planSlug)`
- staging:  `(await mapRubricPlanRows(rows)).filter(...)`

`git diff 6e898b6cf8 staging -- packages/operator-core/lib/rubrics.ts` shows staging added a large acceptance-BAR schema surface to the criterion type (`barContract`, `bar`, `barKey`, `barHash`, `role`, `mandatory`, `requiredScope`, `evidencePlane`, `requiredTestLayers`, `passRatings`, plus `AcceptanceBarProvenance`). The rubric was amended to revision 5 by the NEWER build, so its persisted `template_data` carries that newer shape; the older deployed `rubricTemplateDataSchema` appears to reject it, `planRowToRubric` returns null, and the row is filtered away — surfacing as "no rubric exists".

NOTE: the null-mapping step is the INFERRED mechanism (the observed facts are the A/B split, the seven satisfied predicates, and the identical SQL). It is consistent with all of them but was not isolated further; confirm by running `planRowToRubric` from the deployed sha against this row before fixing.

## Why this matters beyond one plan

`getAcceptanceRubricsForPlan` swallows failures (`catch { return [] }`), so a rubric the deployed build cannot parse is indistinguishable from one that was never authored. The gate's remediation text then instructs the agent to `rubrics:propose` a NEW rubric — which would author a DUPLICATE over a live, correctly-pinned one. Any plan whose rubric was written or amended by a build newer than the deployed one is exposed to this, and the failure actively coaches the wrong repair.

## Suggested direction

Run the same A/B before acting. Then either (a) make the rubric template schema forward-tolerant on read so an older build ignores unknown newer fields rather than nulling the whole rubric, and/or (b) stop `getAcceptanceRubricsForPlan` swallowing a parse failure into `[]` — distinguish 'no rubric' from 'rubric unreadable', so the gate can say `acceptance_rubric_unreadable` and never coach a duplicate propose.

Found while clearing the ship gate for tool-contract-repair-2026-09-05 under WI-2146290.
